1.79.s:
sumanturuvāca
etacchrutvā tu kārtsnyena hṛṣṭo jāmbavatīsutaḥ .
jātakautūhalo bhūyaḥ paripapraccha nāradam1 . . 1
1.79.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु कार्त्स्न्येन हृष्टो जाम्बवतीसुतः ।
जातकौतूहलो भूयः परिपप्रच्छ नारदम्1 ॥ 1
1.79.m: Sumantu said: / Having heard this completely, the son of Jāmbavatī, delighted / and filled with curiosity, questioned Nārada further.

1.79.s:
sāmba uvāca
aho sūryasya māhātmyaṃ varṇitaṃ harṣavardhanam .
yena me bhaktirutpannā parā hyasminvibhāvasau . . 2
1.79.d:
साम्ब उवाच
अहो सूर्यस्य माहात्म्यं वर्णितं हर्षवर्धनम् ।
येन मे भक्तिरुत्पन्ना परा ह्यस्मिन्विभावसौ ॥ 2
1.79.m: Sāmba said: / Ah, the greatness of the sun, which increases joy, has been described, / by which supreme devotion in this Fire-god has arisen in me.

1.79.s:
tato rājñīṃ mahābhāgāṃ nikṣubhāṃ ca mahāmune .
diṇḍinaṃ piṅgalādīṃśca sarvānkathaya me mune . . 3
1.79.d:
ततो राज्ञीं महाभागां निक्षुभां च महामुने ।
दिण्डिनं पिङ्गलादींश्च सर्वान्कथय मे मुने ॥ 3
1.79.m: Now, O great sage, tell me about the fortunate Rājñī and Nikṣubhā, / Diṇḍin, Piṅgala, and all the rest, O sage.

1.79.s:
nārada uvāca
prāgukte'rkasya dve bhārye rājñī nikṣubhasaṃjñite .
tayorhi rājñī dyaurjñeyā nikṣubhā pṛthivī smṛtā . .4
1.79.d:
नारद उवाच
प्रागुक्तेऽर्कस्य द्वे भार्ये राज्ञी निक्षुभसंज्ञिते ।
तयोर्हि राज्ञी द्यौर्ज्ञेया निक्षुभा पृथिवी स्मृता ॥4
1.79.m: Nārada said: / The two wives of the sun previously mentioned are named Rājñī and Nikṣubhā; / of the two, Rājñī is to be known as the sky, and Nikṣubhā is recorded as the earth.

1.79.s:
saumyamāsasya2 saptamyāṃ dyāvārkaḥ saha yujyate .
māghakṛṣṇasya saptamyāṃ mahyā saha bhavedraviḥ . .
bhūrādityaśca bhagavāngacchataḥ saṅgamaṃ tathā . . 5
1.79.d:
सौम्यमासस्य2 सप्तम्यां द्यावार्कः सह युज्यते ।
माघकृष्णस्य सप्तम्यां मह्या सह भवेद्रविः ॥
भूरादित्यश्च भगवान्गच्छतः सङ्गमं तथा ॥ 5
1.79.m: On the seventh day of the Saumya month, the sun is joined with the sky; / on the seventh day of the dark fortnight of Māgha, the sun is joined with the earth; / thus the lord, the sun, and the earth enter into union.

1.79.s:
ṛtusnātā mahī tatra garbhaṃ gṛhṇāti bhāskarāt .
dyaurjalaṃ sūyate garbhaṃ varṣāsviha ca bhūtale . . 6
1.79.d:
ऋतुस्नाता मही तत्र गर्भं गृह्णाति भास्करात् ।
द्यौर्जलं सूयते गर्भं वर्षास्विह च भूतले ॥ 6
1.79.m: The earth, having bathed after her season, then receives the seed from the sun; / the sky brings forth water as its embryo here on the surface of the earth during the rains.

1.79.s:
tatastrailokyabhūtyarthaṃ3 mahī sasyāni sūyate .
sasyopayogasaṃhṛṣṭā juhvatyāhutayo dvijāḥ . . 7
1.79.d:
ततस्त्रैलोक्यभूत्यर्थं3 मही सस्यानि सूयते ।
सस्योपयोगसंहृष्टा जुह्वत्याहुतयो द्विजाः ॥ 7
1.79.m: Then, for the prosperity of the three worlds, the earth brings forth the crops; / delighted by the use of the crops, the twice-born offer oblations,

1.79.s: svāhākārasvadhākārairyajanti pitṛdevatāḥ . . 8
1.79.d: स्वाहाकारस्वधाकारैर्यजन्ति पितृदेवताः ॥ 8
1.79.m: and worship the ancestors and the deities with the utterances of svāhā and svadhā.

1.79.s:
nikṣubhā sūyate yasmādannauṣadhisudhāmṛtaiḥ .
martyānpitṝṃśca devāṃśca tena bhūrnikṣubhā smṛtā . . 9
1.79.d:
निक्षुभा सूयते यस्मादन्नौषधिसुधामृतैः ।
मर्त्यान्पितॄंश्च देवांश्च तेन भूर्निक्षुभा स्मृता ॥ 9
1.79.m: Because Nikṣubhā produces [sustenance] through food, herbs, nectar, and ambrosia / for mortals, ancestors, and gods, therefore the earth is known as Nikṣubhā.

1.79.s:
yathā rājñī dvidhā bhūtā yasya ceyaṃ sutā matā .
apatyāni ca yānyasyāstāni vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ . . 1.79.10
1.79.d:
यथा राज्ञी द्विधा भूता यस्य चेयं सुता मता ।
अपत्यानि च यान्यस्यास्तानि वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः ॥ 1.79.10
1.79.m: How Rājñī became twofold, whose daughter she is considered to be, / and what offspring she bore—these I shall describe in full.

1.79.s:
marīcirbrahmaṇaḥ putro marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ sutaḥ .
tasmāddhiraṇyakaśiṣuḥ prahlādastasya cātmajaḥ . . 11
1.79.d:
मरीचिर्ब्रह्मणः पुत्रो मरीचेः कश्यपः सुतः ।
तस्माद्धिरण्यकशिषुः प्रह्लादस्तस्य चात्मजः ॥ 11
1.79.m: Marīci was the son of Brahmā; Kaśyapa was the son of Marīci; / from him [was born] Hiraṇyakaśipu, and Prahlāda was his son.

1.79.s:
prahlādasya suto nāmnā virocana iti śrutaḥ .
virocanasya bhaginī saṃjñāyā jananī śubhā . . 12
1.79.d:
प्रह्लादस्य सुतो नाम्ना विरोचन इति श्रुतः ।
विरोचनस्य भगिनी संज्ञाया जननी शुभा ॥ 12
1.79.m: Prahlāda had a son named Virocana, famous [in tradition]; / the auspicious sister of Virocana was the mother of Saṃjñā.

1.79.s:
hiraṇyakaśipoḥ pautrī diteḥ putrasya sā smṛtā .
sā viśvakarmaṇaḥ putrī prāhlādī procyate budhaiḥ . . 13
1.79.d:
हिरण्यकशिपोः पौत्री दितेः पुत्रस्य सा स्मृता ।
सा विश्वकर्मणः पुत्री प्राह्लादी प्रोच्यते बुधैः ॥ 13
1.79.m: She is remembered as the granddaughter of Hiraṇyakaśipu, the son of Diti; / as the daughter of Viśvakarman, she is called Prāhlādī by the wise.

1.79.s:
atha nāmnā surūpeti marīcerduhitā śubhā .
putrī hyaṅgirasaḥ sā tu jananī tu bṛhaspateḥ . . 14
1.79.d:
अथ नाम्ना सुरूपेति मरीचेर्दुहिता शुभा ।
पुत्री ह्यङ्गिरसः सा तु जननी तु बृहस्पतेः ॥ 14
1.79.m: Now, the auspicious daughter of Marīci, named Surūpā, / was indeed the daughter of Aṅgiras, and she was the mother of Bṛhaspati.

1.79.s:
bṛhaspatestu bhaginī viśrutā brahmavādinī .
prabhāsasya tu sā patnī vasūnāmaṣṭamasya tu . . 15
1.79.d:
बृहस्पतेस्तु भगिनी विश्रुता ब्रह्मवादिनी ।
प्रभासस्य तु सा पत्नी वसूनामष्टमस्य तु ॥ 15
1.79.m: The sister of Bṛhaspati was a renowned expounder of the Veda; / she was the wife of Prabhāsa, the eighth of the Vasus.

1.79.s:
prasūtā viśvakarmāṇaṃ sarvaśilpakaraṃ varam .
sa vai nāmrā punastvaṣṭā tridaśānāṃ ca vārdhakiḥ . . 16
1.79.d:
प्रसूता विश्वकर्माणं सर्वशिल्पकरं वरम् ।
स वै नाम्रा पुनस्त्वष्टा त्रिदशानां च वार्धकिः ॥ 16
1.79.m: She gave birth to Viśvakarman, the foremost maker of all arts and crafts; / he is also named Tvaṣṭṛ, the carpenter of the gods.

1.79.s:
devācāryaśca tasyeyaṃ duhitā viśvakarmaṇaḥ .
sureṇuriti vikhyātā triṣu lokeṣu bhāminī . . 17
1.79.d:
देवाचार्यश्च तस्येयं दुहिता विश्वकर्मणः ।
सुरेणुरिति विख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु भामिनी ॥ 17
1.79.m: And the teacher of the gods had this daughter of Viśvakarman, / renowned throughout the three worlds by the name of Sureṇu, a passionate woman.

1.79.s:
rājñī saṃjñā ca dyaustvāṣṭrī prabhā saiva vibhāvyate .
tasyāttu yā tanucchāyā nikṣubhā sā mahīmayī . . 18
1.79.d:
राज्ञी संज्ञा च द्यौस्त्वाष्ट्री प्रभा सैव विभाव्यते ।
तस्यात्तु या तनुच्छाया निक्षुभा सा महीमयी ॥ 18
1.79.m: Rājñī, Saṃjñā, Dyauḥ, Tvāṣṭrī, and Prabhā are conceived as one and the same; / but her shadow-body, Nikṣubhā, is composed of the earth.

1.79.s:
sā1 tu bhāryā bhagavato mārtaṇḍasya mahātmanaḥ .
sādhvī pativratā devī rūpayauvanaśālinī . . 19
1.79.d:
सा1 तु भार्या भगवतो मार्तण्डस्य महात्मनः ।
साध्वी पतिव्रता देवी रूपयौवनशालिनी ॥ 19
1.79.m: She was the wife of the lord, the great-souled Mārtaṇḍa, / a virtuous goddess, devoted to her husband, endowed with beauty and youth.

1.79.s:
na tu tāṃ nararūpeṇa sūryo bhajati vai purā .
ādityasyeha tadrūpaṃ mahatā svena tejasā . . 1.79.20
1.79.d:
न तु तां नररूपेण सूर्यो भजति वै पुरा ।
आदित्यस्येह तद्रूपं महता स्वेन तेजसा ॥ 1.79.20
1.79.m: In ancient times, the sun did not approach her in human form; / the form of the Āditya here [shone] with immense radiance of his own.

1.79.s:
gātreṣvapratirūpeṣu nātikāntamivābhavat .
aniṣpatreṣu gātreṣu golaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitāmahaḥ . . 21
1.79.d:
गात्रेष्वप्रतिरूपेषु नातिकान्तमिवाभवत् ।
अनिष्पत्रेषु गात्रेषु गोलं दृष्ट्वा पितामहः ॥ 21
1.79.m: His limbs being unequalled, he was not very attractive; / seeing that globe with limbs lacking definition, the Grandfather [said]:

1.79.s:
mārtastvaṃ bhava cāṇḍastu mārtaṇḍastena sa smṛtaḥ .
devānāṃ ca yatastvādistenāditya iti smṛtaḥ . . 22
1.79.d:
मार्तस्त्वं भव चाण्डस्तु मार्तण्डस्तेन स स्मृतः ।
देवानां च यतस्त्वादिस्तेनादित्य इति स्मृतः ॥ 22
1.79.m: "Be thou dead-in-the-egg (mārta-aṇḍa)!" Therefore he is known as Mārtaṇḍa. / And because he is the foremost of the gods, he is known as Āditya.

1.79.s:
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi prajāstasya mahātmanaḥ .
trīṇyapatyāni saṃjñāyāṃ janayāmāsa vai raviḥ . . 23
1.79.d:
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रजास्तस्य महात्मनः ।
त्रीण्यपत्यानि संज्ञायां जनयामास वै रविः ॥ 23
1.79.m: Hereafter I shall declare the progeny of that great soul: / the Sun begot three children upon Saṃjñā.

1.79.s:
varṣāṇāṃ tu sahasraṃ vai vasamānā piturgṛhe .
bhartuḥ samīpaṃ yāhīti pitroktā sā punaḥpunaḥ . . 24
1.79.d:
वर्षाणां तु सहस्रं वै वसमाना पितुर्गृहे ।
भर्तुः समीपं याहीति पित्रोक्ता सा पुनःपुनः ॥ 24
1.79.m: Dwelling for a thousand years in her father's house, / she was repeatedly told by her father: "Go to your husband!"

1.79.s:
agacchadvaḍavā bhūtvā tyaktvā rūpaṃ yaśasvinī .
uttarāṃśca kurūngatvā tṛṇānyanucacāra ha . . 25
1.79.d:
अगच्छद्वडवा भूत्वा त्यक्त्वा रूपं यशस्विनी ।
उत्तरांश्च कुरून्गत्वा तृणान्यनुचचार ह ॥ 25
1.79.m: Abandoning her form and turning into a mare, the illustrious lady departed / and, going to the Northern Kurus, grazed upon grasses.

1.79.s:
pituḥ samīpaṃ yā bhāryā saṃjñā yā vacanena sā .
saṃjñāyā dhārayadrūpaṃ chāyā sūryamupasthitā . . 26
1.79.d:
पितुः समीपं या भार्या संज्ञा या वचनेन सा ।
संज्ञाया धारयद्रूपं छाया सूर्यमुपस्थिता ॥ 26
1.79.m: That wife who had gone to her father—by the command of Saṃjñā, / Chāyā, assuming the form of Saṃjñā, attended upon the Sun.

1.79.s:
dvitīyāyāṃ tu saṃjñāyāṃ saṃjñeyamiti cintayan .
ādityo janayāmāsa putrau kanyāṃ ca rūpiṇīm . . 27
1.79.d:
द्वितीयायां तु संज्ञायां संज्ञेयमिति चिन्तयन् ।
आदित्यो जनयामास पुत्रौ कन्यां च रूपिणीम् ॥ 27
1.79.m: Thinking, "This is Saṃjñā," the Āditya begot upon that second Saṃjñā / two sons and a shapely daughter.

1.79.s:
pūrvajasya manostulyau sādṛśyena ca tāvubhau .
śrutaśravāśca dharmajñaḥ śrutakarmā tathaiva ca . . 28
1.79.d:
पूर्वजस्य मनोस्तुल्यौ सादृश्येन च तावुभौ ।
श्रुतश्रवाश्च धर्मज्ञः श्रुतकर्मा तथैव च ॥ 28
1.79.m: Both were equal in resemblance to their elder brother Manu: / Śrutaśravas, knower of righteousness, and likewise Śrutakarman.

1.79.s:
śrutaśravā manustābhyāṃ sāvarṇiryo bhaviṣyati .
śrutakarmā tu vijñeyo graho yo vai śanaiścaraḥ . . 29
1.79.d:
श्रुतश्रवा मनुस्ताभ्यां सावर्णिर्यो भविष्यति ।
श्रुतकर्मा तु विज्ञेयो ग्रहो यो वै शनैश्चरः ॥ 29
1.79.m: Śrutaśravas of the two was the Manu who will become Sāvarṇi; / Śrutakarman is to be known as the planet Saturn.

1.79.s:
kanyā ca tapatī nāma rūpeṇāpratirūpiṇī .
saṃjñā tu pārthivī teṣāmātmajānāṃ yathākarot . . 1.79.30
1.79.d:
कन्या च तपती नाम रूपेणाप्रतिरूपिणी ।
संज्ञा तु पार्थिवी तेषामात्मजानां यथाकरोत् ॥ 1.79.30
1.79.m: And the maiden was named Tapatī, peerless in beauty. / But the earthly Saṃjñā, just as she acted toward her own children,

1.79.s:
na snehaṃ pūrvajānāṃ tu tathā kṛtavatī tu sā .
manustu kṣamate tasyā yamastasyā na cakṣame . . 31
1.79.d:
न स्नेहं पूर्वजानां तु तथा कृतवती तु सा ।
मनुस्तु क्षमते तस्या यमस्तस्या न चक्षमे ॥ 31
1.79.m: did not show the same affection toward the earlier-born. / Manu tolerated her [behaviour], but Yama did not tolerate her.

1.79.s:
bahuśo yātyamānastu pituḥ patnyā suduḥkhitaḥ .
sa vai kopācca bālyācca bhāvino'rthasya vai balāt . . 32
1.79.d:
बहुशो यात्यमानस्तु पितुः पत्न्या सुदुःखितः ।
स वै कोपाच्च बाल्याच्च भाविनोऽर्थस्य वै बलात् ॥ 32
1.79.m: Being tormented repeatedly by his father's wife, he became deeply distressed; / indeed, out of anger, childishness, and the force of what was destined to be,

1.79.s:
padā santarjayāmāsa saṃjñāṃ vaivasvato yamaḥ .
taṃ śaśāpa tataḥ krodhātsaṃjñā sā pārthivī bhṛśam . . 33
1.79.d:
पदा सन्तर्जयामास संज्ञां वैवस्वतो यमः ।
तं शशाप ततः क्रोधात्संज्ञा सा पार्थिवी भृशम् ॥ 33
1.79.m: Yama, son of Vivasvat, threatened Saṃjñā with his foot. / Thereupon that earthly Saṃjñā cursed him vehemently in anger:

1.79.s:
padā tarjayase yanmāṃ piturbhāryāṃ garīyasīm .
tasmāttavaiṣa caraṇaḥ patiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ . . 34
1.79.d:
पदा तर्जयसे यन्मां पितुर्भार्यां गरीयसीम् ।
तस्मात्तवैष चरणः पतिष्यति न संशयः ॥ 34
1.79.m: "Since you threaten me with your foot, me, your father's venerable wife, / therefore this foot of yours shall fall off, without a doubt!"

1.79.s:
yamastu tena śāpena bhṛśaṃ pīḍitamānasaḥ .
manunā saha tanmātuḥ pituḥ sarvaṃ nyavedayat . . 35
1.79.d:
यमस्तु तेन शापेन भृशं पीडितमानसः ।
मनुना सह तन्मातुः पितुः सर्वं न्यवेदयत् ॥ 35
1.79.m: Yama, his mind intensely afflicted by that curse, / reported everything concerning that mother to his father, along with Manu:

1.79.s:
snehena tulyamasmāsu mātā deva na vartate .
niḥsnehāñjyāyaso hyasmātkanīyāṃ saṃ bubhūṣati . . 36
1.79.d:
स्नेहेन तुल्यमस्मासु माता देव न वर्तते ।
निःस्नेहाञ्ज्यायसो ह्यस्मात्कनीयां सं बुभूषति ॥ 36
1.79.m: "Lord, mother does not treat us with equal affection; / devoid of affection for us older ones, she cherishes the younger ones.

1.79.s:
tasyā mayodyataḥ pādo na tu deva nipātitaḥ .
bālyādvā yadi vā mohāttadbhavānkṣantumarhati . . 37
1.79.d:
तस्या मयोद्यतः पादो न तु देव निपातितः ।
बाल्याद्वा यदि वा मोहात्तद्भवान्क्षन्तुमर्हति ॥ 37
1.79.m: My foot was raised toward her, but it was not brought down, O lord! / Whether through childishness or delusion, you ought to forgive that.

1.79.s:
śapto'hamasmiṃllokeśa jananyā tapatāṃ vara .
tava prasādāccaraṇastrāyatāṃ mahato bhayāt . . 38
1.79.d:
शप्तोऽहमस्मिंल्लोकेश जनन्या तपतां वर ।
तव प्रसादाच्चरणस्त्रायतां महतो भयात् ॥ 38
1.79.m: I have been cursed in this world, O lord, by my mother, O best of radiant ones! / Through your grace, let my foot be delivered from great danger!"

1.79.s:
raviruvāca
asaṃśayaṃ mahatputra bhaviṣyatyatra kāraṇam .
yena tvāmāviśatkrodho dharmajñaṃ dharmaśālinam . . 39
1.79.d:
रविरुवाच
असंशयं महत्पुत्र भविष्यत्यत्र कारणम् ।
येन त्वामाविशत्क्रोधो धर्मज्ञं धर्मशालिनम् ॥ 39
1.79.m: The Sun said: / "Doubtless, my son, there must be a great reason in this matter, / because of which anger overcame you, a knower of righteousness, full of virtue.

1.79.s:
sarveṣāmeva śāpānāṃ pratighātastu vidyate .
na tu mātrābhiśaptānāṃ kvacinmokṣo bhavediha . . 1.79.40
1.79.d:
सर्वेषामेव शापानां प्रतिघातस्तु विद्यते ।
न तु मात्राभिशप्तानां क्वचिन्मोक्षो भवेदिह ॥ 1.79.40
1.79.m: For all curses there is indeed a counteraction, / but for those cursed by a mother there can be no release anywhere in this world.

1.79.s:
na śakyametanmithyā me kartuṃ māturvacastava .
kiñcitte'haṃ vidhāsyāmi pitṛsnehādanugraham . .4 1
kṛmayo māṃsamādāya yāsyanti tu mahītale .
kṛtaṃ tasyā vacaḥ satyaṃ tvaṃ ca trāto bhaviṣyasi . .4 2
sumanturuvāca
ādityastvabravīcchāyāṃ kimarthaṃ tanayāvubhau .
tulyeṣvabhyadhikaḥ sneha ekatra kriyate tvayā . . 43
1.79.d:
न शक्यमेतन्मिथ्या मे कर्तुं मातुर्वचस्तव ।
किञ्चित्तेऽहं विधास्यामि पितृस्नेहादनुग्रहम् ॥4 1
कृमयो मांसमादाय यास्यन्ति तु महीतले ।
कृतं तस्या वचः सत्यं त्वं च त्रातो भविष्यसि ॥4 2
सुमन्तुरुवाच
आदित्यस्त्वब्रवीच्छायां किमर्थं तनयावुभौ ।
तुल्येष्वभ्यधिकः स्नेह एकत्र क्रियते त्वया ॥ 43
1.79.m:
I cannot make these words of your mother false; / nevertheless, out of paternal affection, I shall grant you a boon: / worms will take away the flesh and go to the surface of the earth; / her word will be fulfilled as true, and you will be saved."
Sumantu said: / The Āditya then said to Chāyā: "Why is it that, although both sets of sons / are equal, greater affection is shown by you to only one [set]?"

1.79.s:
sā1 tatpurābhavaṃ tasmai nācacakṣe vivasvate .
ātmānaṃ sa samādhāya vaktuṃ tasyāmapaśyat . .44
1.79.d:
सा1 तत्पुराभवं तस्मै नाचचक्षे विवस्वते ।
आत्मानं स समाधाय वक्तुं तस्यामपश्यत् ॥44
1.79.m: She did not disclose that former occurrence to Vivasvat. / Gathering himself in contemplation, he perceived the truth in her.

1.79.s:
tāṃ śaptukāmo bhagavānudyataḥ kupitastataḥ .
tataśchāyā yathāvṛttamācacakṣe vivasvate . . 45
1.79.d:
तां शप्तुकामो भगवानुद्यतः कुपितस्ततः ।
ततश्छाया यथावृत्तमाचचक्षे विवस्वते ॥ 45
1.79.m: The lord then became angry, ready to curse her; / thereupon Chāyā recounted to Vivasvat everything just as it happened.

1.79.s:
vivasvāṃstu tataḥ kruddhaḥ śrutvā śvaśuramāgataḥ .
sā cāpi taṃ yathānyāyamarcayitvā divākaram . .
nirdagdhukāmaṃ roṣeṇa sāntvayāmāsa taṃ śanaiḥ ..46
1.79.d:
विवस्वांस्तु ततः क्रुद्धः श्रुत्वा श्वशुरमागतः ।
सा चापि तं यथान्यायमर्चयित्वा दिवाकरम् ॥
निर्दग्धुकामं रोषेण सान्त्वयामास तं शनैः ॥46
1.79.m: Enraged on hearing this, Vivasvat went to his father-in-law. / And he, after duly worshipping the day-maker, / slowly pacified him who was eager to burn everything with his fury.

1.79.s:
viśvakarmovāca
tavātitejasāviṣṭamidaṃ rūpaṃ suduḥsaham .
asahantī tu saṃjñā ca vane carati śādvale ..47
1.79.d:
विश्वकर्मोवाच
तवातितेजसाविष्टमिदं रूपं सुदुःसहम् ।
असहन्ती तु संज्ञा च वने चरति शाद्वले ॥47
1.79.m: Viśvakarman said: / "Filled with excessive splendor, this form of yours is very difficult to endure; / unable to bear it, Saṃjñā wanders in a grassy forest.

1.79.s:
drakṣyate tāṃ bhavānadya svāṃ māyāṃ śubhacāriṇīm .
rūpārthaṃ bhavatoraṇye carantīṃ sumahattapaḥ ..48
1.79.d:
द्रक्ष्यते तां भवानद्य स्वां मायां शुभचारिणीम् ।
रूपार्थं भवतोरण्ये चरन्तीं सुमहत्तपः ॥48
1.79.m: You will see her today, your own power who acts auspiciously, / performing immense asceticism in the forest for the sake of your form.

1.79.s:
rūpaṃ te brahmaṇo vākyādyadi vai rocate vibho .
praśātayāmi devendra śreyo'rthaṃ jagataḥ prabho ..49
1.79.d:
रूपं ते ब्रह्मणो वाक्याद्यदि वै रोचते विभो ।
प्रशातयामि देवेन्द्र श्रेयोऽर्थं जगतः प्रभो ॥49
1.79.m: If it pleases you, O pervasive lord, by the command of Brahmā, / I shall pare down your form, O lord of gods, for the welfare of the world, O ruler!"

1.79.s:
santuṣṭastasya tadvākyaṃ bahu mene mahātapāḥ .
tato'nvajānāttvaṣṭāraṃ rūpanirvartanāya tu ..1.79.50
1.79.d:
सन्तुष्टस्तस्य तद्वाक्यं बहु मेने महातपाः ।
ततोऽन्वजानात्त्वष्टारं रूपनिर्वर्तनाय तु ॥1.79.50
1.79.m: Gratified, the great ascetic held his word in high esteem; / then he gave permission to Tvaṣṭṛ to reshape his form.

1.79.s:
viśvakarmā hyanujñātaḥ śākadvīpe vivasvataḥ .
bhramimāropya tattejaḥ śātayāmāsa tasya vai ..5 1
ājānulikhitaścāsau nipuṇaṃ viśvakarmaṇā .
lekhanaṃ nābhyanandattu tatastena nivāritaḥ ..52
1.79.d:
विश्वकर्मा ह्यनुज्ञातः शाकद्वीपे विवस्वतः ।
भ्रमिमारोप्य तत्तेजः शातयामास तस्य वै ॥5 1
आजानुलिखितश्चासौ निपुणं विश्वकर्मणा ।
लेखनं नाभ्यनन्दत्तु ततस्तेन निवारितः ॥52
1.79.m: Authorized [by him] on Śākadvīpa, Viśvakarman / mounted Vivasvat on a lathe and pared down his radiance. / And he was skillfully pared down to the knees by Viśvakarman; / but he did not rejoice at the carving, and so he was restrained by him.

1.79.s:
tatra tadbhāsitaṃ rūpaṃ tejasā prakṛtena tu .
kāntātkāntataraṃ bhūtvā adhikaṃ śuśubhe tataḥ ..53
1.79.d:
तत्र तद्भासितं रूपं तेजसा प्रकृतेन तु ।
कान्तात्कान्ततरं भूत्वा अधिकं शुशुभे ततः ॥53
1.79.m: There that form, illuminated by its natural radiance, / having become lovelier than the lovely, shone forth even more.

1.79.s:
dadarśa yogamāsthāya svāṃ bhāryāṃ vaḍavāṃ tathā .
adṛśyāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tejasā svena saṃvṛtām ..54
1.79.d:
ददर्श योगमास्थाय स्वां भार्यां वडवां तथा ।
अदृश्यां सर्वभूतानां तेजसा स्वेन संवृताम् ॥54
1.79.m: Resorting to yoga, he saw his wife as a mare, / invisible to all beings, enveloped in her own radiance.

1.79.s:
aśvarūpeṇa mārtaṇḍastāṃ mukhena samāsadat .
maithunāya viceṣṭanto parapuṃso viśaṅkayā ..55
1.79.d:
अश्वरूपेण मार्तण्डस्तां मुखेन समासदत् ।
मैथुनाय विचेष्टन्तो परपुंसो विशङ्कया ॥55
1.79.m: Taking the form of a stallion, Mārtaṇḍa approached her muzzle to muzzle, / striving for union while fearing another male.

1.79.s:
sā taṃ vivasvataḥ śukraṃ nāsābhyāṃ samadhārayat .
devau tasyāmajāyetāmaśvinau bhiṣajāṃ varau ..56
1.79.d:
सा तं विवस्वतः शुक्रं नासाभ्यां समधारयत् ।
देवौ तस्यामजायेतामश्विनौ भिषजां वरौ ॥56
1.79.m: Through her nostrils she received that semen of Vivasvat; / from her were born the two gods, the Aśvins, best of physicians.

1.79.s:
nāsatyaścaiva dasraśca tau smṛtau nāmato'śvinau .
ataḥ paraṃ svakaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa bhāskaraḥ ..
taddṛṣṭvā cāpi saṃjñā tu tutoṣa ca mumoha ca ..57
1.79.d:
नासत्यश्चैव दस्रश्च तौ स्मृतौ नामतोऽश्विनौ ।
अतः परं स्वकं रूपं दर्शयामास भास्करः ॥
तद्दृष्ट्वा चापि संज्ञा तु तुतोष च मुमोह च ॥57
1.79.m: They are known by name as the two Aśvins, Nāsatya and Dasra. / After this, the Sun showed his own form; / and seeing it, Saṃjñā was delighted and captivated.

1.79.s:
tatastu janayāmāsa saṃjñā sūryasutaṃ śubham .
rūpeṇa cātmanastulyaṃ revataṃ nāma nāmataḥ . . 58
1.79.d:
ततस्तु जनयामास संज्ञा सूर्यसुतं शुभम् ।
रूपेण चात्मनस्तुल्यं रेवतं नाम नामतः ॥ 58
1.79.m: Then Saṃjñā gave birth to an auspicious son of Sūrya, / equal to himself in beauty, Revata by name.

1.79.s:
pirtugṛhyāṣṭamaṃ so'śvaṃ jātamātraḥ palāyata .
sa tasmintsakṛdārūḍhastamaśvaṃ naiva muñjati . . 59
1.79.d:
पिर्तुगृह्याष्टमं सोऽश्वं जातमात्रः पलायत ।
स तस्मिन्त्सकृदारूढस्तमश्वं नैव मुञ्जति ॥ 59
1.79.m: Seizing the eighth horse of his father, the newborn immediately fled; / having mounted that horse once, he never relinquishes it.

1.79.s:
tato'rkeṇa samādiṣṭau daṇḍanāyakapiṅgalau .
aśvaṃ pratyānayethāṃ me mā balācchidrato'sya tu . . 1.79.60
1.79.d:
ततोऽर्केण समादिष्टौ दण्डनायकपिङ्गलौ ।
अश्वं प्रत्यानयेथां मे मा बलाच्छिद्रतोऽस्य तु ॥ 1.79.60
1.79.m: Then Daṇḍanāyaka and Piṅgala were commanded by Arka: / 'Bring back my horse, but not by force, [taking it] at his vulnerable moment.'

1.79.s:
pārśvasthau tiṣṭhatastasya aśvacchidrābhikāñkṣiṇau .
na cchidraṃ tu labhete tau tasyādyāpi mahātmanaḥ . . 61
1.79.d:
पार्श्वस्थौ तिष्ठतस्तस्य अश्वच्छिद्राभिकाञ्क्षिणौ ।
न च्छिद्रं तु लभेते तौ तस्याद्यापि महात्मनः ॥ 61
1.79.m: Standing at his side, eager for the horse's vulnerable moment, / the two have still not found a vulnerable moment of that great-souled one even today.

1.79.s:
plavangacchatyasau yasmātsaṃjñāyāḥ śāntidaḥ sutaḥ .
revṛstu ca gatau dhātū revantastena sa smṛtaḥ . . 62
1.79.d:
प्लवन्गच्छत्यसौ यस्मात्संज्ञायाः शान्तिदः सुतः ।
रेवृस्तु च गतौ धातू रेवन्तस्तेन स स्मृतः ॥ 62
1.79.m: Because this peaceful son of Saṃjñā moves by leaping— / the root *revṛ* meaning motion—he is remembered as Revanta.

1.79.s:
manuryamo yamī caiva sāvarṇiḥ sa śanaiścaraḥ .
tapatī cāśvinau caiva revantaśca raveḥ sutāḥ . . 63
1.79.d:
मनुर्यमो यमी चैव सावर्णिः स शनैश्चरः ।
तपती चाश्विनौ चैव रेवन्तश्च रवेः सुताः ॥ 63
1.79.m: Manu, Yama, Yamī, Sāvarṇi, Śanaiścara, / Tapatī, the two Aśvins, and Revanta are the children of Ravi.

1.79.s:
evameṣā purā saṃjñā dvitīyā pārthivī smṛtā .
yā saṃjñā sā smṛtā rājñī chāyā yā sā tu nikṣubhā . . 64
1.79.d:
एवमेषा पुरा संज्ञा द्वितीया पार्थिवी स्मृता ।
या संज्ञा सा स्मृता राज्ञी छाया या सा तु निक्षुभा ॥ 64
1.79.m: Thus of old this was Saṃjñā; the second is known as Pārthivī. / She who was Saṃjñā is known as Rājñī, while she who was Chāyā is Nikṣubhā.

1.79.s:
rājṛdīptau smṛto dhātū rājā rājati yatsadā .
adhikaḥ sarvabhūtebhyo rājate ca divākaraḥ . . 65
1.79.d:
राजृदीप्तौ स्मृतो धातू राजा राजति यत्सदा ।
अधिकः सर्वभूतेभ्यो राजते च दिवाकरः ॥ 65
1.79.m: The root *rājṛ* is recorded in the sense of shining; because a king (*rājā*) always shines, / and the Sun shines surpassingly above all beings,

1.79.s:
adhikaṃ rājate yasmāttasmādrājā sa ucyate .
rājñaḥ patnī tu sā yasmāttasmādrājñī prakīrtitā . . 66
1.79.d:
अधिकं राजते यस्मात्तस्माद्राजा स उच्यते ।
राज्ञः पत्नी तु सा यस्मात्तस्माद्राज्ञी प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 66
1.79.m: and because he shines surpassingly, he is called a king (*rājā*); / and because she is the king's wife, she is proclaimed as Rājñī.

1.79.s:
kṣubha sañcalane dhāturniścalā tena nikṣubhā .
bhavantītyatha vā yasmātsvargīyāḥ 1 kṣudvivarjitāḥ . .
chāyāṃ tāṃ viśate divyāṃ smṛtā sā tena nikṣubhā . . 67
1.79.d:
क्षुभ सञ्चलने धातुर्निश्चला तेन निक्षुभा ।
भवन्तीत्यथ वा यस्मात्स्वर्गीयाः 1 क्षुद्विवर्जिताः ॥
छायां तां विशते दिव्यां स्मृता सा तेन निक्षुभा ॥ 67
1.79.m: The root *kṣubh* means trembling; therefore she who is motionless is Nikṣubhā; / or rather, because the heavenly beings, free from hunger (*kṣudh*), / enter that divine Chāyā, she is on that account known as Nikṣubhā.

1.79.s:
dṛṣṭvā janaṃ sadā tāta bhṛśaṃ pīḍitamānasam .
dharmeṇa rañjayāmāsa dharmarājastataḥ smṛtaḥ . . 68
1.79.d:
दृष्ट्वा जनं सदा तात भृशं पीडितमानसम् ।
धर्मेण रञ्जयामास धर्मराजस्ततः स्मृतः ॥ 68
1.79.m: Seeing people always severely distressed in mind, dear boy, / he gladdened them with righteousness (*dharma*); hence he is known as Dharmarāja.

1.79.s:
śuddhena karmaṇā tāta śubhena paramadyutiḥ .
pitṝṇāmādhipatyaṃ ca lokapālatvamāpa ca . . 69
1.79.d:
शुद्धेन कर्मणा तात शुभेन परमद्युतिः ।
पितॄणामाधिपत्यं च लोकपालत्वमाप च ॥ 69
1.79.m: Through pure and auspicious action, dear boy, possessing supreme splendour, / he attained lordship over the ancestors and the rank of a world protector.

1.79.s:
sāmprataṃ vartate yo'yaṃ manurloke mahāmate .
yasyānvavāye jātastu śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ . . 1.79.70
1.79.d:
साम्प्रतं वर्तते योऽयं मनुर्लोके महामते ।
यस्यान्ववाये जातस्तु शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ॥ 1.79.70
1.79.m: This Manu who currently rules in the world, O wise one— / in his lineage the wielder of the conch, discus, and mace was born.

1.79.s:
yamasya bhaginī yā tu yamī kanyā yaśasvinī .
sābhavatsaritāṃ śreṣṭhā yamunā lokapāvanī . . 71
1.79.d:
यमस्य भगिनी या तु यमी कन्या यशस्विनी ।
साभवत्सरितां श्रेष्ठा यमुना लोकपावनी ॥ 71
1.79.m: Yama's sister, the illustrious maiden Yamī, / became the foremost of rivers, Yamunā, purifier of the world.

1.79.s:
manuḥ prajāpatistveṣa sāvarṇiḥ sa mahāyaśāḥ .
bhaviṣyansa manustāta aṣṭamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ . . 72
1.79.d:
मनुः प्रजापतिस्त्वेष सावर्णिः स महायशाः ।
भविष्यन्स मनुस्तात अष्टमः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 72
1.79.m: This Manu, indeed, is the Prajāpati Sāvarṇi of great fame; / he is proclaimed as the future eighth Manu, dear boy.

1.79.s:
merupṛṣṭhe tapo divyamadyāpi carate prabhuḥ .
bhrātā śanaibhrarastasya grahatvaṃ sa tu labdhavān . . 73
1.79.d:
मेरुपृष्ठे तपो दिव्यमद्यापि चरते प्रभुः ।
भ्राता शनैभ्ररस्तस्य ग्रहत्वं स तु लब्धवान् ॥ 73
1.79.m: Even today the lord performs divine austerities on the summit of Mount Meru. / His brother is Śanaiścara, who attained planetary status.

1.79.s:
tapatī nāma yā nāmnā tayoḥ kanyā garīyasī .
sā babhūva śubhā patnī rājñaḥ saṃvaraṇasya tu . . 74
1.79.d:
तपती नाम या नाम्ना तयोः कन्या गरीयसी ।
सा बभूव शुभा पत्नी राज्ञः संवरणस्य तु ॥ 74
1.79.m: The eldest daughter of the two, named Tapatī, / became the auspicious wife of King Saṃvaraṇa.

1.79.s:
tāpī nāma nadī ceyaṃ vindhyamūlādviniḥsṛtā .
nityaṃ puṇyajalā snāne paścimodadhigāminī . . 75
1.79.d:
तापी नाम नदी चेयं विन्ध्यमूलाद्विनिःसृता ।
नित्यं पुण्यजला स्नाने पश्चिमोदधिगामिनी ॥ 75
1.79.m: And this river named Tāpī, flowing forth from the foot of the Vindhya, / whose waters are ever holy for bathing, flows to the western ocean.

1.79.s:
saumyayā saṅgatā sā tu sarvapāpabhayāpahā .
vaivasvatī yathā vīra saṅgatā 1śivakāntayā . . 76
1.79.d:
सौम्यया सङ्गता सा तु सर्वपापभयापहा ।
वैवस्वती यथा वीर सङ्गता 1शिवकान्तया ॥ 76
1.79.m: Conjoined with the gentle [river], she removes all sins and fears, / just as Vaivasvatī, conjoined with the beloved of Śiva, [does so], O hero.

1.79.s:
aśvinau devavaidyatvaṃ labdhavantau yadūttama .
tayoḥ karmopajīvanti lokesminbhiṣajaḥ sadā . . 77
1.79.d:
अश्विनौ देववैद्यत्वं लब्धवन्तौ यदूत्तम ।
तयोः कर्मोपजीवन्ति लोकेस्मिन्भिषजः सदा ॥ 77
1.79.m: The two Aśvins attained the status of physicians to the gods, O best of the Yadus; / in this world physicians ever depend upon their work.

1.79.s:
revanto nāma yo'rkasya rūpeṇārkasamaḥ sutaḥ .
2aśvānāmādhipatye tu yojitaḥ sa tu bhānunā . . 78
1.79.d:
रेवन्तो नाम योऽर्कस्य रूपेणार्कसमः सुतः ।
2अश्वानामाधिपत्ये तु योजितः स तु भानुना ॥ 78
1.79.m: The son named Revanta, who is equal to the Sun in form, / was appointed by the Sun to the lordship over horses.

1.79.s:
kṣemeṇa gacchate'dhvānaṃ yastaṃ pūjayate pathi .
sukhaprasādyo martyānāṃ sadā yadukulodvaha . . 79
1.79.d:
क्षेमेण गच्छतेऽध्वानं यस्तं पूजयते पथि ।
सुखप्रसाद्यो मर्त्यानां सदा यदुकुलोद्वह ॥ 79
1.79.m: Whoever worships him on the road travels the way in safety; / he is easily propitiated by mortals, O upholder of the Yadu race.

1.79.s:
tvaṣṭāpi tejasā tena mārtaṇḍasyaiva cājñayā .
bhojānutpādayāmāsa pūjāyai satya suvrata . . 1.79.80
1.79.d:
त्वष्टापि तेजसा तेन मार्तण्डस्यैव चाज्ञया ।
भोजानुत्पादयामास पूजायै सत्य सुव्रत ॥ 1.79.80
1.79.m: Tvaṣṭṛ also, by that splendour and by the command of Mārtaṇḍa, / produced the Bhojas for [his] worship, O truly virtuous one.

1.79.s:
ya idaṃ janma devasya śṛṇuyādvā paṭheta vā .
vivasvato hi putrāṇāṃ sarveṣāmamitaujasām . . 81
1.79.d:
य इदं जन्म देवस्य शृणुयाद्वा पठेत वा ।
विवस्वतो हि पुत्राणां सर्वेषाममितौजसाम् ॥ 81
1.79.m: Whoever hears or recites this birth of the god / and of all the sons of Vivasvat of boundless splendour,

1.79.s:
sarvapāpavinirmukto yāti sūryasalokatām .
iha rājā bhavatyeva punaretya na saṃśayaḥ . . 82
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe
ādityamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 79 .
ādityamahimāvarṇanam
1.79.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो याति सूर्यसलोकताम् ।
इह राजा भवत्येव पुनरेत्य न संशयः ॥ 82
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे
आदित्यमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकोनाशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 79 ।
आदित्यमहिमावर्णनम्
1.79.m:
freed from all sins, goes to the world of Sūrya; / returning [to birth], he certainly becomes a king here, there is no doubt.
Thus ends the seventy-ninth chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of Āditya', in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan, in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa containing fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Greatness of Āditya

1.80.s:
sumanturuvāca
itthaṃ śrutvā kathāṃ divyāṃ helimāhātmyamāśritām .
sāmbaḥ papraccha bhūyo'pi nāradaṃ munisattamam . . 1
1.80.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
इत्थं श्रुत्वा कथां दिव्यां हेलिमाहात्म्यमाश्रिताम् ।
साम्बः पप्रच्छ भूयोऽपि नारदं मुनिसत्तमम् ॥ 1
1.80.m: Sumantu said: / Having thus heard the divine story relating to the greatness of Heli, / Sāmba once again asked Nārada, the best of sages.

1.80.s:
sāmba uvāca
sūryapūjāphalaṃ yacca yacca dānaphalaṃ mahat .
praṇipāte phalaṃ yacca gītavādye ca yat phalam . . 2
1.80.d:
साम्ब उवाच
सूर्यपूजाफलं यच्च यच्च दानफलं महत् ।
प्रणिपाते फलं यच्च गीतवाद्ये च यत् फलम् ॥ 2
1.80.m: Sāmba said: / The fruit of worshipping Sūrya, and the great fruit of giving gifts, / the fruit of prostration, and the fruit of singing and instrumental music,

1.80.s:
bhāskarasya dvijaśreṣṭha tanme brūhi samantataḥ .
yena sampūjayāmyeṣa bhānuṃ devaiḥ1 sadārcitam . 3
1.80.d:
भास्करस्य द्विजश्रेष्ठ तन्मे ब्रूहि समन्ततः ।
येन सम्पूजयाम्येष भानुं देवैः1 सदार्चितम् । 3
1.80.m: of the Sun, O best of the twice-born—tell me that in full, / so that I may worship the Sun, who is ever worshipped by the gods.

1.80.s:
nārada uvāca
imamarthaṃ purā pṛṣṭo brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ .
diṇḍinā yaduśārdūla śṛṇuṣvaikāgramānasaḥ . . 4
1.80.d:
नारद उवाच
इममर्थं पुरा पृष्टो ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ।
दिण्डिना यदुशार्दूल शृणुष्वैकाग्रमानसः ॥ 4
1.80.m: Nārada said: / Brahmā, grandfather of the worlds, was questioned on this matter of old / by Diṇḍi, O tiger among the Yadus; listen with single-minded attention.

1.80.s:
sukhāsīnaṃ tathā devaṃ surajyeṣṭhaṃ pitāmaham .
praṇamya śirasā diṇḍiridaṃ vacanamabravīt . . 5
1.80.d:
सुखासीनं तथा देवं सुरज्येष्ठं पितामहम् ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा दिण्डिरिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 5
1.80.m: Bowing his head to the god comfortably seated, the grandfather and eldest of the deities, / Diṇḍi spoke these words:

1.80.s:
diṇḍiruvāca
sūryapūjāphalaṃ brūhi brūhi dānaphalaṃ tathā .
praṇāme yatphalaṃ deva yaccoktaṃ tauryakatraye . . 6
1.80.d:
दिण्डिरुवाच
सूर्यपूजाफलं ब्रूहि ब्रूहि दानफलं तथा ।
प्रणामे यत्फलं देव यच्चोक्तं तौर्यकत्रये ॥ 6
1.80.m: Diṇḍi said: / Tell me the fruit of worshipping Sūrya, and likewise tell the fruit of giving gifts; / what fruit there is in bowing down, O god, and what is spoken of in the triad of performing arts;

1.80.s:
itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ kārite śravaṇe tathā .
purato devadevasya yatphalaṃ syāttaducyatām . . 7
1.80.d:
इतिहासपुराणाभ्यां कारिते श्रवणे तथा ।
पुरतो देवदेवस्य यत्फलं स्यात्तदुच्यताम् ॥ 7
1.80.m: likewise, what fruit there is when hearing of the Itihāsas and Purāṇas / is caused to be done before the God of gods, let that be told;

1.80.s:
mārjane lepane yacca devadevasya mandire .
bhāskarasya kṛte brūhi mama lokapitāmaha . . 8
1.80.d:
मार्जने लेपने यच्च देवदेवस्य मन्दिरे ।
भास्करस्य कृते ब्रूहि मम लोकपितामह ॥ 8
1.80.m: and what [fruit there is] in sweeping and plastering the temple of the God of gods— / tell me that for the Sun, O grandfather of the worlds.

1.80.s:
brahmovāca
stutijapyopahāreṇa pūjayā na naro raveḥ .
upavāsena ṣaṣṭhyāṃ ca sarvapāpaḥ pramucyate . . 9
1.80.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
स्तुतिजप्योपहारेण पूजया न नरो रवेः ।
उपवासेन षष्ठ्यां च सर्वपापः प्रमुच्यते ॥ 9
1.80.m: Brahmā said: / Through praise, recitation of mantras, offerings, and worship of Ravi, / and by fasting on the sixth lunar day, a man is released from all sin.

1.80.s:
praṇidhāya śiro bhūmau namaskāraparo raveḥ .
tatkṣaṇātsarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 1.80.10
1.80.d:
प्रणिधाय शिरो भूमौ नमस्कारपरो रवेः ।
तत्क्षणात्सर्वपापेभ्यो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥ 1.80.10
1.80.m: Devoted to bowing down before Ravi, having laid his head on the ground, / he is instantly freed from all sins; of this there is no doubt.

1.80.s:
bhaktiyukto naro yastu raveḥ kuryātpradakṣiṇām .
pradakṣiṇī kṛtā tena saptadvīpā 1bhavenmahī . . 11
1.80.d:
भक्तियुक्तो नरो यस्तु रवेः कुर्यात्प्रदक्षिणाम् ।
प्रदक्षिणी कृता तेन सप्तद्वीपा 1भवेन्मही ॥ 11
1.80.m: That man who, endowed with devotion, circumambulates Ravi / has circumambulated the earth with its seven continents.

1.80.s:
sūryalokaṃ vrajeccāpi iha rogaiśca mucyate .
upānahau parityajya anyathā narakaṃ vrajet . . 12
1.80.d:
सूर्यलोकं व्रजेच्चापि इह रोगैश्च मुच्यते ।
उपानहौ परित्यज्य अन्यथा नरकं व्रजेत् ॥ 12
1.80.m: He goes to the world of Sūrya, and here [on earth] is freed from diseases, / [provided he does so] having removed his shoes; otherwise he would go to hell.

1.80.s:
sopānatko naro yastu ārohetsūryamandiram .
sa yāti narakaṃ ghoramasipatravanaṃ vibho . . 13
1.80.d:
सोपानत्को नरो यस्तु आरोहेत्सूर्यमन्दिरम् ।
स याति नरकं घोरमसिपत्रवनं विभो ॥ 13
1.80.m: That man who should ascend into the temple of Sūrya wearing shoes / goes to the dreadful Asipatravana hell, O lord.

1.80.s:
sūryaṃ manasi yaḥ kṛtvā kuryādvyomapradakṣiṇām .
pradakṣiṇī kṛtāstena sarve devā bhavanti hi . . 14
1.80.d:
सूर्यं मनसि यः कृत्वा कुर्याद्व्योमप्रदक्षिणाम् ।
प्रदक्षिणी कृतास्तेन सर्वे देवा भवन्ति हि ॥ 14
1.80.m: He who, having fixed Sūrya in his mind, circumambulates the sky— / by him, indeed, all the gods have been circumambulated.

1.80.s:
parituṣṭāśca te sarve prayacchanti gatiṃ śubhām .
sarve devā mahābāho hyabhīṣṭaṃ tu parantapa . . 15
1.80.d:
परितुष्टाश्च ते सर्वे प्रयच्छन्ति गतिं शुभाम् ।
सर्वे देवा महाबाहो ह्यभीष्टं तु परन्तप ॥ 15
1.80.m: And when they are all well-pleased, they grant an auspicious state, / all the gods indeed grant what is desired, O great-armed scorcher of foes.

1.80.s:
ekāhāro naro bhūtvā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ yo'rcayate ravim .
saptamyāṃ vā mahābāho sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati . . 16
1.80.d:
एकाहारो नरो भूत्वा षष्ठ्यां योऽर्चयते रविम् ।
सप्तम्यां वा महाबाहो सूर्यलोकं स गच्छति ॥ 16
1.80.m: A man who, taking a single meal, worships the sun on the sixth / or on the seventh lunar day, O great-armed one, goes to the sun's realm.

1.80.s:
ahorātropavāsī sa pūjayedyastu bhāskaram .
saptamyāṃ vātha ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vā sa gacchetparamāṃ gatim . . 17
1.80.d:
अहोरात्रोपवासी स पूजयेद्यस्तु भास्करम् ।
सप्तम्यां वाथ षष्ठ्यां वा स गच्छेत्परमां गतिम् ॥ 17
1.80.m: And one who fasts day and night and worships the sun / on the seventh or on the sixth lunar day goes to the supreme state.

1.80.s:
kṛṣṇapakṣasya saptamyāṃ sopavāso jitendriyaḥ .
sarvaraktopahāreṇa pūjayedyastu bhāskaram . . 18
1.80.d:
कृष्णपक्षस्य सप्तम्यां सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः ।
सर्वरक्तोपहारेण पूजयेद्यस्तु भास्करम् ॥ 18
1.80.m: On the seventh lunar day of the dark fortnight, fasting and with senses conquered, / whoever worships the sun with an offering of all red things,

1.80.s:
paṅkajaiḥ karavīrairvā kuṅkamodakacandanaiḥ .
modakaiśca gaṇaśreṣṭha sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati . . 19
1.80.d:
पङ्कजैः करवीरैर्वा कुङ्कमोदकचन्दनैः ।
मोदकैश्च गणश्रेष्ठ सूर्यलोकं स गच्छति ॥ 19
1.80.m: with lotuses or oleanders, with saffron, water, and sandalwood, / and with sweetmeats, O best of the gaṇa, goes to the sun's realm.

1.80.s:
śuklapakṣasya saptamyāmupavāsarataḥ sadā .
sarvaśuklopahāreṇa pūjayedyastu bhāskaram . . 1.80.20
1.80.d:
शुक्लपक्षस्य सप्तम्यामुपवासरतः सदा ।
सर्वशुक्लोपहारेण पूजयेद्यस्तु भास्करम् ॥ 1.80.20
1.80.m: On the seventh lunar day of the bright fortnight, always devoted to fasting, / whoever worships the sun with an offering of all white things,

1.80.s:
jātīmudgarakaiścaiva śvetotpalakadambakaiḥ .
pāyasena 1tathā devaṃ savajreṇārcayedravim . . 21
1.80.d:
जातीमुद्गरकैश्चैव श्वेतोत्पलकदम्बकैः ।
पायसेन 1तथा देवं सवज्रेणार्चयेद्रविम् ॥ 21
1.80.m: with jasmine, mudgaraka flowers, white lotuses, and kadamba blossoms, / with milk-rice, and thus worships the sun-god with vajra flowers,

1.80.s:
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā vidhuḥ kāntyā na saṃśayaḥ .
haṃsayuktena yānena haṃsalokamavāpnute . . 22
1.80.d:
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा विधुः कान्त्या न संशयः ।
हंसयुक्तेन यानेन हंसलोकमवाप्नुते ॥ 22
1.80.m: his soul purified of all sins, like the moon in radiance, beyond doubt, / attains the world of the sun in a chariot harnessed to swans.

1.80.s:
diṇḍiruvāca
brūhi me vistarāddeva saptamīkalpamuttamam .
upoṣya saptamīṃ yena gamiṣye śaraṇaṃ raveḥ . . 23
1.80.d:
दिण्डिरुवाच
ब्रूहि मे विस्तराद्देव सप्तमीकल्पमुत्तमम् ।
उपोष्य सप्तमीं येन गमिष्ये शरणं रवेः ॥ 23
1.80.m: Diṇḍi said: / Tell me in detail, O god, the supreme rite of the seventh lunar day, / by fasting on which seventh lunar day I shall go to the sun's refuge.

1.80.s:
brahmovāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi bhavatā saptamīkalpamuttamam .
yathā sahasrakiraṇaḥ purā pṛṣṭo'ruṇena vai . . 24
1.80.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि भवता सप्तमीकल्पमुत्तमम् ।
यथा सहस्रकिरणः पुरा पृष्टोऽरुणेन वै ॥ 24
1.80.m: Brahmā said: / Well have I been asked by you regarding the supreme rite of the seventh lunar day, / just as of old the thousand-rayed sun was asked by Aruṇa.

1.80.s:
kathitāḥ sapta saptamyo bhānunā śreyase nṛṇām .
aruṇasya gaṇaśreṣṭha pṛcchataḥ kāraṇāntare . . 25
1.80.d:
कथिताः सप्त सप्तम्यो भानुना श्रेयसे नृणाम् ।
अरुणस्य गणश्रेष्ठ पृच्छतः कारणान्तरे ॥ 25
1.80.m: Seven seventh lunar days were described by the sun for the welfare of men / when Aruṇa asked on another occasion, O best of the gaṇa.

1.80.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya devadevaṃ divākaram .
dhyānamāśritya tiṣṭhantamaruṇo vākyamabravīt . . 26
1.80.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य देवदेवं दिवाकरम् ।
ध्यानमाश्रित्य तिष्ठन्तमरुणो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 26
1.80.m: Once at a certain time, to the god of gods, the sun, / who stood absorbed in meditation, Aruṇa spoke these words:

1.80.s:
kimarthaṃ devadevaśa dhyānamāśritya tiṣṭhasi .
dinaṃ na yāti deveśa kāraṇaṃ mama kathyatām . . 27
1.80.d:
किमर्थं देवदेवश ध्यानमाश्रित्य तिष्ठसि ।
दिनं न याति देवेश कारणं मम कथ्यताम् ॥ 27
1.80.m: "Why, O god of gods, do you stand absorbed in meditation? / The day does not pass, O lord of gods; let the reason be told to me.

1.80.s:
kuru caṅkramaṇaṃ deva vahamāno divaspate .
ityevaṃ bhagavānpṛṣṭa idaṃ vacanamabravīt . . 28
1.80.d:
कुरु चङ्क्रमणं देव वहमानो दिवस्पते ।
इत्येवं भगवान्पृष्ट इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 28
1.80.m: Perform your course, O god, moving along, O lord of the day-sky." / Being thus questioned, the Blessed One spoke this word:

1.80.s:
śṛṇu tvaṃ dvijaśārdūla yadarthaṃ dhyānamāśritaḥ .
arvāvasurdvijaśreṣṭhaḥ sa cāputraḥ khagottama . . 29
1.80.d:
शृणु त्वं द्विजशार्दूल यदर्थं ध्यानमाश्रितः ।
अर्वावसुर्द्विजश्रेष्ठः स चापुत्रः खगोत्तम ॥ 29
1.80.m: "Listen, O tiger among the twice-born, to the reason why I have resorted to meditation: / Arvāvasu, the best of the twice-born, is sonless, O best of birds.

1.80.s:
ārādhayati māṃ nityaṃ gandhapuṣpopahārakaiḥ .
putrakāmaḥ khagaśreṣṭha na ca jānātyayaṃ yathā . . 1.80.30
1.80.d:
आराधयति मां नित्यं गन्धपुष्पोपहारकैः ।
पुत्रकामः खगश्रेष्ठ न च जानात्ययं यथा ॥ 1.80.30
1.80.m: He worships me continually with perfumes, flowers, and offerings, / desiring a son, O best of birds, yet he does not know how

1.80.s:
putrado'haṃ bhave yena vidhinā pūjitaḥ khaga .
śrūyatāṃ ca vidhiḥ sarve yena prīto bhave nṛṇām . . 31
1.80.d:
पुत्रदोऽहं भवे येन विधिना पूजितः खग ।
श्रूयतां च विधिः सर्वे येन प्रीतो भवे नृणाम् ॥ 31
1.80.m: I become the giver of a son, by which rite I am worshipped, O bird. / And let the entire rite be heard by which I become pleased with men:

1.80.s:
saptamīkalpasaṃjño vai vidhīnāmuttamo vidhiḥ .
yastu māṃ pūjayennityaṃ tasya putrāndadāmyaham .. 32
1.80.d:
सप्तमीकल्पसंज्ञो वै विधीनामुत्तमो विधिः ।
यस्तु मां पूजयेन्नित्यं तस्य पुत्रान्ददाम्यहम् ॥ 32
1.80.m: the highest of all rites, indeed, known as the rite of the seventh lunar day. / Whoever worships me constantly, to him I give sons.

1.80.s:
gṛhṇīṣva saptamīkalpaṃ gatvā brūhi dvijottamam .
yenāhaṃ bahuputratvaṃ dadyāṃ tasya tathā khaga . . 33
1.80.d:
गृह्णीष्व सप्तमीकल्पं गत्वा ब्रूहि द्विजोत्तमम् ।
येनाहं बहुपुत्रत्वं दद्यां तस्य तथा खग ॥ 33
1.80.m: Receive the rite of the seventh lunar day, go, and tell that best of the twice-born, / so that I may grant him many sons, O bird."

1.80.s:
śrutvā bhānoḥ kṣaṇādeva jagāma sa khagottamaḥ .
kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ bhānorvacanamāditaḥ . . 34
1.80.d:
श्रुत्वा भानोः क्षणादेव जगाम स खगोत्तमः ।
कथयामास तत्सर्वं भानोर्वचनमादितः ॥ 34
1.80.m: Having heard from the sun, that best of birds departed instantly, / and related all that word of the sun from the beginning

1.80.s:
brāhmaṇasya khagaśreṣṭha sa ca śrutvā dvijottamaḥ .
cakāra saptamīkalpaṃ yathākhyātaṃ khagena tu . . 35
1.80.d:
ब्राह्मणस्य खगश्रेष्ठ स च श्रुत्वा द्विजोत्तमः ।
चकार सप्तमीकल्पं यथाख्यातं खगेन तु ॥ 35
1.80.m: to the brāhmaṇa, O best of birds; and having heard it, that best of the twice-born / performed the rite of the seventh lunar day just as told by the bird.

1.80.s:
ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ tathārogyaṃ prāpya putrāṃśca puṣkalān .
gato'sau sūryalokaṃ ca tejasā tatsamobhavat . . 36
1.80.d:
ऋद्धिं वृद्धिं तथारोग्यं प्राप्य पुत्रांश्च पुष्कलान् ।
गतोऽसौ सूर्यलोकं च तेजसा तत्समोभवत् ॥ 36
1.80.m: Attaining prosperity, increase, and freedom from disease, as well as abundant sons, / he went to the sun's realm and became equal to him in splendour.

1.80.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi
saptamīkalpamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 80 .
vijayāsaptamīvarṇanam
1.80.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि
सप्तमीकल्पमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामाशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 80 ।
विजयासप्तमीवर्णनम्
1.80.m:
Thus ends the eightieth chapter, called "Description of the Greatness of the Rite of the Seventh Lunar Day," in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Vijayāsaptamī

1.81.s:
brahmovāca
jayā ca vijayā caiva jayantī cāparājitā .
mahājavā ca nandā ca bhadrā cānyā prakīrtitā . . 1
1.81.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
जया च विजया चैव जयन्ती चापराजिता ।
महाजवा च नन्दा च भद्रा चान्या प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 1
1.81.m: Brahmā said: / Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, Aparājitā, / Mahājavā, Nandā, and another called Bhadrā are proclaimed.

1.81.s:
śuklapakṣasya saptamyāṃ sūryavāro bhavedyadi .
saptamī vijayā nāma tatra dattaṃ mahāphalam . . 2
1.81.d:
शुक्लपक्षस्य सप्तम्यां सूर्यवारो भवेद्यदि ।
सप्तमी विजया नाम तत्र दत्तं महाफलम् ॥ 2
1.81.m: If Sunday falls on the seventh lunar day of the bright fortnight, / that seventh lunar day is called Vijayā; whatever is given on it yields great fruit.

1.81.s:
snānaṃ dāna tathā homaṃ upavāsastathaiva ca.
sarvaṃ vijayasaptamyāṃ mahāpātakanāśanam . . 3
1.81.d:
स्नानं दान तथा होमं उपवासस्तथैव च।
सर्वं विजयसप्तम्यां महापातकनाशनम् ॥ 3
1.81.m: Bathing, giving, fire sacrifice, and likewise fasting— / all on Vijayāsaptamī destroy heinous sins.

1.81.s:
pañcamyāmekabhaktaṃ syātpaṣṭhyāṃ naktaṃ pracakṣate .
upavāsastu saptamyāmaṣṭamyāṃ pāraṇaṃ bhavet . . 4
1.81.d:
पञ्चम्यामेकभक्तं स्यात्पष्ठ्यां नक्तं प्रचक्षते ।
उपवासस्तु सप्तम्यामष्टम्यां पारणं भवेत् ॥ 4
1.81.m: On the fifth there should be a single meal, on the sixth a nocturnal meal is prescribed, / on the seventh fasting, and on the eighth the breaking of the fast.

1.81.s:
keciddevamuśantyeva neti cānye gaṇādhipa .
abhipretastu me 1 ṣaṣṭhyāmupavāso gaṇottama . . 5
1.81.d:
केचिद्देवमुशन्त्येव नेति चान्ये गणाधिप ।
अभिप्रेतस्तु मे 1 षष्ठ्यामुपवासो गणोत्तम ॥ 5
1.81.m: Some indeed wish it thus, O lord of the gaṇa, and others do not; / but fasting on the sixth is what I approve, O best of the gaṇa.

1.81.s:
caturthyāmekabhaktaṃ tu pañcamyāṃ naktamādiśet .
upavāsastu ṣaṣṭhyāṃ syātsaptamyāṃ pāraṇaṃ bhavet . 16
1.81.d:
चतुर्थ्यामेकभक्तं तु पञ्चम्यां नक्तमादिशेत् ।
उपवासस्तु षष्ठ्यां स्यात्सप्तम्यां पारणं भवेत् । 16
1.81.m: One should prescribe a single meal on the fourth, a nocturnal meal on the fifth, / fasting on the sixth, and breaking of the fast on the seventh.

1.81.s:
upavāsaparaḥ ṣaṣṭhyāmabdeśaṃ pūjayedbudhaḥ .
gandhapuṣpopahāraiśca bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ . . 7
1.81.d:
उपवासपरः षष्ठ्यामब्देशं पूजयेद्बुधः ।
गन्धपुष्पोपहारैश्च भक्त्या श्रद्धासमन्वितः ॥ 7
1.81.m: Devoted to fasting on the sixth, the wise man should worship the lord of the day / with perfumes, flowers, and offerings, endowed with devotion and faith.

1.81.s:
prakalpya pūjāṃ bhūmau tu devasya purataḥ svapet .
japamānastu2 gāyatrīṃ saurasūktamathāpi vā . . 8
1.81.d:
प्रकल्प्य पूजां भूमौ तु देवस्य पुरतः स्वपेत् ।
जपमानस्तु2 गायत्रीं सौरसूक्तमथापि वा ॥ 8
1.81.m: Having arranged the worship, he should sleep on the ground before the god, / reciting the Gāyatrī or the Saura hymn,

1.81.s:
akṣaraṃ vā mahāśvetaṃ ṣaḍakṣaramathāpi vā .
vibuddhastvatha saptamyāṃ kṛtvā snānaṃ gaṇādhipa . . 9
1.81.d:
अक्षरं वा महाश्वेतं षडक्षरमथापि वा ।
विबुद्धस्त्वथ सप्तम्यां कृत्वा स्नानं गणाधिप ॥ 9
1.81.m: or the great white syllable, or the six-syllabled mantra. / Awakening then on the seventh lunar day, having bathed, O lord of the gaṇa,

1.81.s:
graheśaṃ pūjayitvā tu homaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ .
brāhmaṇānbhojayedbhaktyā śaktyā ca gaṇanāyaka . . 1.81.1 0
śālyodanamapūpāśca khaṇḍaveṣṭāṃśca śaktitaḥ .
saghṛtaṃ pāyasaṃ dadyāttathā vipreṣu śaktitaḥ . . 11
1.81.d:
ग्रहेशं पूजयित्वा तु होमं कृत्वा विधानतः ।
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेद्भक्त्या शक्त्या च गणनायक ॥ 1.81.1 0
शाल्योदनमपूपाश्च खण्डवेष्टांश्च शक्तितः ।
सघृतं पायसं दद्यात्तथा विप्रेषु शक्तितः ॥ 11
1.81.m: having worshipped the lord of planets and performed the fire sacrifice according to rule, / he should feed brāhmaṇas with devotion and according to his means, O leader of the gaṇa, / with cooked rice of winter grain, cakes, and sweetmeats according to his ability; / likewise, according to his capacity, he should give milk-rice with clarified butter to the vipras.

1.81.s:
dattvā ca dakṣiṇā bhaktyā 1 tato viprānvisarjayet .
ityeṣā kathitā deva puṇyā vijayasaptamī . 12
1.81.d:
दत्त्वा च दक्षिणा भक्त्या 1 ततो विप्रान्विसर्जयेत् ।
इत्येषा कथिता देव पुण्या विजयसप्तमी । 12
1.81.m: And having given a sacrificial fee with devotion, he should then dismiss the vipras. / Thus has this holy Vijayāsaptamī been described, O god,

1.81.s:
yāmupoṣya naro gacchetpadaṃ vairocanaṃ param .
karavīrāṇi raktāni kuṅkumaṃ ca vilepanam . . 13
1.81.d:
यामुपोष्य नरो गच्छेत्पदं वैरोचनं परम् ।
करवीराणि रक्तानि कुङ्कुमं च विलेपनम् ॥ 13
1.81.m: by fasting on which a man goes to the supreme abode of the sun. / Red oleander flowers, saffron unguent,

1.81.s:
vijayaṃ dhūpamasyāṃ tu bhānostuṣṭikarāṇi vai .
eṣā puṇyā pāpaharā mahāpātakanāśinī . . 14
1.81.d:
विजयं धूपमस्यां तु भानोस्तुष्टिकराणि वै ।
एषा पुण्या पापहरा महापातकनाशिनी ॥ 14
1.81.m: and on this day the incense called vijaya indeed cause the sun's satisfaction. / This day is holy, sin-destroying, and a destroyer of heinous sins.

1.81.s:
atra dattaṃ hutaṃ cāpi kṣīyate na gaṇādhipa .
snānaṃ dānaṃ tathā homaḥ pitṛdevābhipūjanam . . 15
1.81.d:
अत्र दत्तं हुतं चापि क्षीयते न गणाधिप ।
स्नानं दानं तथा होमः पितृदेवाभिपूजनम् ॥ 15
1.81.m: What is given and offered into fire on this day does not diminish, O lord of the gaṇa. / Bathing, giving, fire sacrifice, and the worship of ancestors and gods—

1.81.s:
sarvaṃ vijayasaptamyāṃ mahāpātakanāśanam .
ādityavāreṇa yutā smṛtā vijayasaptamī .16
1.81.d:
सर्वं विजयसप्तम्यां महापातकनाशनम् ।
आदित्यवारेण युता स्मृता विजयसप्तमी .16
1.81.m: all on Vijayāsaptamī destroy heinous sins. / Joined with Sunday, it is traditionally known as Vijayāsaptamī.

1.81.s:
ityeṣā kathitā vīra sarvakāmapradāyinī .
dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ kīrtitaṃ śravaṇaṃ tathā . . 17
1.81.d:
इत्येषा कथिता वीर सर्वकामप्रदायिनी ।
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं कीर्तितं श्रवणं तथा ॥ 17
1.81.m: Thus this has been related, O hero, as granting all desires; / hearing it is proclaimed as bringing fortune, fame, and long life,

1.81.s: smaraṇaṃ tu tathāsyāṃ tu puṇyadaṃ tripurāntaka . . 18
1.81.d: स्मरणं तु तथास्यां तु पुण्यदं त्रिपुरान्तक ॥ 18
1.81.m: and remembering it brings merit, O destroyer of Tripura.

1.81.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe
vijayasaptamīvarṇanaṃ nāmaikāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 81 .
nandavarṇanam
1.81.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे
विजयसप्तमीवर्णनं नामैकाशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 81 ।
नन्दवर्णनम्
1.81.m:
Thus ends the eighty-first chapter, called "Description of the Vijayāsaptamī," in the Rite of the Seventh Lunar Day, in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand verses.
Description of Nandā

1.82.s:
diṇḍiruvāca
ye tvādityadine brahmanpūjayanti divākaram .
snānadānādikaṃ teṣāṃ kiṃ phalaṃ syādbravītu me..1
1.82.d:
दिण्डिरुवाच
ये त्वादित्यदिने ब्रह्मन्पूजयन्ति दिवाकरम् ।
स्नानदानादिकं तेषां किं फलं स्याद्ब्रवीतु मे॥1
1.82.m: Diṇḍi said: / Those who worship the sun on Sunday, O Brahman, / what fruit is there of their bathing, giving, and the like? Let it be told to me.

1.82.s:
puṇyā sā saptamī proktā yuktā tena pitāmaha .
vijayeti tathā nāma varṇyatāmasya 1 puṇyatā . . 2
1.82.d:
पुण्या सा सप्तमी प्रोक्ता युक्ता तेन पितामह ।
विजयेति तथा नाम वर्ण्यतामस्य 1 पुण्यता ॥ 2
1.82.m: That seventh lunar day combined with it has been declared holy, O grandfather, / with the name Vijayā; let its holiness be described.

1.82.s:
brahmovāca
ye tvādityadine brahmañchrāddhaṃ2 kurvanti mānavāḥ .
saptajanmasu te jātāḥ sambhavanti virogiṇaḥ . . 3
1.82.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
ये त्वादित्यदिने ब्रह्मञ्छ्राद्धं2 कुर्वन्ति मानवाः ।
सप्तजन्मसु ते जाताः सम्भवन्ति विरोगिणः ॥ 3
1.82.m: Brahmā said: / Men who perform a śrāddha on Sunday, O brāhmaṇa, / are born free from disease for seven births.

1.82.s:
naktaṃ kurvanti ye tatra mānavāḥ sthairyamāśritāḥ .
japamānā paraṃ jāpyamādityahadayaṃ param . .4
1.82.d:
नक्तं कुर्वन्ति ये तत्र मानवाः स्थैर्यमाश्रिताः ।
जपमाना परं जाप्यमादित्यहदयं परम् ॥4
1.82.m: Those men who observe a nocturnal meal on that day, remaining steadfast, / whispering the supreme mantra to be recited, the ultimate Ādityahṛdaya,

1.82.s:
ārogyamiha vai prāpya sūryalokaṃ vrajanti te .
upavāsaṃ ca ye kuryurādityasya dine sadā . . 5
1.82.d:
आरोग्यमिह वै प्राप्य सूर्यलोकं व्रजन्ति ते ।
उपवासं च ये कुर्युरादित्यस्य दिने सदा ॥ 5
1.82.m: having attained health in this world, go to the world of the Sun. / And those who always observe a fast on the day of the Sun,

1.82.s:
japanti ca mahāśvetāṃ te labhante yathepsitam .
ahorātreṇa naktena trirātraniyamena vā . . 6
1.82.d:
जपन्ति च महाश्वेतां ते लभन्ते यथेप्सितम् ।
अहोरात्रेण नक्तेन त्रिरात्रनियमेन वा ॥ 6
1.82.m: and recite the Mahāśvetā, attain whatever they desire, / whether through a full day and night, a nocturnal meal, or the discipline of three nights.

1.82.s:
japamāno mahāśvetāmīpsitaṃ labhate phalam .
viśeṣataḥ sūryadine japamāno gaṇādhipa . . 7
1.82.d:
जपमानो महाश्वेतामीप्सितं लभते फलम् ।
विशेषतः सूर्यदिने जपमानो गणाधिप ॥ 7
1.82.m: Reciting the Mahāśvetā, one obtains the desired fruit, / especially when reciting it on a Sunday, O lord of the gaṇas.

1.82.s:
ṣaḍakṣaraṃ3 tathā śvetāṃ gacchedvairocanaṃ padam .
dvādaśeha smṛtā vārā ādityasya mahātmanaḥ . . 8
1.82.d:
षडक्षरं3 तथा श्वेतां गच्छेद्वैरोचनं पदम् ।
द्वादशेह स्मृता वारा आदित्यस्य महात्मनः ॥ 8
1.82.m: [Reciting] the six-syllable mantra and the Śvetā, he goes to the realm of Vairocana. / Twelve days of the great-souled Sun are traditionally handed down here:

1.82.s:
nando bhadrastathā saumyaḥ kāmadaḥ putradastathā .
jayo jayanto vijaya ādityābhimukha sthitaḥ . . 9
1.82.d:
नन्दो भद्रस्तथा सौम्यः कामदः पुत्रदस्तथा ।
जयो जयन्तो विजय आदित्याभिमुख स्थितः ॥ 9
1.82.m: Nanda, Bhadra, Saumya, Kāmada, Putrada, / Jaya, Jayanta, Vijaya, Ādityābhimukhasthita,

1.82.s:
hṛdayo rogahā caiva mahāśvetapriyo'paraḥ .
śuklapakṣasya ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu māghe māsi gaṇādhipa . . 1.82.10
1.82.d:
हृदयो रोगहा चैव महाश्वेतप्रियोऽपरः ।
शुक्लपक्षस्य षष्ठ्यां तु माघे मासि गणाधिप ॥ 1.82.10
1.82.m: Hṛdaya, Rogahā, and another called Mahāśvetapriya. / On the sixth lunar day of the bright fortnight in the month of Māgha, O lord of the gaṇas,

1.82.s:
yaḥ4 kuryātsa bhavedbhūpaḥ sarvapāpabhayāpahaḥ .
atra naktaṃ smṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ ghṛtena snapanaṃ raveḥ . . 11
1.82.d:
यः4 कुर्यात्स भवेद्भूपः सर्वपापभयापहः ।
अत्र नक्तं स्मृतं पुण्यं घृतेन स्नपनं रवेः ॥ 11
1.82.m: whoever undertakes this becomes a king, free of fear from all sins. / Here a nocturnal meal is taught as meritorious, as is bathing the Sun with ghee.

1.82.s:
agastyakusumānīha bhānostuṣṭikarāṇi tu .
vilepanaṃ sugandhastu śvetacandanamuttamam . . 12
1.82.d:
अगस्त्यकुसुमानीह भानोस्तुष्टिकराणि तु ।
विलेपनं सुगन्धस्तु श्वेतचन्दनमुत्तमम् ॥ 12
1.82.m: Agastya flowers here bring delight to the Sun, / and the fragrant smearing is excellent white sandalwood;

1.82.s:
dhūpastu guggulaḥ śreṣṭho naivedyaṃ pūpameva hi .
dattvā pūpaṃ tu viprasya tato bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ . . 13
1.82.d:
धूपस्तु गुग्गुलः श्रेष्ठो नैवेद्यं पूपमेव हि ।
दत्त्वा पूपं तु विप्रस्य ततो भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥ 13
1.82.m: the incense is the best bdellium, and the food offering is indeed a cake of flour. / Having given the cake to a Brahmin, he should then eat in silence.

1.82.s:
nakṣatradarśanānnaktaṃ kecidicchanti mānada1 .
muhūrtonaṃ dinaṃ kecitpravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ . . 14
1.82.d:
नक्षत्रदर्शनान्नक्तं केचिदिच्छन्ति मानद1 ।
मुहूर्तोनं दिनं केचित्प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः ॥ 14
1.82.m: Some desire the nocturnal meal upon the appearance of the stars, O honour-giver; / some wise men state it to be when the day is short of a muhūrta.

1.82.s:
nakṣatradarśanānnaktamahammanye gaṇādhipa .
prasthamātraṃ bhavetpūpaṃ godhūmamayamuttamam . . 15
1.82.d:
नक्षत्रदर्शनान्नक्तमहम्मन्ये गणाधिप ।
प्रस्थमात्रं भवेत्पूपं गोधूममयमुत्तमम् ॥ 15
1.82.m: I consider the nocturnal meal to be upon the appearance of the stars, O lord of the gaṇas. / The cake should be of a prastha's measure, made of the best wheat,

1.82.s:
yavodbhavaṃ vā kurvīta saguḍaṃ sarpiṣānvitam .
sahiraṇyaṃ ca dātavyaṃ brāhmaṇe setihāsake 2 . . 16
1.82.d:
यवोद्भवं वा कुर्वीत सगुडं सर्पिषान्वितम् ।
सहिरण्यं च दातव्यं ब्राह्मणे सेतिहासके 2 ॥ 16
1.82.m: or one should make it of barley, mixed with jaggery and clarified butter. / Accompanied with gold, it should be given to a Brahmin versed in the Itihāsas.

1.82.s:
bhaume divye'tha vā deyaṃ nyasedvā purato raveḥ .
dātavyo mantrataścāyaṃ maṇḍako3 grāhya eva hi . . 17
1.82.d:
भौमे दिव्येऽथ वा देयं न्यसेद्वा पुरतो रवेः ।
दातव्यो मन्त्रतश्चायं मण्डको3 ग्राह्य एव हि ॥ 17
1.82.m: It should be given on an earthen [vessel] or a celestial one, or placed before the Sun; / and this pastry should be given and received with the mantra:

1.82.s:
bhūtvādityena vai bhaktyā ādityaṃ tu namasya ca .
ādityatejasotpannaṃ rājñīkaravinirmitam . .
śreyase mama vipra tvaṃ pratīcchāpūpamuttamam . . 18
1.82.d:
भूत्वादित्येन वै भक्त्या आदित्यं तु नमस्य च ।
आदित्यतेजसोत्पन्नं राज्ञीकरविनिर्मितम् ॥
श्रेयसे मम विप्र त्वं प्रतीच्छापूपमुत्तमम् ॥ 18
1.82.m: ‘Having become one with the Sun in devotion, and having bowed to the Sun: / Arisen from the splendour of the Sun, prepared by the hand of Rājñī, / O Brahmin, receive this excellent cake for my welfare!’

1.82.s:
kāmadaṃ sukhadaṃ dharmyaṃ dhanadaṃ putradaṃ tathā .
sadāstu te pratīcchāmi maṇḍakaṃ bhāskarapripam . . 19
1.82.d:
कामदं सुखदं धर्म्यं धनदं पुत्रदं तथा ।
सदास्तु ते प्रतीच्छामि मण्डकं भास्करप्रिपम् ॥ 19
1.82.m: ‘Granting desires, granting happiness, righteous, granting wealth, and granting sons, / may it always be yours! I receive the pastry dear to the Sun.’

1.82.s:
etau caiva mahāmantrau dānādāne ravipriyau .
apūpasya gaṇaśreṣṭha śreyase nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 1.82.20
1.82.d:
एतौ चैव महामन्त्रौ दानादाने रविप्रियौ ।
अपूपस्य गणश्रेष्ठ श्रेयसे नात्र संशयः ॥ 1.82.20
1.82.m: These two great mantras, dear to the Sun, are for the giving and receiving / of the cake, O best of the gaṇas, for welfare; there is no doubt here.

1.82.s:
eṣa nandavidhiḥ prokto narāṇāṃ śreyase vibho .
anena vidhinā yastu naraḥ4 pūjayate ravim . .
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sūryaloke mahīyate . . 21
1.82.d:
एष नन्दविधिः प्रोक्तो नराणां श्रेयसे विभो ।
अनेन विधिना यस्तु नरः4 पूजयते रविम् ॥
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥ 21
1.82.m: This procedure for Nanda has been declared for the welfare of men, O mighty one. / The man who worships the Sun according to this rite, / freed from all sins, is glorified in the world of the Sun.

1.82.s:
na daridraṃ na rogaśca kule tasya mahātmanaḥ .
yo'nena pūjayedbhānuṃ na kṣayaḥ santatestathā . . 22
1.82.d:
न दरिद्रं न रोगश्च कुले तस्य महात्मनः ।
योऽनेन पूजयेद्भानुं न क्षयः सन्ततेस्तथा ॥ 22
1.82.m: There is no poverty and no disease in the family of that great-souled one / who worships the Sun through this [observance], nor any decay of progeny.

1.82.s:
sūryalokāccyutaścāsau rājā bhavati bhūtale .
bahuratnasamāyukta6 stejasā dvijasannibhaḥ7 . . 23
1.82.d:
सूर्यलोकाच्च्युतश्चासौ राजा भवति भूतले ।
बहुरत्नसमायुक्त6 स्तेजसा द्विजसन्निभः7 ॥ 23
1.82.m: Falling from the world of the Sun, he becomes a king on the earth's surface, / endowed with many gems, resembling a twice-born in splendour.

1.82.s:
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ cedaṃ vidhānaṃ tripurāntaka .
kaṃ 1 dadātyacalaṃ divyamambujāmacalāṃ tathā . 24
1.82.d:
पठतां शृण्वतां चेदं विधानं त्रिपुरान्तक ।
कं 1 ददात्यचलं दिव्यमम्बुजामचलां तथा । 24
1.82.m: For those who read and listen to this ordinance, O destroyer of Tripura, / it grants celestial, immovable bliss and the immovable goddess born of the lotus.

1.82.s:
iti śrī bhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi ādityavārakalpe nandavidhivarṇanaṃ
nāma dvayaśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 82 .
bhadravidhivarṇanam
1.82.d:
इति श्री भविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि आदित्यवारकल्पे नन्दविधिवर्णनं
नाम द्वयशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 82 ।
भद्रविधिवर्णनम्
1.82.m:
Thus, in the glorious Bhaviṣyapurāṇa, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the section on the observance of Sundays, the description of the procedure for Nanda, being the eighty-second chapter.
Description of the procedure for Bhadra.

1.83.s:
brahmovāca
māsi bhādrapade vīra śukte pakṣe tu yo bhavet .
ṣaṣṭhyāṃ gaṇakulaśreṣṭha sa bhadraḥ parikīrtitaḥ . . 1
1.83.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
मासि भाद्रपदे वीर शुक्ते पक्षे तु यो भवेत् ।
षष्ठ्यां गणकुलश्रेष्ठ स भद्रः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 1
1.83.m: Brahmā said: / In the month of Bhādrapada, O hero, on the bright fortnight, which falls / on the sixth lunar day, O best of the host of gaṇas, that is proclaimed as Bhadra.

1.83.s:
tatra naktaṃ tu yaḥ kuryādupavāsamathāpi vā .
haṃsayānasamārūḍho yāti haṃsasalokatām . . 2
1.83.d:
तत्र नक्तं तु यः कुर्यादुपवासमथापि वा ।
हंसयानसमारूढो याति हंससलोकताम् ॥ 2
1.83.m: Whoever observes a nocturnal meal there, or even a fast, / mounted on a swan-vehicle, attains the same world as the Swan [Sun].

1.83.s:
mālatīkusumānīha tathā śvetaṃ ca candanam .
vijayaṃ ca tathā dhūpaṃ naivedyaṃ pāyasaṃ param . . 3
1.83.d:
मालतीकुसुमानीह तथा श्वेतं च चन्दनम् ।
विजयं च तथा धूपं नैवेद्यं पायसं परम् ॥ 3
1.83.m: Mālatī flowers, white sandalwood, / incense named Vijaya, and the supreme food offering of milk-rice;

1.83.s:
pūjāyāṃ bhāskarasyeha kuryāttripurasūdanam .
itthaṃ sampūjya deveśaṃ madhyāhne ca dinādhipam . 4
1.83.d:
पूजायां भास्करस्येह कुर्यात्त्रिपुरसूदनम् ।
इत्थं सम्पूज्य देवेशं मध्याह्ने च दिनाधिपम् । 4
1.83.m: one should perform this in the worship of the Sun, O destroyer of Tripura. / Having thus worshipped the lord of gods, the lord of the day at midday,

1.83.s:
dattvā tu dakṣiṇāṃ śaktyā tato bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ .
pāyasaṃ gaṇaśārdūla saguḍaṃ sarpiṣā saha . 5
1.83.d:
दत्त्वा तु दक्षिणां शक्त्या ततो भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ।
पायसं गणशार्दूल सगुडं सर्पिषा सह । 5
1.83.m: and given a priestly fee according to one's capacity, one should then eat in silence / milk-rice mixed with jaggery and clarified butter, O tiger among gaṇas.

1.83.s:
ya evaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā mānavastimirāpaham .
sarvakāmānavāpnoti putradāradhanādikān . . 6
1.83.d:
य एवं पूजयेद्भक्त्या मानवस्तिमिरापहम् ।
सर्वकामानवाप्नोति पुत्रदारधनादिकान् ॥ 6
1.83.m: The man who thus worships the dispeller of darkness with devotion / obtains all desires—sons, wives, wealth, and the rest;

1.83.s:
vimuktaḥ sarvapāpebhyo vrajadbhānusalokatām .
eṣa bhadrā vidhiḥ prokto mayā yaste gaṇādhipa ..7
1.83.d:
विमुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यो व्रजद्भानुसलोकताम् ।
एष भद्रा विधिः प्रोक्तो मया यस्ते गणाधिप ॥7
1.83.m: freed from all sins, he goes to the same world as the Sun. / This procedure for Bhadra has been declared by me to you, O lord of the gaṇas,

1.83.s: śrutvā kṛtvā ca yatpāpānmucyate mānavo bhuvi . . 8
1.83.d: श्रुत्वा कृत्वा च यत्पापान्मुच्यते मानवो भुवि ॥ 8
1.83.m: by hearing and performing which a man on earth is freed from sin.

1.83.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇyādityavārakalpe bhadravidhivarṇanaṃ nāma
tryaśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 83 .
saumyavidhivarṇanam
1.83.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वण्यादित्यवारकल्पे भद्रविधिवर्णनं नाम
त्र्यशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 83 ।
सौम्यविधिवर्णनम्
1.83.m:
Thus, in the glorious Bhaviṣyapurāṇa, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the section on the observance of Sundays, the description of the procedure for Bhadra, being the eighty-third chapter.
Description of the procedure for Saumya.

1.84.s:
brahmovāca
nakṣatraṃ rohiṇī vīra yadā vāre'sya vai bhavet .
yātyasau saumyatāṃ vīra1 sa saumyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ . . 1
1.84.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नक्षत्रं रोहिणी वीर यदा वारेऽस्य वै भवेत् ।
यात्यसौ सौम्यतां वीर1 स सौम्यः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 1
1.84.m: Brahmā said: / When the asterism Rohiṇī falls on his day, O hero, / that day attains pleasantness, O hero, and is proclaimed as Saumya.

1.84.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ pitṛdevāditarpaṇam .
akṣayaṃ syānna sandehastvatra vāre mahātmanaḥ . . 2
1.84.d:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः पितृदेवादितर्पणम् ।
अक्षयं स्यान्न सन्देहस्त्वत्र वारे महात्मनः ॥ 2
1.84.m: Bathing, giving gifts, recitation, fire offering, and libations to ancestors, gods, and others, / become inexhaustible—there is no doubt—on this day of the great-souled one.

1.84.s:
naktaṃ samāśrito yo'tra pūjayedbhāskaraṃ naraḥ .
yāti lokaṃ sa devasya bhāskarasya na saṃśayaḥ . . 3
1.84.d:
नक्तं समाश्रितो योऽत्र पूजयेद्भास्करं नरः ।
याति लोकं स देवस्य भास्करस्य न संशयः ॥ 3
1.84.m: The man who, observing a nocturnal meal on this day, worships the Sun, / goes to the world of the divine Sun; of this there is no doubt.

1.84.s:
raktotpalāni vai tatra tathā raktaṃ ca candanam .
sugandhaścāpi dhūpastu naivedyaṃ pāyasaṃ tathā . .
brāhmaṇāya ca dātavyaṃ bhoktavyaṃ cātmanā tathā . . 4
1.84.d:
रक्तोत्पलानि वै तत्र तथा रक्तं च चन्दनम् ।
सुगन्धश्चापि धूपस्तु नैवेद्यं पायसं तथा ॥
ब्राह्मणाय च दातव्यं भोक्तव्यं चात्मना तथा ॥ 4
1.84.m: Red water lilies are [offered] there, as well as red sandalwood, / fragrant incense, and likewise the food offering of milk-rice; / it should be given to a Brahmin and eaten by oneself.

1.84.s:
ya evaṃ pūjayetsaumye citrabhānuṃ gavāmpatim .
sa vimuktastu pāpebhyastvāṣṭrīṃ kāntimavāpnuyāt . . 5
1.84.d:
य एवं पूजयेत्सौम्ये चित्रभानुं गवाम्पतिम् ।
स विमुक्तस्तु पापेभ्यस्त्वाष्ट्रीं कान्तिमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 5
1.84.m: The one who thus worships the Fire of diverse rays, the lord of light rays, on Saumya, / is freed from sins and attains the splendour of Tvaṣṭṛ's daughter.

1.84.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi ādityavārakalpe saumyavidhivarṇanaṃ
nāma caturaśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 84 .
kāmadavidhivarṇanam
1.84.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि आदित्यवारकल्पे सौम्यविधिवर्णनं
नाम चतुरशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 84 ।
कामदविधिवर्णनम्
1.84.m:
Thus, in the glorious Bhaviṣyapurāṇa, in the Brāhmaparvan, in the section on the observance of Sundays, the description of the procedure for Saumya, being the eighty-fourth chapter.
Description of the procedure for Kāmada.

1.85.s:
brahmovāca
prāpte mārgaśire māsi śuklaṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu yo bhavet .
sa jñeyaḥ kāmado vāraḥ sadeṣṭo bhāskarasya tu . . 1
1.85.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
प्राप्ते मार्गशिरे मासि शुक्लषष्ठ्यां तु यो भवेत् ।
स ज्ञेयः कामदो वारः सदेष्टो भास्करस्य तु ॥ 1
1.85.m: Brahmā said: / When the month of Mārgaśīrṣa has arrived, whichever falls on the bright sixth lunar day, / that is to be known as the Kāmada day, always dear to the Sun.

1.85.s:
tatra yaḥ pūjayedbhānuṃ bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ .
vimuktaḥ sarvapāpaistu prāpnute nandanādhipam1 .. 2
1.85.d:
तत्र यः पूजयेद्भानुं भक्त्या श्रद्धासमन्वितः ।
विमुक्तः सर्वपापैस्तु प्राप्नुते नन्दनाधिपम्1 ॥ 2
1.85.m: Whoever worships the Sun on that day with devotion and endowed with faith, / freed from all sins, attains the master of Nandana.

1.85.s:
raktacandanamiśrāṇi karavīrāṇi suvrata .
dhūpaṃ ghṛtāhutiṃ vīra bhāskarasya prayojayet . . 3
1.85.d:
रक्तचन्दनमिश्राणि करवीराणि सुव्रत ।
धूपं घृताहुतिं वीर भास्करस्य प्रयोजयेत् ॥ 3
1.85.m: One should offer oleander flowers mixed with red sandalwood, O observer of good vows, / incense, and an oblation of ghee to the Sun, O hero;

1.85.s:
naivedyaṃ cāpi kṛśaraṃ sugandhaṃ tīkṣṇameva ca .
kṛtvopavāsamatha vā naktaṃ tripurasūdana . . 4
1.85.d:
नैवेद्यं चापि कृशरं सुगन्धं तीक्ष्णमेव च ।
कृत्वोपवासमथ वा नक्तं त्रिपुरसूदन ॥ 4
1.85.m: and the food offering should be spiced rice and grains, fragrant and pungent; / having observed a fast or a nocturnal meal, O destroyer of Tripura.

1.85.s:
itthaṃ prapūjito hyatra bhāskaro lokabhāskaraḥ .
kāmāndadāti sarvānvai atoyaṃ kāmadaḥ smṛtaḥ . . 5
1.85.d:
इत्थं प्रपूजितो ह्यत्र भास्करो लोकभास्करः ।
कामान्ददाति सर्वान्वै अतोयं कामदः स्मृतः ॥ 5
1.85.m: When the Sun, the illuminator of the worlds, is worshipped thus on this day, / he grants all desires; therefore it is remembered as Kāmada.

1.85.s:
sa putra putrakāmasya dhanakāmasya vā dhanam .
vidyārthine śubhāṃ vidyāmārogyaṃ rogiṇe vibho . . 6
1.85.d:
स पुत्र पुत्रकामस्य धनकामस्य वा धनम् ।
विद्यार्थिने शुभां विद्यामारोग्यं रोगिणे विभो ॥ 6
1.85.m: He grants a son to one who desires a son, or wealth to one who desires wealth, / auspicious knowledge to a seeker of knowledge, and health to a sick person, O mighty one.

1.85.s:
anyāṃśca vividhānkāmānmantraiḥ sampūjito raviḥ .
dadāti gaṇaśārdūla atoyaṃ kāmadaḥ smṛtaḥ . . 7
1.85.d:
अन्यांश्च विविधान्कामान्मन्त्रैः सम्पूजितो रविः ।
ददाति गणशार्दूल अतोयं कामदः स्मृतः ॥ 7
1.85.m: And worshiped with mantras, the sun gives various other desires, / O tiger among the Gaṇas; therefore it is called desire-granting.

1.85.s:
dadyādyo maṇḍakaṃ cātra gopatergotrabhūṣaṇaḥ .
gotrāritejasā3 tulyo gopatergopuraṃ vrajet . . 8
1.85.d:
दद्याद्यो मण्डकं चात्र गोपतेर्गोत्रभूषणः ।
गोत्रारितेजसा3 तुल्यो गोपतेर्गोपुरं व्रजेत् ॥ 8
1.85.m: Whoever gives a sweet cake here to the sun, an ornament to his lineage, / equal in splendor to Indra, would go to the gatehouse of the sun.

1.85.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi ādityavārakalpe kāmadavidhivarṇanaṃ
nāma pañcāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 85 .
jayavāratithivarṇanam
1.85.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि आदित्यवारकल्पे कामदविधिवर्णनं
नाम पञ्चाशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 85 ।
जयवारतिथिवर्णनम्
1.85.m:
Thus ends the eighty-fifth chapter, titled 'Description of the Rule for the Desire-granting [Sunday]', in the Aditya-Sunday ritual in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣyamahāpurāṇa.
Description of the lunar day of the Jayavāra

1.86.s:
brahmovāca
pañcatāraṃ bhavedyatra nakṣatraṃ te vṛṣadhvaja .
vāre tu devadevasya sa vāraḥ putradaḥ smṛtaḥ . . 1
1.86.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पञ्चतारं भवेद्यत्र नक्षत्रं ते वृषध्वज ।
वारे तु देवदेवस्य स वारः पुत्रदः स्मृतः ॥ 1
1.86.m: Brahmā said: / When a five-starred asterism occurs, O you whose banner is the bull, / on the day of the God of gods, that day is remembered as son-granting.

1.86.s:
upavāso bhavettatra śrāddhaṃ kāryaṃ tathā bhavet .
prāśanaṃ cāpi piṇḍasya madhyamasya prakīrtitam . . 2
1.86.d:
उपवासो भवेत्तत्र श्राद्धं कार्यं तथा भवेत् ।
प्राशनं चापि पिण्डस्य मध्यमस्य प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 2
1.86.m: Fasting should take place on that day, and an ancestral rite should also be performed; / and the eating of the middle ancestral cake is prescribed.

1.86.s:
sopavāsastu yo bhaktyā pūjayedatra gopatim .
dhūpamālyopahāraistu divyagandhasamanvitaiḥ . . 3
1.86.d:
सोपवासस्तु यो भक्त्या पूजयेदत्र गोपतिम् ।
धूपमाल्योपहारैस्तु दिव्यगन्धसमन्वितैः ॥ 3
1.86.m: Having fasted, whoever worships the sun here with devotion, / with offerings of incense and garlands endowed with divine perfumes,

1.86.s:
evaṃ pūjya vivasvantaṃ tasyaiva purato niśi .
bhūmau svapiti vai vīra japañchvetāṃ mahāmate . . 4
1.86.d:
एवं पूज्य विवस्वन्तं तस्यैव पुरतो निशि ।
भूमौ स्वपिति वै वीर जपञ्छ्वेतां महामते ॥ 4
1.86.m: Having thus worshiped Vivasvat, right in front of him at night / he sleeps on the ground, O hero, reciting the Śvetā mantra, O wise one.

1.86.s:
prātarutthāya ca snānaṃ kṛtvā dattvārghyamuttamam .
raktacandanasammiśraiḥ karavīrairgaṇādhipa . . 5
1.86.d:
प्रातरुत्थाय च स्नानं कृत्वा दत्त्वार्घ्यमुत्तमम् ।
रक्तचन्दनसम्मिश्रैः करवीरैर्गणाधिप ॥ 5
1.86.m: Rising at dawn and having bathed, offering an excellent water offering / with oleander blossoms mixed with red sandalwood, O lord of the Gaṇas,

1.86.s:
prapūjya grahabhūteśamaṃśumantaṃ trilocana .
vīraṃ 1 ca pūjayitvā tu tataḥ śrāddhaṃ prakalpayet . . 6
1.86.d:
प्रपूज्य ग्रहभूतेशमंशुमन्तं त्रिलोचन ।
वीरं 1 च पूजयित्वा तु ततः श्राद्धं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 6
1.86.m: Having worshiped the radiant lord of planets and beings, O three-eyed one, / and having worshiped the hero, he should then arrange an ancestral rite.

1.86.s:
pañcabhirbrāhmaṇairdeva divyaibhomaiśca2 suvrata .
magasaṃjñau3 tatra divyau brāhmaṇau parikalpayet . . 7
1.86.d:
पञ्चभिर्ब्राह्मणैर्देव दिव्यैभोमैश्च2 सुव्रत ।
मगसंज्ञौ3 तत्र दिव्यौ ब्राह्मणौ परिकल्पयेत् ॥ 7
1.86.m: With five Brahmins, O god, divine and earthly, O you of noble vows, / two divine Brahmins known as Magas should be designated there;

1.86.s:
trīnatra brāhmaṇānbhīmānprakalpyāndhakasūdana .
kuryādevaṃ tataḥ śrāddhaṃ pārvaṇaṃ bhāskarapriyam . . 8
1.86.d:
त्रीनत्र ब्राह्मणान्भीमान्प्रकल्प्यान्धकसूदन ।
कुर्यादेवं ततः श्राद्धं पार्वणं भास्करप्रियम् ॥ 8
1.86.m: Having designated three fierce Brahmins here, O slayer of Andhaka, / he should then perform the Pārvaṇa ancestral rite beloved of the Sun.

1.86.s:
śrāddhe tvatha samāpte tu dadyātpiṇḍaṃ tu madhyamam .
purato devadevasya sthitvā mantreṇa suvrata . . 9
1.86.d:
श्राद्धे त्वथ समाप्ते तु दद्यात्पिण्डं तु मध्यमम् ।
पुरतो देवदेवस्य स्थित्वा मन्त्रेण सुव्रत ॥ 9
1.86.m: When the ancestral rite is concluded, he should offer the middle ancestral cake, / standing before the God of gods with the mantra, O you of noble vows:

1.86.s:
sa eṣa piṇḍo deveśa yo'bhīṣṭastava sarvadā .
aśnāmi paśyate tubhyaṃ tena me santatirbhavet . . 1.86.10
1.86.d:
स एष पिण्डो देवेश योऽभीष्टस्तव सर्वदा ।
अश्नामि पश्यते तुभ्यं तेन मे सन्ततिर्भवेत् ॥ 1.86.10
1.86.m: 'This is that ancestral cake, O Lord of gods, which is always desired by you; / I eat it while you look on; through that may offspring be mine!

1.86.s:
prasādāttava deveśa iti me bhāvitaṃ manaḥ .
itthaṃ sampūjito hyatra bhāskaraḥ putrado bhavet . . 11
1.86.d:
प्रसादात्तव देवेश इति मे भावितं मनः ।
इत्थं सम्पूजितो ह्यत्र भास्करः पुत्रदो भवेत् ॥ 11
1.86.m: Through your grace, O Lord of gods!—thus is my mind directed.' / Worshiped in this way here, the Sun becomes a giver of sons.

1.86.s:
ato'yaṃ putrado vāro devasya parikīrtitaḥ .
evamatra sadā yastu bhāskaraṃ pūjayennaraḥ . . 12
1.86.d:
अतोऽयं पुत्रदो वारो देवस्य परिकीर्तितः ।
एवमत्र सदा यस्तु भास्करं पूजयेन्नरः ॥ 12
1.86.m: Therefore this day of the god is proclaimed as son-granting. / Whoever always worships the Sun in this manner here,

1.86.s:
upavāsaparaḥ śrāddhe sa putraṃ labhate dhruvam .
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca ārogyaṃ sukhadaṃ tathā . .
sūryalokaṃ ca samprāpya tato rājā bhavennṛṣu . . 13
1.86.d:
उपवासपरः श्राद्धे स पुत्रं लभते ध्रुवम् ।
धनं धान्यं हिरण्यं च आरोग्यं सुखदं तथा ॥
सूर्यलोकं च सम्प्राप्य ततो राजा भवेन्नृषु ॥ 13
1.86.m: intent on fasting during the ancestral rite, he certainly obtains a son, / wealth, grain, gold, and health that bestows happiness; / and having attained the realm of the Sun, he then becomes a king among men.

1.86.s:
prabhayā dvijasaṃkāśaḥ kāntyā cāmbujasannibhaḥ .
vīryeṇa gopatestulyo gāmbhīrye sāgaropamaḥ . . 14
1.86.d:
प्रभया द्विजसंकाशः कान्त्या चाम्बुजसन्निभः ।
वीर्येण गोपतेस्तुल्यो गाम्भीर्ये सागरोपमः ॥ 14
1.86.m: Resembling the moon in radiance and like a lotus in loveliness, / equal to the sun in strength, and like the ocean in depth.

1.86.s:
( iti putradavidhivarṇanam)
brahmovāca
dakṣiṇe tvayane yaḥ syātsa jayaḥ parikīrtitaḥ . . 15
1.86.d:
( इति पुत्रदविधिवर्णनम्)
ब्रह्मोवाच
दक्षिणे त्वयने यः स्यात्स जयः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 15
1.86.m: (Thus ends the description of the rule for the son-granting [observance].) / Brahmā said: / That which falls in the southern course [of the sun] is proclaimed as Jaya.

1.86.s:
atropavāso naktaṃ ca snānaṃ dānaṃ japastathā .
bhavecchataguṇaṃ deva bhāskaraprītaye kṛtam . . 16
1.86.d:
अत्रोपवासो नक्तं च स्नानं दानं जपस्तथा ।
भवेच्छतगुणं देव भास्करप्रीतये कृतम् ॥ 16
1.86.m: Here, fasting, nocturnal meals, bathing, gift-giving, and recitation of mantras, / done for the pleasure of the Sun, become multiplied a hundredfold, O god.
Therefore, nocturnal meals and the like should be performed, since it becomes multiplied a hundredfold, O Lord.

1.86.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi ādityavārakalpe jayavāratithivarṇanaṃ nāma
ṣaḍaśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 86 .
jayantavidhivarṇanam
1.86.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि आदित्यवारकल्पे जयवारतिथिवर्णनं नाम
षडशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 86 ।
जयन्तविधिवर्णनम्
1.86.m:
Thus ends the eighty-sixth chapter, titled 'Description of the Jayavāra and the Lunar Day', in the Aditya-Sunday ritual in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣyamahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Rule for the Jayanta [Sunday]

1.87.s:
brahmovāca
jayanto hyuttare jñeyaścāyane gaṇanāyaka .
vāro devasya yaḥ syādvai tatra pūjyo divākaraḥ . . 1
1.87.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
जयन्तो ह्युत्तरे ज्ञेयश्चायने गणनायक ।
वारो देवस्य यः स्याद्वै तत्र पूज्यो दिवाकरः ॥ 1
1.87.m: Brahmā said: / Jayanta is to be known in the northern course [of the sun], O leader of the Gaṇas; / on whichever day belongs to the god, the maker of day is to be worshiped there.

1.87.s:
pūjitastatra deveśaḥ sahasraguṇitaṃ phalam .
dadāti devaśārdūla snānadānādikarmaṇām . . 2
1.87.d:
पूजितस्तत्र देवेशः सहस्रगुणितं फलम् ।
ददाति देवशार्दूल स्नानदानादिकर्मणाम् ॥ 2
1.87.m: Worshiped there, the Lord of gods gives a thousandfold fruit, / O tiger among gods, of actions such as bathing and giving gifts.

1.87.s:
ghṛtena payasā yatra snānamikṣurasena tu .
vilepanaṃ kuṅkumaṃ tu praśastaṃ bhāskare priyam . . 3
1.87.d:
घृतेन पयसा यत्र स्नानमिक्षुरसेन तु ।
विलेपनं कुङ्कुमं तु प्रशस्तं भास्करे प्रियम् ॥ 3
1.87.m: Where bathing is done with ghee, milk, and sugarcane juice, / an ointment of saffron is praised, dear to the Sun.

1.87.s:
dhūpakriyā guggulena naivedye modakaḥ smṛtaḥ .
itthaṃ sampūjya deveśaṃ kuryāddhomaṃ tatastilaiḥ . .
brāhmaṇānbhojayetpaścānmodakāṃstilaśaṣkulīḥ . . 4
1.87.d:
धूपक्रिया गुग्गुलेन नैवेद्ये मोदकः स्मृतः ।
इत्थं सम्पूज्य देवेशं कुर्याद्धोमं ततस्तिलैः ॥
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्पश्चान्मोदकांस्तिलशष्कुलीः ॥ 4
1.87.m: The fumigation is done with bdellium, and the food offering is remembered as modaka; / having worshiped the Lord of gods thus, one should then make a fire sacrifice with sesamum; / afterwards one should feed Brahmins with modakas and sesamum cakes.

1.87.s:
itthaṃ yaḥ pūjayedbhānuṃ mantreṇaiva gaṇādhipa .
sahasraguṇitaṃ tasya phalaṃ devo dadāti vai . . 5.
snānadānajapādīnāmupavāsasya vai vibho . . 6
1.87.d:
इत्थं यः पूजयेद्भानुं मन्त्रेणैव गणाधिप ।
सहस्रगुणितं तस्य फलं देवो ददाति वै ॥ 5.
स्नानदानजपादीनामुपवासस्य वै विभो ॥ 6
1.87.m: Whoever worships the sun in this way with a mantra, O leader of the Gaṇas, / the god gives him a thousandfold fruit / of bathing, gift-giving, recitation of mantras, and fasting, O Lord.

1.87.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇyādityavārakalpe jayantavidhivarṇanaṃ nāma
saptāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 87 .
vijayavāravidhivarṇanam
1.87.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वण्यादित्यवारकल्पे जयन्तविधिवर्णनं नाम
सप्ताशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 87 ।
विजयवारविधिवर्णनम्
1.87.m:
Thus ends the eighty-seventh chapter, titled 'Description of the Rule for the Jayanta', in the Aditya-Sunday ritual in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣyamahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Rule for the Vijayavāra

1.88.s:
brahmovāca
śuklapakṣasya saptamyāṃ prājāpatyarkṣasaṃyutaḥ .
sa jñeyo vijayo nāma sarvapāpabhayāpahaḥ . . 1
1.88.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शुक्लपक्षस्य सप्तम्यां प्राजापत्यर्क्षसंयुतः ।
स ज्ञेयो विजयो नाम सर्वपापभयापहः ॥ 1
1.88.m: Brahmā said: / On the seventh lunar day of the bright fortnight, joined with the asterism sacred to Prajāpati, / it is known as Vijaya, dispelling all sins and fears.

1.88.s:
tatra koṭiguṇaṃ sarvaphalaṃ puṇyasya karmaṇaḥ .
dadāti bhagavāndevaḥ pūjitaścandanādhipaḥ . . 2
1.88.d:
तत्र कोटिगुणं सर्वफलं पुण्यस्य कर्मणः ।
ददाति भगवान्देवः पूजितश्चन्दनाधिपः ॥ 2
1.88.m: There the Blessed Lord, the master of sandalwood, gives ten million times / the full fruit of meritorious actions when he is worshiped.

1.88.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ pitṛdevādipūjanam .
naktaṃ cāpyupavāsastu sarvamatra divākaraḥ . . 3
1.88.d:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः पितृदेवादिपूजनम् ।
नक्तं चाप्युपवासस्तु सर्वमत्र दिवाकरः ॥ 3
1.88.m: Bathing, gift-giving, recitation of mantras, fire sacrifices, worship of ancestors, gods, and others, / nocturnal meals, and fasting—all this here the maker of day

1.88.s:
kuryātkoṭiguṇaṃ sarvaṃ pūjito hyatra gopatiḥ .
tasmādatra sadā devaṃ pūjayedbhaktimānnaraḥ . . 4
1.88.d:
कुर्यात्कोटिगुणं सर्वं पूजितो ह्यत्र गोपतिः ।
तस्मादत्र सदा देवं पूजयेद्भक्तिमान्नरः ॥ 4
1.88.m: multiplies ten-million-fold when the sun is worshiped here; / therefore a devoted man should always worship the god on this occasion,

1.88.s:
sarveśaṃ saptadvīpeśaṃ saptasaindhavavāhanam .
saptamyāṃ tu samārādhya saptaprakṛtisambhavam . .5
1.88.d:
सर्वेशं सप्तद्वीपेशं सप्तसैन्धववाहनम् ।
सप्तम्यां तु समाराध्य सप्तप्रकृतिसम्भवम् ॥5
1.88.m: The Lord of all, lord of the seven continents, who has seven horses for his vehicle; / having propitiated on the seventh day him who originates from the seven primary principles,
he obtains sovereignty over the seven worlds by means of the seven rays.

1.88.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇyādityavārakalpe vijayavāravidhivarṇanaṃ
nāmāṣṭāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 88 .
ādityābhimukhavidhivarṇanam
1.88.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वण्यादित्यवारकल्पे विजयवारविधिवर्णनं
नामाष्टाशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 88 ।
आदित्याभिमुखविधिवर्णनम्
1.88.m:
Thus ends the eighty-eighth chapter, titled 'Description of the Rule for the Vijayavāra', in the Aditya-Sunday ritual in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣyamahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Rule of Facing the Sun

1.89.s:
brahmovāca
kṛṣṇapakṣasya saptamyāṃ māghamāse bhavettu yaḥ .
sādityābhimukho1 jñeyaḥ śṛṇu cāsya vidhiṃ param . . 1
1.89.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
कृष्णपक्षस्य सप्तम्यां माघमासे भवेत्तु यः ।
सादित्याभिमुखो1 ज्ञेयः शृणु चास्य विधिं परम् ॥ 1
1.89.m: Brahmā said: / That which occurs on the seventh lunar day of the dark fortnight in the month of Māgha / is to be known as 'Facing the Sun'; hear its supreme rule.

1.89.s:
kṛtvaikabhaktaṃ kṛṣṇasya vāre tripurasūdana2 .
prātaḥ kṛtvā tataḥ snānaṃ pūjayitvā divākaram . . 2
1.89.d:
कृत्वैकभक्तं कृष्णस्य वारे त्रिपुरसूदन2 ।
प्रातः कृत्वा ततः स्नानं पूजयित्वा दिवाकरम् ॥ 2
1.89.m: Having eaten a single meal on the day of the dark fortnight, O destroyer of Tripura, / then having bathed in the morning and having worshiped the maker of day,

1.89.s:
ādityābhimukhastiṣṭhedyāvadastamanaṃ raveḥ .
japamāno mahāśvetāṃ lābhamāśritya suvrata . . 3
1.89.d:
आदित्याभिमुखस्तिष्ठेद्यावदस्तमनं रवेः ।
जपमानो महाश्वेतां लाभमाश्रित्य सुव्रत ॥ 3
