1.89.m: One should stand facing the sun until the setting of the sun, / reciting the Mahāśvetā mantra, intent upon benefit, O you of noble vows.

1.89.s:
caturhastamṛjaṃ ślakṣṇamavraṇaṃ susamaṃ dṛḍham .
raktacandanavṛkṣasya stambhaṃ kṛtvā gaṇādhipa . . 4
1.89.d:
चतुर्हस्तमृजं श्लक्ष्णमव्रणं सुसमं दृढम् ।
रक्तचन्दनवृक्षस्य स्तम्भं कृत्वा गणाधिप ॥ 4
1.89.m: Having made a pillar of red sandalwood four cubits long, smooth, / without blemishes, perfectly straight, and firm, O lord of the Gaṇas,

1.89.s:
tamāśritya mahābhaktyā devadevaṃ divākaram .
paśyamāno japañśvetāṃ tiṣṭhedastamanādraveḥ . . 5
1.89.d:
तमाश्रित्य महाभक्त्या देवदेवं दिवाकरम् ।
पश्यमानो जपञ्श्वेतां तिष्ठेदस्तमनाद्रवेः ॥ 5
1.89.m: Relying upon it with great devotion, beholding the maker of day, the God of gods, / reciting the Śvetā mantra, one should stand until the sun sets.

1.89.s:
gandhapuṣpopahāraistu pūjayitvā divākaram .
brāhmaṇe dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā tato bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ . . 6
1.89.d:
गन्धपुष्पोपहारैस्तु पूजयित्वा दिवाकरम् ।
ब्राह्मणे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा ततो भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ॥ 6
1.89.m: Having worshiped the maker of day with offerings of perfume and flowers, / and having given a priestly fee to a Brahmin, he should then eat with restrained speech.

1.89.s:
itthametaṃ tu yaḥ kuryādādityaprītaye naraḥ .
bhānumāṃstasya prītaḥ syātsarvaṃ prīto dadādi hi . . 7
1.89.d:
इत्थमेतं तु यः कुर्यादादित्यप्रीतये नरः ।
भानुमांस्तस्य प्रीतः स्यात्सर्वं प्रीतो ददादि हि ॥ 7
1.89.m: Whoever performs this in this way for the pleasure of the sun, / the radiant one is pleased with him and gives everything when pleased:

1.89.s:
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ tathā putramārogyaṃ bhārgavo yaśaḥ .
tasmātsampūjayedatra gīrvāṇādhipatiṃ hara . . 8
1.89.d:
धनं धान्यं तथा पुत्रमारोग्यं भार्गवो यशः ।
तस्मात्सम्पूजयेदत्र गीर्वाणाधिपतिं हर ॥ 8
1.89.m: wealth, grain, a son, health, brilliance, and fame; / therefore, one should worship the lord of the gods here, O Hara.

1.89.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇyādityavārakalpe ādityābhimukhavidhivarṇanaṃ
nāma navāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 89 .
hṛdayavāravidhivarṇanam
1.89.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वण्यादित्यवारकल्पे आदित्याभिमुखविधिवर्णनं
नाम नवाशीतितमोऽध्यायः । 89 ।
हृदयवारविधिवर्णनम्
1.89.m:
Thus ends the eighty-ninth chapter, titled 'Description of the Rule of Facing the Sun', in the Aditya-Sunday ritual in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣyamahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Rule for the Hṛdayavāra

1.90.s:
brahmovāca
ravisaṅkramaṇe yaḥ syādravervāro gaṇādhipa .
sa jñeyo hṛdayo nāma ādityahadayapriyaḥ . . 1
1.90.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
रविसङ्क्रमणे यः स्याद्रवेर्वारो गणाधिप ।
स ज्ञेयो हृदयो नाम आदित्यहदयप्रियः ॥ 1
1.90.m:
Brahmā said:
The solar day which falls at the Sun's transit, O leader of the ganas, / is to be known as 'Hṛdaya', dear to the heart of the Sun.

1.90.s:
tatra naktaṃ samāśritya devaṃ sampūjya bhaktitaḥ .
gatvā ca sadane bhānorādityābhimukhasthitaḥ . . 2
1.90.d:
तत्र नक्तं समाश्रित्य देवं सम्पूज्य भक्तितः ।
गत्वा च सदने भानोरादित्याभिमुखस्थितः ॥ 2
1.90.m: There, having resorted to the nocturnal meal and worshipped the deity with devotion, / and having gone to the abode of the Sun, remaining facing the Sun,

1.90.s:
japedādityahadayaṃ saṅkhyayāṣṭaśataṃ budhaḥ .
atha vāstamanaṃ yāvadbhāskaraṃ ciṃtayeddhṛdi . . 3
1.90.d:
जपेदादित्यहदयं सङ्ख्ययाष्टशतं बुधः ।
अथ वास्तमनं यावद्भास्करं चिंतयेद्धृदि ॥ 3
1.90.m: the wise man should recite the Ādityahṛdaya one hundred and eight times, / or else contemplate the Sun in his heart until sunset.

1.90.s:
gṛhametya tato viprānbhojayecchaktitaḥ śiva .
bhuktvā tu pāyasaṃ vīra tato bhūmau svapedbudhaḥ . . 4
1.90.d:
गृहमेत्य ततो विप्रान्भोजयेच्छक्तितः शिव ।
भुक्त्वा तु पायसं वीर ततो भूमौ स्वपेद्बुधः ॥ 4
1.90.m: Having returned home, O Śiva, he should then feed brahmins according to his ability. / Having eaten milk-rice, O hero, the wise man should then sleep on the ground.

1.90.s:
yo'tra sampūyedbhānuṃ bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ .
sa kāmām̐llabhate sarvānbhāskarāddhṛdayasthitān . . 5
1.90.d:
योऽत्र सम्पूयेद्भानुं भक्त्या श्रद्धासमन्वितः ।
स कामाम्̐ल्लभते सर्वान्भास्कराद्धृदयस्थितान् ॥ 5
1.90.m: Whoever worships the Sun here with devotion and endowed with faith / obtains from the Sun all the desires situated in his heart.

1.90.s:
tejasā yaśasā tulyaḥ prabhayaiṣāṃ mahātmanaḥ .
śakragopāṇḍajānāṃ tu gopatergovṛṣekṣaṇa . . 6
1.90.d:
तेजसा यशसा तुल्यः प्रभयैषां महात्मनः ।
शक्रगोपाण्डजानां तु गोपतेर्गोवृषेक्षण ॥ 6
1.90.m: He becomes equal in splendour and renown to the radiant energy of this great soul, / O bull-eyed one, [equal to] the lord of cows among birds and ladybugs.

1.90.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇyādityavārakalpe hṛdayavāravidhivarṇanaṃ
nāma navatitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 90 .
rogaharavidhivarṇanam
1.90.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वण्यादित्यवारकल्पे हृदयवारविधिवर्णनं
नाम नवतितमोऽध्यायः । 90 ।
रोगहरविधिवर्णनम्
1.90.m:
Thus ends the ninetieth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Rite of Hṛdayavāra', in the Ādityavārakalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Rite that Destroys Diseases

1.91.s:
brahmovāca
pūṣṇo bhavedyadā ṛkṣaṃ bhavecca bhagadaivatam .
vāsaraḥ sa mahānproktaḥ sarvarogabhayāpahaḥ . . 1
1.91.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
पूष्णो भवेद्यदा ऋक्षं भवेच्च भगदैवतम् ।
वासरः स महान्प्रोक्तः सर्वरोगभयापहः ॥ 1
1.91.m:
Brahmā said:
When the asterism belongs to Pūṣan and the deity is Bhaga, / that day is declared great, removing the fear of all diseases.

1.91.s:
yo'tra pūjayate bhānuṃ śubhagandhavilepanaiḥ .
sarvarogavinirmukto yāti bhānusalokatām . . 2
1.91.d:
योऽत्र पूजयते भानुं शुभगन्धविलेपनैः ।
सर्वरोगविनिर्मुक्तो याति भानुसलोकताम् ॥ 2
1.91.m: Whoever worships the Sun on this day with auspicious fragrant ointments / is freed from all diseases and attains the world of the Sun.

1.91.s:
arkapatrapuṭe kṛtyā puṣpāṇyarkasya suvrata .
devasya purato rātrau bhaktyā yaḥ sthāpayedbudhaḥ . . 3
1.91.d:
अर्कपत्रपुटे कृत्या पुष्पाण्यर्कस्य सुव्रत ।
देवस्य पुरतो रात्रौ भक्त्या यः स्थापयेद्बुधः ॥ 3
1.91.m: Having placed arka flowers in an arka-leaf cup, O you of good vows, / the wise man who devoutly places them before the deity at night,

1.91.s:
pūjayitvārkapuṣpaistu arkamarkapriyaṃ sadā .
prāśayitvārkapuṣpaṃ1 tu dattvā viprāya dakṣiṇām . . 4
1.91.d:
पूजयित्वार्कपुष्पैस्तु अर्कमर्कप्रियं सदा ।
प्राशयित्वार्कपुष्पं1 तु दत्त्वा विप्राय दक्षिणाम् ॥ 4
1.91.m: having worshipped with arka flowers the Sun who is ever fond of arka, / having consumed an arka flower, and having given a sacrificial fee to a brahmin,

1.91.s:
bhaktyā ca pāyasaṃ vīra rātrau svapiti bhūtale .
anena vidhinā yastu pūjayedatra vai ravim . . 5
1.91.d:
भक्त्या च पायसं वीर रात्रौ स्वपिति भूतले ।
अनेन विधिना यस्तु पूजयेदत्र वै रविम् ॥ 5
1.91.m: and [eaten] milk-rice with devotion, O hero, sleeps at night on the ground. / He who worships the Sun in this manner on this day,

1.91.s:
sa muktaḥ sarvarogaistu3 gaccheddinakarālayam4 .
tasmādapi vrajellokaṃ phuṃkāraravahetinaḥ . . 6
1.91.d:
स मुक्तः सर्वरोगैस्तु3 गच्छेद्दिनकरालयम्4 ।
तस्मादपि व्रजेल्लोकं फुंकाररवहेतिनः ॥ 6
1.91.m: freed from all diseases, goes to the abode of the Maker of the Day; / and from there he goes to the world of him whose weapon is the whistling roar.

1.91.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇyādityakalpe rogaharavidhivarṇanaṃ
nāmaikanavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 91 .
mahāśvetavāravidhivarṇanam
1.91.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वण्यादित्यकल्पे रोगहरविधिवर्णनं
नामैकनवतितमोऽध्यायः । 91 ।
महाश्वेतवारविधिवर्णनम्
1.91.m:
Thus ends the ninety-first chapter, entitled 'Description of the Rite that Destroys Diseases', in the Ādityakalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Rite of Mahāśvetāvāra

1.92.s:
brahmovāca
yastvādityagrahasyāsya vāro devasya suvrata .
śasyaḥ proktaḥ priyo loke khyāto gośrutibhūṣaṇaḥ . . 1
1.92.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यस्त्वादित्यग्रहस्यास्य वारो देवस्य सुव्रत ।
शस्यः प्रोक्तः प्रियो लोके ख्यातो गोश्रुतिभूषणः ॥ 1
1.92.m:
Brahmā said:
The day belonging to this deity of the Sun-eclipse, O you of good vows, / is declared praiseworthy and dear in the world, renowned as an ornament to Vedic revelation.

1.92.s:
yastu pūjayate tasminpataṅgaṃ patagapriyam .
gandhapuṣpopahāraistu sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati . . 2
1.92.d:
यस्तु पूजयते तस्मिन्पतङ्गं पतगप्रियम् ।
गन्धपुष्पोपहारैस्तु सूर्यलोकं स गच्छति ॥ 2
1.92.m: Whoever worships on this day the Sun, dear to birds, / with offerings of fragrant incense and flowers, goes to the world of the Sun.

1.92.s:
sopavāso gaṇaśreṣṭha ādityagrahaṇe śuciḥ .
japamāno mahāśvetāṃ khapoṣamatha vā śivam . . 3
1.92.d:
सोपवासो गणश्रेष्ठ आदित्यग्रहणे शुचिः ।
जपमानो महाश्वेतां खपोषमथ वा शिवम् ॥ 3
1.92.m: Fasting, O best of the ganas, pure during an eclipse of the Sun, / reciting [the mantra of] Mahāśvetā, or Khapoṣa, or Śiva,

1.92.s:
pūjayejjagatāmīśaṃ tamonāśanamāśugam .
pūjayitvā khapoṣaṃ tu mahāśvetāṃ tato japet . .4
1.92.d:
पूजयेज्जगतामीशं तमोनाशनमाशुगम् ।
पूजयित्वा खपोषं तु महाश्वेतां ततो जपेत् ॥4
1.92.m: he should worship the Lord of the worlds, the dispeller of darkness, swift-moving. / Having worshipped Khapoṣa, he should then recite [the mantra of] Mahāśvetā.

1.92.s:
pūjayitvā mahāśvetāṃ raviṃ devaṃ samarcayet 1 .
mahāśvetāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya gandhapuṣpaiḥ supūjitām . . 5
1.92.d:
पूजयित्वा महाश्वेतां रविं देवं समर्चयेत् 1 ।
महाश्वेतां प्रतिष्ठाप्य गन्धपुष्पैः सुपूजिताम् ॥ 5
1.92.m: Having worshipped Mahāśvetā, he should worship the divine Sun. / Having installed Mahāśvetā, well-honoured with perfumes and flowers,

1.92.s:
tasyā eva bahiḥ2 kāryaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ susamāhitaḥ .
śucau bhūmivibhāge tu vīraṃ saṃsthāpya yatnataḥ . . 6
1.92.d:
तस्या एव बहिः2 कार्यं स्थण्डिलं सुसमाहितः ।
शुचौ भूमिविभागे तु वीरं संस्थाप्य यत्नतः ॥ 6
1.92.m: a sacrificial ground should be prepared outside of her, highly concentrated in mind; / and having carefully placed the hero upon a pure piece of ground,

1.92.s:
kuryāddhomaṃ tilaiḥ snātaḥ sarpiṣā ca viśeṣataḥ .
ādityagrahavelāyāṃ japeñchvetāṃ mahāmate . . 7
1.92.d:
कुर्याद्धोमं तिलैः स्नातः सर्पिषा च विशेषतः ।
आदित्यग्रहवेलायां जपेञ्छ्वेतां महामते ॥ 7
1.92.m: having bathed, he should perform an oblation with sesame seeds and especially with clarified butter. / At the time of the solar eclipse, O highly intelligent one, he should recite [the mantra of] Śvetā.

1.92.s:
mukte dinakare paścātsnānaṃ kṛtvā samāhitaḥ .
pūjayitvā mahāśvetāṃ khagolkaṃ3 ca grahādhipam . . 8
1.92.d:
मुक्ते दिनकरे पश्चात्स्नानं कृत्वा समाहितः ।
पूजयित्वा महाश्वेतां खगोल्कं3 च ग्रहाधिपम् ॥ 8
1.92.m: After the Maker of the Day is released, having bathed with a concentrated mind, / and having worshipped Mahāśvetā, Khagolka, and the lord of the planets,

1.92.s:
brāhmaṇān vācayitvā ca tato bhuñjīta vāgyataḥ .
ādityagrahayukte'sminvāre tripurasūdana . . 9
1.92.d:
ब्राह्मणान् वाचयित्वा च ततो भुञ्जीत वाग्यतः ।
आदित्यग्रहयुक्तेऽस्मिन्वारे त्रिपुरसूदन ॥ 9
1.92.m: and having caused the brahmins to recite blessings, he should then eat in silence. / On this weekday conjoined with a solar eclipse, O destroyer of Tripura,

1.92.s:
yatkarma kriyate puṇyaṃ tatsarvaṃ śubhadaṃ bhavet .
snānadānajapādīnāṃ karmaṇāṃ govṛṣadhvaja . . 1.92.10
1.92.d:
यत्कर्म क्रियते पुण्यं तत्सर्वं शुभदं भवेत् ।
स्नानदानजपादीनां कर्मणां गोवृषध्वज ॥ 1.92.10
1.92.m: whatever meritorious deed is performed becomes all auspicious. / Of actions such as bathing, giving, and recitation, O bull-bannered one,

1.92.s:
anantaṃ hi phalaṃ teṣāṃ bhavatyasminna saṃśayaḥ .
kṛtānāṃ tu gaṇaśreṣṭhā bhāskarasya vaco yathā . . 11
1.92.d:
अनन्तं हि फलं तेषां भवत्यस्मिन्न संशयः ।
कृतानां तु गणश्रेष्ठा भास्करस्य वचो यथा ॥ 11
1.92.m: the fruit of those performed on this day becomes endless, there is no doubt, / according to the words of the Sun, O best of the ganas.

1.92.s:
tasmāddvijagaṇaiḥ kāryaṃ puṇyakarmavicakṣaṇaiḥ .
ekabhaktaṃ ca naktaṃ ca upavāsaṃ gaṇādhipa . . 12
1.92.d:
तस्माद्द्विजगणैः कार्यं पुण्यकर्मविचक्षणैः ।
एकभक्तं च नक्तं च उपवासं गणाधिप ॥ 12
1.92.m: Therefore, the multitudes of the twice-born skilled in meritorious deeds / should observe a single meal, a nocturnal meal, and fasting, O leader of the ganas.

1.92.s:
ye vādityadine kuryuste yānti paramaṃ padam .
dharmyaṃ puṇyaṃ yaśasyaṃ ca putrīyaṃ kāmadaṃ tathā . . 13
1.92.d:
ये वादित्यदिने कुर्युस्ते यान्ति परमं पदम् ।
धर्म्यं पुण्यं यशस्यं च पुत्रीयं कामदं तथा ॥ 13
1.92.m: Those who observe them on the Sun's day go to the supreme state; / it is righteous, meritorious, fame-yielding, brings sons, and bestows desires.

1.92.s:
tasmindānamapūpasya godānena samaṃ bhavet .
dvādaśaite mahābāho vīrabhānormahātmanaḥ . . 14
1.92.d:
तस्मिन्दानमपूपस्य गोदानेन समं भवेत् ।
द्वादशैते महाबाहो वीरभानोर्महात्मनः ॥ 14
1.92.m: On that day, the gift of a cake is equal to the gift of a cow. / These twelve [Sundays], O mighty-armed one, belonging to the heroic, great-souled Sun,

1.92.s:
tuṣṭidāḥ kathitāstubhyaṃ sarvapāpabhayāpahāḥ .
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ tāta kurvatāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ . . 15
1.92.d:
तुष्टिदाः कथितास्तुभ्यं सर्वपापभयापहाः ।
पठतां शृण्वतां तात कुर्वतां च विशेषतः ॥ 15
1.92.m: which bestow satisfaction, have been spoken to you, removing all sin and fear, / for those who read, hear, and especially perform them, O dear one.

1.92.s:
kṛtvaikameṣāṃ vidhivadvāraṃ vṛṣabhavāhana .
vṛṣāditritayaṃ prāpya cātrijāmacalāṃ tathā . . 16
1.92.d:
कृत्वैकमेषां विधिवद्वारं वृषभवाहन ।
वृषादित्रितयं प्राप्य चात्रिजामचलां तथा ॥ 16
1.92.m: Having performed even one of these weekdays according to the rules, O rider of the bull, / having attained the triad beginning with righteousness, and steady wealth,

1.92.s:
tato yāti paraṃ lokaṃ vṛṣaketo mahātmanaḥ .
tejasāmbujasaṃkāśaḥ prabhayāṇḍajasannibhaḥ . . 17
1.92.d:
ततो याति परं लोकं वृषकेतो महात्मनः ।
तेजसाम्बुजसंकाशः प्रभयाण्डजसन्निभः ॥ 17
1.92.m: he then goes to the supreme world of the great-souled one, O bull-bannered one, / resembling a lotus in brilliance and like the bird [Garuḍa] in splendour,
equal to the wielder of arrows in valour, and endowed with light like the moon.

1.92.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇyādityavārakalpe mahāśvetavāravidhivarṇanaṃ
nāma dvinavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 92 .
bhānumahimavarṇanam
1.92.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वण्यादित्यवारकल्पे महाश्वेतवारविधिवर्णनं
नाम द्विनवतितमोऽध्यायः । 92 ।
भानुमहिमवर्णनम्
1.92.m:
Thus ends the ninety-second chapter, entitled 'Description of the Rite of Mahāśvetāvāra', in the Ādityavārakalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Greatness of the Sun

1.93.s:
brahmovāca
yeṣāṃ dharmakriyāḥ sarvāḥ sadaivoddiśya bhāskaram .
na kule jāyate teṣāṃ daridro vyādhito'pi vā . . 1
1.93.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
येषां धर्मक्रियाः सर्वाः सदैवोद्दिश्य भास्करम् ।
न कुले जायते तेषां दरिद्रो व्याधितोऽपि वा ॥ 1
1.93.m:
Brahmā said:
In the family of those whose religious rites are always dedicated to the Sun, / no one is born poor or afflicted with disease.

1.93.s:
devāyatanabhūmestu gomayenopalepanam .
yaḥ karoti naro bhaktyā sadyaḥ pāpātpramucyate . . 2
1.93.d:
देवायतनभूमेस्तु गोमयेनोपलेपनम् ।
यः करोति नरो भक्त्या सद्यः पापात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ 2
1.93.m: A man who devoutly smears the floor of the deity's temple with cow dung / is immediately freed from sin.

1.93.s:
śvetayā raktayā vāpi pītamṛttikayāpi vā .
upalepanakartā vai cintitaṃ labhate phalam . . 3
1.93.d:
श्वेतया रक्तया वापि पीतमृत्तिकयापि वा ।
उपलेपनकर्ता वै चिन्तितं लभते फलम् ॥ 3
1.93.m: One who smears it with white, red, or yellow clay / indeed obtains his desired fruit.

1.93.s:
citrabhānuṃ virañcyaiva1 kusumairyaḥ sugandhibhiḥ .
pūjayetsopavāsastu sa kāmānīpsitām̐llabhet . . 4
1.93.d:
चित्रभानुं विरञ्च्यैव1 कुसुमैर्यः सुगन्धिभिः ।
पूजयेत्सोपवासस्तु स कामानीप्सिताम्̐ल्लभेत् ॥ 4
1.93.m: He who, fasting, worships the bright Sun with fragrant flowers, / having created them, obtains his wished-for desires.

1.93.s:
ghṛtena dīpakaṃ jvālya tilatailena vā raveḥ .
prayāti sūryalokaṃ sa dīpakoṭiśatairvṛtaḥ . . 5
1.93.d:
घृतेन दीपकं ज्वाल्य तिलतैलेन वा रवेः ।
प्रयाति सूर्यलोकं स दीपकोटिशतैर्वृतः ॥ 5
1.93.m: Having kindled a lamp with clarified butter or with sesame oil for the Sun, / he departs to the world of the Sun, surrounded by hundreds of millions of lamps.

1.93.s:
dīpatailapradānena na yāti narakaṃ naraḥ .
dīpatailaṃ tilāścaiva2 mahāpātakanāśanāḥ . . 6
1.93.d:
दीपतैलप्रदानेन न याति नरकं नरः ।
दीपतैलं तिलाश्चैव2 महापातकनाशनाः ॥ 6
1.93.m: By donating lamp-oil, a man does not go to hell; / lamp-oil and sesame seeds destroy the great sins.

1.93.s:
dīpaṃ dadāti yo nityaṃ bhāskarāyataneṣu3 vai .
catuṣpatheṣu tīrtheṣu rūpaujasvī ha jāyate . . 7
1.93.d:
दीपं ददाति यो नित्यं भास्करायतनेषु3 वै ।
चतुष्पथेषु तीर्थेषु रूपौजस्वी ह जायते ॥ 7
1.93.m: He who always gives a lamp in the temples of the Sun, / at crossroads, and at holy bathing places, is born beautiful and vigorous.

1.93.s:
yastu kārayate4 dīpaṃ raverbhaktisamanvitaḥ .
sa kāmānīpsitānprāpya vṛndārakapuraṃ vrajet . . 8
1.93.d:
यस्तु कारयते4 दीपं रवेर्भक्तिसमन्वितः ।
स कामानीप्सितान्प्राप्य वृन्दारकपुरं व्रजेत् ॥ 8
1.93.m: He who arranges a lamp for the Sun, endowed with devotion, / having attained his desired wishes, goes to the city of the gods.

1.93.s:
yaḥ samālabhate sūryaṃ candanāgurukuṅkumaiḥ .
karpūreṇa vimiśraiśca tathā kastūrikānvitaiḥ . . 9
1.93.d:
यः समालभते सूर्यं चन्दनागुरुकुङ्कुमैः ।
कर्पूरेण विमिश्रैश्च तथा कस्तूरिकान्वितैः ॥ 9
1.93.m: He who anoints the Sun with sandalwood, agallochum, and saffron / mixed with camphor, as well as accompanied with musk,

1.93.s:
śubhaṃ kālaṃ koṭiśataṃ vihṛtya5 ca bhavālaye .
punaḥ sañjāyate bhūmau rājarājo na saṃśayaḥ . .
sarvakāmasamṛddhātmā sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ . . 1.93.10
1.93.d:
शुभं कालं कोटिशतं विहृत्य5 च भवालये ।
पुनः सञ्जायते भूमौ राजराजो न संशयः ॥
सर्वकामसमृद्धात्मा सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः ॥ 1.93.10
1.93.m: having sported for a hundred million auspicious eras in the abode of Śiva, / is born again on earth as a king of kings, without a doubt, / his mind fulfilled in every desire, bowed to by all the worlds.

1.93.s:
candanodakamiśraiśca dattvārghyaṃ kusumai raveḥ .
saputrapautrapatnīkaḥ svargaloke mahīyate6 . . 11
1.93.d:
चन्दनोदकमिश्रैश्च दत्त्वार्घ्यं कुसुमै रवेः ।
सपुत्रपौत्रपत्नीकः स्वर्गलोके महीयते6 ॥ 11
1.93.m: Having offered water oblations to the Sun mixed with sandalwood water and flowers, / he is honoured in the heavenly world together with his sons, grandsons, and wife.

1.93.s:
sugandhodakamiśraistu dattvārghyaṃ kusumai raveḥ .
devaloke ciraṃ sthitvā rājā bhavati bhūtale . . 12
1.93.d:
सुगन्धोदकमिश्रैस्तु दत्त्वार्घ्यं कुसुमै रवेः ।
देवलोके चिरं स्थित्वा राजा भवति भूतले ॥ 12
1.93.m: Having offered water oblations to the Sun with flowers mixed with fragrant water, / having dwelt for a long time in the world of the gods, he becomes a king on earth.

1.93.s:
sa hiraṇyena cārgheṇa raktodakayutena vā .
koṭīśataṃ tu varṣāṇāṃ svargaloke mahīyate . . 13
1.93.d:
स हिरण्येन चार्घेण रक्तोदकयुतेन वा ।
कोटीशतं तु वर्षाणां स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥ 13
1.93.m: And with an arghya offering of gold or mixed with red water, / he is honoured in the heavenly realm for a hundred crore years.

1.93.s:
padmairabhyarcanaṃ kṛtvā raveḥ svargagato naraḥ .
padme vasati varṣāṇāṃ strīpadmaśatasaṃvṛtaḥ . . 14
1.93.d:
पद्मैरभ्यर्चनं कृत्वा रवेः स्वर्गगतो नरः ।
पद्मे वसति वर्षाणां स्त्रीपद्मशतसंवृतः ॥ 14
1.93.m: Having worshipped the Sun with lotuses, a man goes to heaven / and dwells in the Lotus [realm] for years, surrounded by a hundred lotus-like women.

1.93.s:
guggulaṃ saghṛtaṃ dattvā raverbhaktisamanvitaḥ 1 .
tatkṣaṇātsarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 15
1.93.d:
गुग्गुलं सघृतं दत्त्वा रवेर्भक्तिसमन्वितः 1 ।
तत्क्षणात्सर्वपापेभ्यो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥ 15
1.93.m: Offering guggulu mixed with ghee to the Sun with devotion, / he is freed instantly from all sins; there is no doubt about this.

1.93.s:
pakṣaṃ tu guggulaṃ dattvā mucyate brahmahatyayā .
saṃvatsareṇa labhate aśvamedhaphalaṃ śiva . . 16
1.93.d:
पक्षं तु गुग्गुलं दत्त्वा मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया ।
संवत्सरेण लभते अश्वमेधफलं शिव ॥ 16
1.93.m: Offering guggulu for a fortnight, he is freed from the murder of a brahmin; / in a year, O Śiva, he obtains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice.

1.93.s:
dhūpena labhate svargaṃ turuṣkeṇa sugandhinā .
karpūrāgurudhūpena rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet . . 17
1.93.d:
धूपेन लभते स्वर्गं तुरुष्केण सुगन्धिना ।
कर्पूरागुरुधूपेन राजसूयफलं लभेत् ॥ 17
1.93.m: Through fragrant turuṣka incense, he attains heaven; / through camphor and aguru incense, he obtains the fruit of a rājasūya sacrifice.

1.93.s:
pūrvāhṇe mānavo bhaktyā śraddhayā yo'rcayedravim .
sa tatphalamavāpnoti yaddatte kapilāśate . . 18
1.93.d:
पूर्वाह्णे मानवो भक्त्या श्रद्धया योऽर्चयेद्रविम् ।
स तत्फलमवाप्नोति यद्दत्ते कपिलाशते ॥ 18
1.93.m: The man who worships the Sun in the morning with devotion and faith / obtains that reward which [arises] when a hundred brown cows are given.

1.93.s:
madhyāhne yo'rcayetsūryaṃ prayatātmā jitendriyaḥ .
labhate bhūmidānasya gośatasya ca tatphalam . . 19
1.93.d:
मध्याह्ने योऽर्चयेत्सूर्यं प्रयतात्मा जितेन्द्रियः ।
लभते भूमिदानस्य गोशतस्य च तत्फलम् ॥ 19
1.93.m: He who, disciplined in mind and with senses conquered, worships the Sun at midday, / obtains the reward of a gift of land and of a hundred cows.

1.93.s:
paścimāyāṃ tu sandhyāyāṃ yo'rcayedbhāskaraṃ naraḥ .
śuciḥ śuklāmbaroṣṇīṣo gosahasraphalaṃ labhet . . 1.93.20
1.93.d:
पश्चिमायां तु सन्ध्यायां योऽर्चयेद्भास्करं नरः ।
शुचिः शुक्लाम्बरोष्णीषो गोसहस्रफलं लभेत् ॥ 1.93.20
1.93.m: The man who worships the Sun at the western twilight, / pure, dressed in white garments with a turban, obtains the reward of a thousand cows.

1.93.s:
ardharātre tu yo heliṃ bhaktyā sampūjayennaraḥ .
jātismaratvamāpnoti kule jāto vṛṣānvitaḥ . . 21
1.93.d:
अर्धरात्रे तु यो हेलिं भक्त्या सम्पूजयेन्नरः ।
जातिस्मरत्वमाप्नोति कुले जातो वृषान्वितः ॥ 21
1.93.m: The man who with devotion worships Heli at midnight / attains the recollection of past lives, born in a [noble] family and endowed with virtue.

1.93.s:
pradoṣarātrivelāyāṃ yaḥ pūjayati bhāskaram .
sa gatvā sahasā vīra krīḍetsaumanasaṃ2 kṣayam . . 22
1.93.d:
प्रदोषरात्रिवेलायां यः पूजयति भास्करम् ।
स गत्वा सहसा वीर क्रीडेत्सौमनसं2 क्षयम् ॥ 22
1.93.m: He who worships the Sun at the evening twilight hour of night, / he, having gone quickly, O hero, sports in the Saumanasa realm.

1.93.s:
daṇḍanāyakavelāyāṃ prabhātasamaye punaḥ .
pūjayitvā raviṃ bhaktyā vrajedanimiṣālayam . . 23
1.93.d:
दण्डनायकवेलायां प्रभातसमये पुनः ।
पूजयित्वा रविं भक्त्या व्रजेदनिमिषालयम् ॥ 23
1.93.m: Again, at dawn, during the hour of the Daṇḍanāyaka, / having worshipped the Sun with devotion, he goes to the abode of the gods.

1.93.s:
evaṃ velāsu sarvāsu avelāsu ca mānavaḥ .
bhaktyā pūjayate yo'rkamarkapuṣpaiḥ samāhitaḥ . .
tejasādityasaṃkāśo hyarkaloke mahīyate . . 24
1.93.d:
एवं वेलासु सर्वासु अवेलासु च मानवः ।
भक्त्या पूजयते योऽर्कमर्कपुष्पैः समाहितः ॥
तेजसादित्यसंकाशो ह्यर्कलोके महीयते ॥ 24
1.93.m: In this way, during all proper hours and improper hours, the man / who, composed, worships Arka with devotion using arka flowers, / equal in radiance to the Sun, is honoured in the realm of Arka.

1.93.s:
ayane tūttare sūryamatha vā dakṣiṇāyane .
pūjayedyastu vai bhaktyā sa gacchetkañjajālayam . . 25
1.93.d:
अयने तूत्तरे सूर्यमथ वा दक्षिणायने ।
पूजयेद्यस्तु वै भक्त्या स गच्छेत्कञ्जजालयम् ॥ 25
1.93.m: And he who worships the Sun with devotion during the northern solstice / or during the southern solstice goes to the abode of Brahmā.

1.93.s:
tatrasthaḥ pūjyate keśaiḥ1 sarveḥ sumanasastathā .
gopatiḥ pūjyate yadvadgopatipramukhaiḥ suraiḥ . . 26
1.93.d:
तत्रस्थः पूज्यते केशैः1 सर्वेः सुमनसस्तथा ।
गोपतिः पूज्यते यद्वद्गोपतिप्रमुखैः सुरैः ॥ 26
1.93.m: Dwelling there, he is worshipped by all the gods and the wise, / just as Indra is worshipped by the gods headed by Indra.

1.93.s:
viṣuveṣūparāgeṣu ṣaḍaśītimukheṣu ca .
pūjayitvā raviṃ bhaktyā nātmānaṃ śocate naraḥ . . 27
1.93.d:
विषुवेषूपरागेषु षडशीतिमुखेषु च ।
पूजयित्वा रविं भक्त्या नात्मानं शोचते नरः ॥ 27
1.93.m: Having worshipped the Sun with devotion at the equinoxes, eclipses, / and the beginnings of the eighty-six divisions, a man does not grieve for himself.

1.93.s:
vibudhya2 vā svayaṃ vāpi yo namaskurute ravim .
santuṣṭo bhāskarastasmai gatimiṣṭāṃ prayacchati . . 28
1.93.d:
विबुध्य2 वा स्वयं वापि यो नमस्कुरुते रविम् ।
सन्तुष्टो भास्करस्तस्मै गतिमिष्टां प्रयच्छति ॥ 28
1.93.m: He who bows down to the Sun, whether upon waking or on his own, / to him the pleased Sun grants his desired destination.

1.93.s:
kṛśarāpāyasāpūpapalalonmiśramodakaiḥ .
baliṃ kṛtvā tu sūryāya sarvakāmamavāpnuyāt . . 29
1.93.d:
कृशरापायसापूपपललोन्मिश्रमोदकैः ।
बलिं कृत्वा तु सूर्याय सर्वकाममवाप्नुयात् ॥ 29
1.93.m: Having made an offering to the Sun of kṛśarā, milk-rice, rice-cakes, / and modakas mixed with sesamum paste, he attains all desires.

1.93.s:
modakānāṃ pradānena3 pāyasasya ca suvrata .
madhumāṃsarasaiścāpi prīyate'tīvabhāskaraḥ . . 1.93.30
1.93.d:
मोदकानां प्रदानेन3 पायसस्य च सुव्रत ।
मधुमांसरसैश्चापि प्रीयतेऽतीवभास्करः ॥ 1.93.30
1.93.m: By the offering of modakas and milk-rice, O observer of auspicious vows, / and also with honey, meat, and juices, the Sun is exceedingly pleased.

1.93.s:
ghṛtena tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā sadā snigdho bhavennaraḥ .
tarpayitvā tu māṃsena sadyaḥ pāpātpramucyate . . 31
1.93.d:
घृतेन तर्पणं कृत्वा सदा स्निग्धो भवेन्नरः ।
तर्पयित्वा तु मांसेन सद्यः पापात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ 31
1.93.m: Having performed a libation with ghee, a man is always nourished; / having satisfied [him] with meat, he is instantly freed from sin.

1.93.s:
ghṛtena snapanaṃ kṛtvā ekāhamudaye raveḥ .
gavāṃ śatasahasrasya dattasya phalamaśnute . . 32
1.93.d:
घृतेन स्नपनं कृत्वा एकाहमुदये रवेः ।
गवां शतसहस्रस्य दत्तस्य फलमश्नुते ॥ 32
1.93.m: Having performed bathing [of the deity] with ghee for one day at the rising of the Sun, / he enjoys the fruit of a hundred thousand cows given away.

1.93.s:
gavāṃ kṣīreṇa santarpya puṇḍarīkaphalaṃ labhet .
rasena snāpayeddevamaśvamedhaphalaṃ 5 labhet . . 33
1.93.d:
गवां क्षीरेण सन्तर्प्य पुण्डरीकफलं लभेत् ।
रसेन स्नापयेद्देवमश्वमेधफलं 5 लभेत् ॥ 33
1.93.m: Having satisfied [him] with cow's milk, he obtains the reward of a Puṇḍarīka sacrifice; / if he bathes the god with juice, he obtains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice.

1.93.s:
sūryāya taruṇīṃ dhenuṃ gāmekāṃ yaḥ prayacchati .
kañjajāmacalāṃ prāpya punarlekhapuraṃ vrajet . . 34
1.93.d:
सूर्याय तरुणीं धेनुं गामेकां यः प्रयच्छति ।
कञ्जजामचलां प्राप्य पुनर्लेखपुरं व्रजेत् ॥ 34
1.93.m: He who offers a single young milch cow to the Sun, / having attained the immovable [abode] of Brahmā, goes again to the city of the gods.

1.93.s:
gośarīre tu romāṇi yāvanti tripurāntaka .
sa tāvadvarṣakoṭīstu lekhaloke mahīyate . . 35
1.93.d:
गोशरीरे तु रोमाणि यावन्ति त्रिपुरान्तक ।
स तावद्वर्षकोटीस्तु लेखलोके महीयते ॥ 35
1.93.m: As many hairs as there are on the cow's body, O Destroyer of Tripura, / for so many crores of years is he honoured in the world of the gods.

1.93.s:
gośataṃ bhānave dattvā rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet .
aśvamedhaphalaṃ tasya yaḥ sahasraṃ prayacchati . . 36
1.93.d:
गोशतं भानवे दत्त्वा राजसूयफलं लभेत् ।
अश्वमेधफलं तस्य यः सहस्रं प्रयच्छति ॥ 36
1.93.m: Giving a hundred cows to the Sun, he obtains the fruit of a rājasūya sacrifice; / the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice belongs to him who gives a thousand.

1.93.s:
guggulaṃ devadāruṃ ca dahennityaṃ ghṛtasravam .
ājyadhūmo6 hi devānāṃ prakṛtyaiva priyaḥ sadā . . 37
1.93.d:
गुग्गुलं देवदारुं च दहेन्नित्यं घृतस्रवम् ।
आज्यधूमो6 हि देवानां प्रकृत्यैव प्रियः सदा ॥ 37
1.93.m: One should daily burn guggulu and deodar cedar dripping with ghee; / for the smoke of clarified butter is always dear to the gods by their very nature.

1.93.s:
bheryādīni ca vādyāni śaṅkhaveṇvādikāni ca .
ye prayacchanti sūryāya yānti te haṃsamandiram . . 38
1.93.d:
भेर्यादीनि च वाद्यानि शङ्खवेण्वादिकानि च ।
ये प्रयच्छन्ति सूर्याय यान्ति ते हंसमन्दिरम् ॥ 38
1.93.m: Those who offer musical instruments such as kettle-drums, conches, flutes, and the like / to the Sun go to the abode of the Sun.

1.93.s:
vajramāharate yastu raverbhaktisamanvitaḥ .
tīrthodakamathaivānyaḥ sa yāti vibudhālayam . . 39
1.93.d:
वज्रमाहरते यस्तु रवेर्भक्तिसमन्वितः ।
तीर्थोदकमथैवान्यः स याति विबुधालयम् ॥ 39
1.93.m: He who brings a diamond to the Sun with devotion, / or another [who brings] water from a sacred ford, goes to the abode of the gods.

1.93.s:
vimānaiḥ strīśatākīrṇaiḥ krīḍayitvā ciraṃ naraḥ .
mānuṣatvamanuprāpya rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ . .1.93.4 0
chatraṃ dhvajaṃ vitānaṃ ca patākāścāmarāṇi ca .
hemadaṇḍāni vai dadyādraveryo bhaktimānnaraḥ . . 41
1.93.d:
विमानैः स्त्रीशताकीर्णैः क्रीडयित्वा चिरं नरः ।
मानुषत्वमनुप्राप्य राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥1.93.4 0
छत्रं ध्वजं वितानं च पताकाश्चामराणि च ।
हेमदण्डानि वै दद्याद्रवेर्यो भक्तिमान्नरः ॥ 41
1.93.m: Having sported for a long time in celestial chariots filled with hundreds of women, / the man, attaining human birth, becomes a righteous king. / The devoted man who offers to the Sun a royal parasol, a banner, a canopy, / pennants, chowries, and golden staffs,

1.93.s:
vimānena sa divyena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā .
sūryalokamato gatvā bhavatyapsarasāṃ patiḥ . . 42
1.93.d:
विमानेन स दिव्येन किङ्किणीजालमालिना ।
सूर्यलोकमतो गत्वा भवत्यप्सरसां पतिः ॥ 42
1.93.m: he, having gone thence to the world of the Sun in a divine celestial chariot / adorned with garlands of rows of small bells, becomes the lord of apsarases.

1.93.s:
tatroṣya suciraṃ kālaṃ svargātpratyāgataḥ punaḥ .
mānuṣye jāyate rājā sarvarājanamaskṛtaḥ . . 43
1.93.d:
तत्रोष्य सुचिरं कालं स्वर्गात्प्रत्यागतः पुनः ।
मानुष्ये जायते राजा सर्वराजनमस्कृतः ॥ 43
1.93.m: Having dwelt there for a very long time, returned again from heaven, / he is born among humans as a king reverenced by all kings.

1.93.s:
dattvā vāsāṃsi sūryāya alaṅkārāṃstathaiva ca .
krīḍate janalokastho yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam . . 44
1.93.d:
दत्त्वा वासांसि सूर्याय अलङ्कारांस्तथैव च ।
क्रीडते जनलोकस्थो यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् ॥ 44
1.93.m: Having given garments to the Sun and ornaments as well, / dwelling in Janaloka he sports until the dissolution of all beings.

1.93.s:
gītavāditranṛtyaiśca kuryājjāgaraṇaṃ raveḥ .
gandharvāpsarasāṃ madhye krīḍate suciraṃ naraḥ . . 45
1.93.d:
गीतवादित्रनृत्यैश्च कुर्याज्जागरणं रवेः ।
गन्धर्वाप्सरसां मध्ये क्रीडते सुचिरं नरः ॥ 45
1.93.m: One should keep a vigil for the Sun with songs, instruments, and dances; / the man sports for a very long time among gandharvas and apsarases.

1.93.s:
gandhaiḥ puṣpaistathā patraiḥ stotrairvā vividhaistathā .
ye stuvanti raviṃ bhaktyā te yānti patagālayam . . 46
1.93.d:
गन्धैः पुष्पैस्तथा पत्रैः स्तोत्रैर्वा विविधैस्तथा ।
ये स्तुवन्ति रविं भक्त्या ते यान्ति पतगालयम् ॥ 46
1.93.m: Those who praise the Sun with devotion, with perfumes, flowers, and leaves, / or with various hymns of praise, go to the abode of the Bird.

1.93.s:
uṣaḥ stuvanti ye sūryamupagāyanti te sadā .
pāṭhakāścāraṇāścaiva sarve te svargagāminaḥ . . 47
1.93.d:
उषः स्तुवन्ति ये सूर्यमुपगायन्ति ते सदा ।
पाठकाश्चारणाश्चैव सर्वे ते स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 47
1.93.m: Those who praise the Sun at dawn, who always sing his praise, / the reciters and the bards, all of them go to heaven.

1.93.s:
aśvayuktaṃ yugairyuktaṃ yo dadyādravaye ratham.
kāñcanaṃ vāpi raupyaṃ vā maṇiratnānvitaṃ śubham . . 48
1.93.d:
अश्वयुक्तं युगैर्युक्तं यो दद्याद्रवये रथम्।
काञ्चनं वापि रौप्यं वा मणिरत्नान्वितं शुभम् ॥ 48
1.93.m: He who gives to the Sun an auspicious chariot yoked with horses and equipped with yokes, / whether made of gold or silver, endowed with gems and jewels,

1.93.s:
sa yānenārkavarṇena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā .
svargalokamito gatvā krīḍate'psarasā saha .4 9
yastu dārumayaṃ kuryādrave rathamanuttamam .
sa yātyarkasavarṇena1 vimānenārkamaṇḍalam . . 1.93.50
1.93.d:
स यानेनार्कवर्णेन किङ्किणीजालमालिना ।
स्वर्गलोकमितो गत्वा क्रीडतेऽप्सरसा सह .4 9
यस्तु दारुमयं कुर्याद्रवे रथमनुत्तमम् ।
स यात्यर्कसवर्णेन1 विमानेनार्कमण्डलम् ॥ 1.93.50
1.93.m: he, having gone from here to the heavenly realm in a vehicle the colour of the Sun, / adorned with garlands of rows of small bells, sports with an apsaras. / But he who makes an unsurpassed wooden chariot for the Sun / goes to the solar orb in a celestial chariot of the same colour as the Sun.

1.93.s:
yātrāṃ kurvanti ye bhānornarāḥ saṃvatsarādapi .
ṣaṇmāsādvā gaṇaśreṣṭha teṣāṃ puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu . . 51
1.93.d:
यात्रां कुर्वन्ति ये भानोर्नराः संवत्सरादपि ।
षण्मासाद्वा गणश्रेष्ठ तेषां पुण्यफलं शृणु ॥ 51
1.93.m: Hear the meritorious reward of those men who perform a procession for the Sun / even after a year or after six months, O best of the gaṇas.

1.93.s:
dhyānino yoginaścaiva prāpnuvantīha yāṃ gatim .
tāṃ gatiṃ pratipadyante sūryavartmāvagāhinaḥ . . 52
1.93.d:
ध्यानिनो योगिनश्चैव प्राप्नुवन्तीह यां गतिम् ।
तां गतिं प्रतिपद्यन्ते सूर्यवर्त्मावगाहिनः ॥ 52
1.93.m: Whatever state of being the meditators and yogins attain in this world, / that very state of being those who enter upon the path of the Sun attain.

1.93.s:
rathaṃ vahanti ye bhānornarā bhaktisamanvitāḥ .
arogāścādaridrāśca jātau jātau bhavanti te . . 53
1.93.d:
रथं वहन्ति ये भानोर्नरा भक्तिसमन्विताः ।
अरोगाश्चादरिद्राश्च जातौ जातौ भवन्ति ते ॥ 53
1.93.m: Those men endowed with devotion who pull the chariot of the Sun / become free from disease and free from poverty in birth after birth.

1.93.s:
kartāro rathayātrāyā ye narā bhāskarasya tu .
te bhānulokamāsādya viharanti yathāsukham . . 54
1.93.d:
कर्तारो रथयात्राया ये नरा भास्करस्य तु ।
ते भानुलोकमासाद्य विहरन्ति यथासुखम् ॥ 54
1.93.m: Those men who are the organizers of the chariot procession of the Sun, / having reached the world of the Sun, amuse themselves at pleasure.

1.93.s:
yātrābhaṅgaṃ tu yo mohātkrodhādvā kurute naraḥ .
mandehāste narā jñeyā rākṣasāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ . . 55
1.93.d:
यात्राभङ्गं तु यो मोहात्क्रोधाद्वा कुरुते नरः ।
मन्देहास्ते नरा ज्ञेया राक्षसाः पापकारिणः ॥ 55
1.93.m: The man who, out of delusion or anger, causes the disruption of the procession, / such men should be known as Mandēhas, sin-performing rākṣasas.

1.93.s:
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ hiraṇyaṃ vā vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca .
ye prayacchanti sūryāya te yānti paramāṃ gatim . . 56
1.93.d:
धनं धान्यं हिरण्यं वा वासांसि विविधानि च ।
ये प्रयच्छन्ति सूर्याय ते यान्ति परमां गतिम् ॥ 56
1.93.m: Those who offer wealth, grain, gold, or various garments / to the Sun go to the supreme state.

1.93.s:
gā vātha mahiṣīrvāpi gajānaśvāṃśca śobhanān .
ya prayacchati sūryāya tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu . . 57
1.93.d:
गा वाथ महिषीर्वापि गजानश्वांश्च शोभनान् ।
य प्रयच्छति सूर्याय तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु ॥ 57
1.93.m: He who offers cows, female buffaloes, elephants, and handsome horses / to the Sun—hear his meritorious reward:

1.93.s:
akṣayaṃ sarvakāmīyamaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .
sahasraguṇitaṃ tacca dānamasyopatiṣṭhati . . 58
1.93.d:
अक्षयं सर्वकामीयमश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ।
सहस्रगुणितं तच्च दानमस्योपतिष्ठति ॥ 58
1.93.m: he obtains the inexhaustible fruit of a horse sacrifice that fulfills all desires, / and that gift accrues to him multiplied a thousandfold.

1.93.s:
mahīṃ dadāti yo'rkāya kṛṣṭāṃ phalavatī śubhām .
sa tārayati vai vaṃśyāndaśa pūrvāndaśāparān . . 59
1.93.d:
महीं ददाति योऽर्काय कृष्टां फलवती शुभाम् ।
स तारयति वै वंश्यान्दश पूर्वान्दशापरान् ॥ 59
1.93.m: Whoever gives to the sun cultivated, fruitful, auspicious land / delivers indeed ten ancestors and ten descendants of his lineage.

1.93.s:
vimānena ca divyena gopuraṃ gopatervrajet .
krīḍatyapsarasāṃ madhye karīva kariṇīgaṇe . . 1.93.60
1.93.d:
विमानेन च दिव्येन गोपुरं गोपतेर्व्रजेत् ।
क्रीडत्यप्सरसां मध्ये करीव करिणीगणे ॥ 1.93.60
1.93.m: And by means of a divine celestial chariot he goes to the city of the lord of rays; / he disports in the midst of Apsarases, like an elephant in a herd of female elephants.

1.93.s:
grāmaṃ dadāti yo bhaktyā sūryāya matimānnaraḥ1 .
vimānenārkavarṇena sa yāti paramāṃ gatim . . 61
1.93.d:
ग्रामं ददाति यो भक्त्या सूर्याय मतिमान्नरः1 ।
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ 61
1.93.m: A wise man who gives a village with devotion to the sun / goes to the supreme state in a celestial chariot possessing the splendour of the sun.

1.93.s:
ārāmānye prayacchanti patrapuṣpaphalopagān .
bhānave bhaktiyuktāstu te yānti paramāṃ gatim . . 62
1.93.d:
आरामान्ये प्रयच्छन्ति पत्रपुष्पफलोपगान् ।
भानवे भक्तियुक्तास्तु ते यान्ति परमां गतिम् ॥ 62
1.93.m: Those who, full of devotion, bestow upon the sun / pleasure groves endowed with leaves, flowers, and fruits, go to the supreme state.

1.93.s:
mānasaṃ vācikaṃ vāpi karmajaṃ yacca duṣkṛtam .
sarvaṃ sūryaprasādena aśeṣaṃ ca praṇaśyati . . 63
1.93.d:
मानसं वाचिकं वापि कर्मजं यच्च दुष्कृतम् ।
सर्वं सूर्यप्रसादेन अशेषं च प्रणश्यति ॥ 63
1.93.m: Whatever evil deed was born of mind, speech, or physical action, / all of it, without remainder, is destroyed by the sun's grace.

1.93.s:
ārto vā vyādhito vāpi daridro duḥkhito'pi vā .
ādityaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatvā nātmānaṃ śocate naraḥ . . 64
1.93.d:
आर्तो वा व्याधितो वापि दरिद्रो दुःखितोऽपि वा ।
आदित्यं शरणं गत्वा नात्मानं शोचते नरः ॥ 64
1.93.m: Whether distressed, diseased, impoverished, or sorrowful, / a man who takes refuge in the sun does not grieve for himself.

1.93.s:
ekāhenāpi yadbhānoḥ pūjāyāḥ prāpyate phalam .
tadvai kratuśatairiṣṭaiḥ prāpyate phalamuttamam . . 65
1.93.d:
एकाहेनापि यद्भानोः पूजायाः प्राप्यते फलम् ।
तद्वै क्रतुशतैरिष्टैः प्राप्यते फलमुत्तमम् ॥ 65
1.93.m: The fruit obtained even by a single day's worship of the sun / is indeed the supreme fruit obtained by performing hundreds of sacrifices.

1.93.s:
kṛtvā prekṣaṇakaṃ bhānordivyamāyatane śubham .
akṣayaṃ sarvakāmīyaṃ rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet . . 66
1.93.d:
कृत्वा प्रेक्षणकं भानोर्दिव्यमायतने शुभम् ।
अक्षयं सर्वकामीयं राजसूयफलं लभेत् ॥ 66
1.93.m: Having arranged a delightful, divine dramatic spectacle for the sun in his sanctuary, / one obtains the inexhaustible fruit of a rājasūya sacrifice, fulfilling all desires.

1.93.s:
veśyākadambakaṃ yastu dadyātsūryāya bhaktitaḥ .
sa gacchetparamaṃ sthānaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati bhānumān . . 67
1.93.d:
वेश्याकदम्बकं यस्तु दद्यात्सूर्याय भक्तितः ।
स गच्छेत्परमं स्थानं यत्र तिष्ठति भानुमान् ॥ 67
1.93.m: Moreover, he who devotedly gives a troop of courtesans to the sun / shall go to the supreme abode where the radiant sun resides.

1.93.s:
pustakaṃ bhānave dadyādbhāratasya gaṇādhipa .
sarvapāpavimuktātmā viṣṇuloke mahīyate . . 68
1.93.d:
पुस्तकं भानवे दद्याद्भारतस्य गणाधिप ।
सर्वपापविमुक्तात्मा विष्णुलोके महीयते ॥ 68
1.93.m: One should give a manuscript of the Mahābhārata to the sun, O leader of the gaṇas; / with his soul liberated from all sins, he is honoured in the world of Viṣṇu.

1.93.s:
rāmāyaṇasya datvā tu pustakaṃ tripurāntaka .
vājapeyaphalaṃ prāpya gopateḥ puramāvrajet . . 69
1.93.d:
रामायणस्य दत्वा तु पुस्तकं त्रिपुरान्तक ।
वाजपेयफलं प्राप्य गोपतेः पुरमाव्रजेत् ॥ 69
1.93.m: Having given a manuscript of the Rāmāyaṇa, O destroyer of Tripura, / and obtained the fruit of a vājapeya sacrifice, he goes to the city of the lord of rays.

1.93.s:
bhaviṣyaṃ sāmbasaṃjñaṃ vā dattvā sūryāya pustakam .
rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ . .1.93.7 0
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti yāti sūryasalokatām .
sūryaloke ciraṃ sthitvā brahmalokaṃ vrajetpunaḥ . .
sthitvā kalpaśataṃ tatra rājā bhavati bhūtale . . 71
1.93.d:
भविष्यं साम्बसंज्ञं वा दत्त्वा सूर्याय पुस्तकम् ।
राजसूयाश्वमेधाभ्यां फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥1.93.7 0
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति याति सूर्यसलोकताम् ।
सूर्यलोके चिरं स्थित्वा ब्रह्मलोकं व्रजेत्पुनः ॥
स्थित्वा कल्पशतं तत्र राजा भवति भूतले ॥ 71
1.93.m: Having given to the sun a manuscript of the Bhaviṣya or the Sāmba, / a mortal obtains the fruit of a rājasūya and a horse sacrifice. / He attains all desires and goes to the same world as the sun. / Having dwelt for a long time in the world of the sun, he goes once more to the world of Brahmā; / after remaining there for a hundred kalpas, he becomes a king on the face of the earth.

1.93.s:
bhānorāyatane yastu prapāṃ kuryādgaṇādhipa .
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ divyaṃ saumanasaṃ naraḥ . . 72
1.93.d:
भानोरायतने यस्तु प्रपां कुर्याद्गणाधिप ।
स याति परमं स्थानं दिव्यं सौमनसं नरः ॥ 72
1.93.m: A man who sets up a public water stall in the sanctuary of the sun, O leader of the gaṇas, / goes to the supreme, divine abode of Saumanasa.

1.93.s:
śītakāle ghanaṃ dadyānnarāṇāṃ śītanāśanam .
bhānorāyatane deva aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet . . 73
1.93.d:
शीतकाले घनं दद्यान्नराणां शीतनाशनम् ।
भानोरायतने देव अश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥ 73
1.93.m: In the cold season, one should give dense [clothing] to men to dispel the cold; / in the sanctuary of the sun, O lord, he obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

1.93.s:
itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ puṇyaṃ pustakavācanam .
aśvamedhasahasraṃ yo nityaṃ kartuṃ pravartate . .
na tatphalamavāpnoti yadāpnotyasya karmaṇaḥ . . 74
1.93.d:
इतिहासपुराणाभ्यां पुण्यं पुस्तकवाचनम् ।
अश्वमेधसहस्रं यो नित्यं कर्तुं प्रवर्तते ॥
न तत्फलमवाप्नोति यदाप्नोत्यस्य कर्मणः ॥ 74
1.93.m: Recitation from manuscripts of the Itihāsas and Purāṇas is meritorious. / Even one who constantly undertakes to perform a thousand horse sacrifices / does not obtain the fruit that one obtains from this deed.

1.93.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena kāryaṃ pustakavācanam .
itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ bhānorāyatane śubham . . 75
1.93.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन कार्यं पुस्तकवाचनम् ।
इतिहासपुराणाभ्यां भानोरायतने शुभम् ॥ 75
1.93.m: Therefore, with every effort, auspicious recitation from manuscripts / of the Itihāsas and Purāṇas should be performed in the sanctuary of the sun.

1.93.s:
nānyatpuṣṭikaraṃ bhānostathā tuṣṭikaraṃ param .
puṇyākhyānakathā yāstu yathā tuṣyati bhāskaraḥ . . 76
1.93.d:
नान्यत्पुष्टिकरं भानोस्तथा तुष्टिकरं परम् ।
पुण्याख्यानकथा यास्तु यथा तुष्यति भास्करः ॥ 76
1.93.m: There is nothing else that nourishes the sun and pleases him supreme / like the narrations of sacred legends, through which the sun is pleased.

1.93.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamī kalpe bhānumahimavarṇanaṃ
nāma trinavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 93 .
puṇyaśravaṇamāhātmyavarṇanam
1.93.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमी कल्पे भानुमहिमवर्णनं
नाम त्रिनवतितमोऽध्यायः । 93 ।
पुण्यश्रवणमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्
1.93.m:
Thus ends the ninety-third chapter, entitled "Description of the Greatness of the Sun", in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Greatness of Hearing Sacred [Texts]

1.94.s:
brahmovāca
atrākhyānamuśantīha saṃvādaṃ gaṇapuṅgava .
pitāmahakumārābhyāṃ puṇyaṃ pāpaharaṃ śivam . . 1
1.94.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
अत्राख्यानमुशन्तीह संवादं गणपुङ्गव ।
पितामहकुमाराभ्यां पुण्यं पापहरं शिवम् ॥ 1
1.94.m: Brahmā said: / In this regard, they recount this narrative, a dialogue, O bull among the gaṇas, / between the Grandfather and Kumāra, which is meritorious, dispels sins, and is auspicious.

1.94.s:
sraṣṭāraṃ sarvalokānāṃ sukhāsīnaṃ pitāmaham .
praṇamya śirasā devaṃ śraddhābhaktisamanvitaḥ . . 2
1.94.d:
स्रष्टारं सर्वलोकानां सुखासीनं पितामहम् ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं श्रद्धाभक्तिसमन्वितः ॥ 2
1.94.m: Having bowed with his head to the Grandfather, the creator of all the worlds, / who was seated at ease, the god, endowed with faith and devotion,

1.94.s:
kumāro devaśārdūla idaṃ vacanamabravīt .
gato'hamadya bhagavandraṣṭuṃ devaṃ divākaram . . 3
1.94.d:
कुमारो देवशार्दूल इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
गतोऽहमद्य भगवन्द्रष्टुं देवं दिवाकरम् ॥ 3
1.94.m: Kumāra, O tiger among the gods, spoke this word: / "Today, O Blessed One, I went to see the god who makes the day.

1.94.s:
kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ devaḥ sa mayā pūjito raviḥ .
praṇamya śirasā bhaktyā parayā śraddhayā vibho . . 4
1.94.d:
कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं देवः स मया पूजितो रविः ।
प्रणम्य शिरसा भक्त्या परया श्रद्धया विभो ॥ 4
1.94.m: Having circumambulated him, that god Ravi was worshipped by me; / having bowed with my head with highest faith and devotion, O omnipresent one,

1.94.s:
anujñātastatastena sukhāsīno hyahaṃ sthitaḥ .
āsīnena mayā tatra dṛṣṭamāścaryamadbhutam . . 5
1.94.d:
अनुज्ञातस्ततस्तेन सुखासीनो ह्यहं स्थितः ।
आसीनेन मया तत्र दृष्टमाश्चर्यमद्भुतम् ॥ 5
1.94.m: I then sat at ease, permitted by him. / While seated there, a wonderful marvel was seen by me.

1.94.s:
kāñcanena vimānena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā .
maṇimuktāvicitreṇa vaidūryavaravedinā . . 6
1.94.d:
काञ्चनेन विमानेन किङ्किणीजालमालिना ।
मणिमुक्ताविचित्रेण वैदूर्यवरवेदिना ॥ 6
1.94.m: In a golden celestial chariot garlanded with networks of small bells, / decorated with jewels and pearls, and furnished with an excellent terrace of cat's-eye gems,

1.94.s:
āgataṃ puruṣaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā devo divākaraḥ1 .
sasambhramaṃ samutthāya āsanādeva sattama . . 7
1.94.d:
आगतं पुरुषं तत्र दृष्ट्वा देवो दिवाकरः1 ।
ससम्भ्रमं समुत्थाय आसनादेव सत्तम ॥ 7
1.94.m: seeing a man who had arrived there, the god who makes the day, / hurriedly rising from his very seat, O best of beings,

1.94.s:
gṛhītvā1 dakṣiṇe pāṇau purataḥ prāpya taṃ naram .
śirasyāghrāya deveśa pūjayāmāsa vai raviḥ . . 8
1.94.d:
गृहीत्वा1 दक्षिणे पाणौ पुरतः प्राप्य तं नरम् ।
शिरस्याघ्राय देवेश पूजयामास वै रविः ॥ 8
1.94.m: taking that man by the right hand as he approached before him, / smelling him on the head, O lord of the gods, Ravi indeed honoured him.

1.94.s:
upaviṣṭaṃ tu taṃ bhānuridaṃ vacanamabravīt .
susvāgataṃ bhadra sukhakṛtā prītāstvayā vayam . . 9
1.94.d:
उपविष्टं तु तं भानुरिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।
सुस्वागतं भद्र सुखकृता प्रीतास्त्वया वयम् ॥ 9
1.94.m: To him who was seated, the sun spoke this word: / 'A very warm welcome, my good man! Joy has been brought to us; we are pleased by you.

1.94.s:
samīpe mama tiṣṭha tvaṃ yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam .
punaryāsyasi tatsthānaṃ yatra brahmā svayaṃ sthitaḥ . . 1.94.10
1.94.d:
समीपे मम तिष्ठ त्वं यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् ।
पुनर्यास्यसि तत्स्थानं यत्र ब्रह्मा स्वयं स्थितः ॥ 1.94.10
1.94.m: Dwell near me until the dissolution of all beings; / then you will go to that place where Brahmā himself resides.'

1.94.s:
etasminnaṃtare cānyo vimānavaramāsthitaḥ .
āgataḥ puruṣo devo yatra tiṣṭhati bhāskaraḥ . . 11
1.94.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे चान्यो विमानवरमास्थितः ।
आगतः पुरुषो देवो यत्र तिष्ठति भास्करः ॥ 11
1.94.m: In the meantime, another divine man mounted upon an excellent celestial chariot / arrived where the radiant sun resides.

1.94.s:
sa cāpyevaṃ naro deva pūjito bhānunā tadā .
sāmapūrvaṃ tathoktastu praśrayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ . . 12
1.94.d:
स चाप्येवं नरो देव पूजितो भानुना तदा ।
सामपूर्वं तथोक्तस्तु प्रश्रयावनतः स्थितः ॥ 12
1.94.m: And that man too, O lord, was then honoured in the same way by the sun; / addressed with soothing words, he stood bowed with modest deference.

1.94.s:
tatra me kautukaṃ jātaṃ dṛṣṭvā pūjāṃ kṛtāṃ tayoḥ .
bhānunā devaśārdūla pṛṣṭo bhānurmayā tataḥ . . 13
1.94.d:
तत्र मे कौतुकं जातं दृष्ट्वा पूजां कृतां तयोः ।
भानुना देवशार्दूल पृष्टो भानुर्मया ततः ॥ 13
1.94.m: Curiosity arose in me there, seeing the honour paid to the two of them / by the sun, O tiger among gods. Then the sun was asked by me:

1.94.s:
kimanena kṛtaṃ deva yo'yaṃ pūrvamihāgataḥ .
narastatra sakāśaṃ vai yasya tuṣṭo bhavādṛśām . . 14
1.94.d:
किमनेन कृतं देव योऽयं पूर्वमिहागतः ।
नरस्तत्र सकाशं वै यस्य तुष्टो भवादृशाम् ॥ 14
1.94.m: 'What was done by this man who previously arrived here / into your presence, O lord, with whom one such as you is pleased,

1.94.s:
yadasya bhavatā pūjā kṛtā hi svayameva tu .
atra me kautukaṃ jātaṃ vismayaśca viśeṣataḥ . . 15
1.94.d:
यदस्य भवता पूजा कृता हि स्वयमेव तु ।
अत्र मे कौतुकं जातं विस्मयश्च विशेषतः ॥ 15
1.94.m: so that honour was paid to him indeed by your own self? / At this, curiosity and especially wonder have arisen in me.

1.94.s:
tathaivāsya kṛtā pūjā dvitīyasya narasya ca .
sarvathā puṇyakarmāṇāvimau naravarottamau . . 16
1.94.d:
तथैवास्य कृता पूजा द्वितीयस्य नरस्य च ।
सर्वथा पुण्यकर्माणाविमौ नरवरोत्तमौ ॥ 16
1.94.m: In the same manner, honour was paid to this second man as well. / Truly, these two most excellent among men are doers of meritorious deeds.

1.94.s:
brahmaviṣṇuśivādyaistu pūjyate bhagavānsadā .
yastvamābhyāṃ paraṃ pūjāṃ kṛtavāndevasattama . . 17
1.94.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवाद्यैस्तु पूज्यते भगवान्सदा ।
यस्त्वमाभ्यां परं पूजां कृतवान्देवसत्तम ॥ 17
1.94.m: The Blessed One is always worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the others; / yet you, O best of the gods, have shown the highest honour to these two!

1.94.s:
kathyatāṃ mama deveśa kimetau karma cakratuḥ .
yasyedṛkparamaṃ puṇyaṃ phalaṃ divyamavāpatuḥ . .
śrutvā tadvacanaṃ deva idaṃ vacanamabravīt . . 18
1.94.d:
कथ्यतां मम देवेश किमेतौ कर्म चक्रतुः ।
यस्येदृक्परमं पुण्यं फलं दिव्यमवापतुः ॥
श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं देव इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 18
1.94.m: Tell me, O lord of gods, what deed did these two perform, / through which they obtained such supreme, meritorious, and divine fruit?' / Hearing those words, O god, he spoke this speech:

1.94.s:
sūrya uvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi bhavatā karmaṇo nirṇayaṃ param . . 19
1.94.d:
सूर्य उवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि भवता कर्मणो निर्णयं परम् ॥ 19
1.94.m: The Sun said: / 'I have been well asked by you concerning the highest determination of actions.

1.94.s:
yadanena kṛtaṃ karma nareṇa munisattama .
yo'sau sūryamihāyātastacchṛṇuṣva mahāmate . . 1.94.20
1.94.d:
यदनेन कृतं कर्म नरेण मुनिसत्तम ।
योऽसौ सूर्यमिहायातस्तच्छृणुष्व महामते ॥ 1.94.20
1.94.m: The deed that was performed by this man, O best of sages, / who has come here to the sun—listen to that, O noble-minded one.

1.94.s:
yeyaṃ madaṃśasambhūtaiḥ pārthivaiḥ pālitā sadā .
ayodhyā nāma nagarī prakhyātā pṛthivītale . . 21
1.94.d:
येयं मदंशसम्भूतैः पार्थिवैः पालिता सदा ।
अयोध्या नाम नगरी प्रख्याता पृथिवीतले ॥ 21
1.94.m: This famous city named Ayodhyā on the face of the earth, / which was always ruled by monarchs born from parts of me—

1.94.s:
tatrāsau vaiśyajātīyo dhanapāla iti smṛtaḥ .
tasyāḥ puryāṃ dvijaśreṣṭha divyamāyatanaṃ vyadhāt1 . . 22
1.94.d:
तत्रासौ वैश्यजातीयो धनपाल इति स्मृतः ।
तस्याः पुर्यां द्विजश्रेष्ठ दिव्यमायतनं व्यधात्1 ॥ 22
1.94.m: there lived a man of the vaiśya caste remembered as Dhanapāla. / In that city, O best of the twice-born, he constructed a divine sanctuary.

1.94.s:
tasminnāyatane divye hyāmnāyārthaṃ tathāśritaḥ .
brāhmaṇānāṃ viśiṣṭānāṃ pūjayityā kadambakam . . 23
1.94.d:
तस्मिन्नायतने दिव्ये ह्याम्नायार्थं तथाश्रितः ।
ब्राह्मणानां विशिष्टानां पूजयित्या कदम्बकम् ॥ 23
1.94.m: In that divine sanctuary, he who was devoted to the meaning of the sacred tradition / worshipped an assemblage of distinguished Brahmins,

1.94.s:
itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ vācakaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .
pūjayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ munaśreṣṭhaṃ mahāmunim . . 24
1.94.d:
इतिहासपुराणाभ्यां वाचकं च विशेषतः ।
पूजयित्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठं मुनश्रेष्ठं महामुनिम् ॥ 24
1.94.m: and, having worshipped in particular the reader of the Itihāsas and Purāṇas, / that best of the twice-born, the eminent sage, the great sage,

1.94.s:
pustakaṃ cāpi sampūjya gandhapuṣpopahārataḥ .
tasya viprakadambasya vyāsasya ca yathāgrataḥ . . 25
1.94.d:
पुस्तकं चापि सम्पूज्य गन्धपुष्पोपहारतः ।
तस्य विप्रकदम्बस्य व्यासस्य च यथाग्रतः ॥ 25
1.94.m: And having worshipped the manuscript with offerings of perfumes and flowers, / in front of that assembly of brāhmaṇas and of Vyāsa,

1.94.s:
prakalpyokto dvijo'nena pāṭhako2 vācakottamaḥ .
eṣa tiṣṭhati deveśaḥ sahasrakiraṇo raviḥ . . 26
1.94.d:
प्रकल्प्योक्तो द्विजोऽनेन पाठको2 वाचकोत्तमः ।
एष तिष्ठति देवेशः सहस्रकिरणो रविः ॥ 26
1.94.m: having appointed a brāhmaṇa, an excellent recitation-reader, he said: / 'Here stands the lord of gods, the thousand-rayed Sun.

1.94.s:
cāturvarṇyamidaṃ vāpi śrotukāmaṃ kadambakam .
tiṣṭha ceha dvijaśreṣṭha kuru pustakavācanam . . 27
1.94.d:
चातुर्वर्ण्यमिदं वापि श्रोतुकामं कदम्बकम् ।
तिष्ठ चेह द्विजश्रेष्ठ कुरु पुस्तकवाचनम् ॥ 27
1.94.m: And this assembly of four castes is eager to listen. / Stay here, best of the twice-born, and perform the recitation of the manuscript,

1.94.s:
yena me varado bhānuḥ3 sapta janmāni vai bhavet .
yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ vipra pragṛhya vṛttimuttamām . . 28
1.94.d:
येन मे वरदो भानुः3 सप्त जन्मानि वै भवेत् ।
यावत्संवत्सरं विप्र प्रगृह्य वृत्तिमुत्तमाम् ॥ 28
1.94.m: so that the Sun may become the granter of boons to me for seven births. / Taking up an excellent livelihood for a year, O brāhmaṇa,

1.94.s:
svarṇaniṣkaśataṃ vipra tato dāsye tathāparam .
pūrṇe varṣe dvijaśreṣṭha śreyo'rthamahamātmanaḥ . . 29
1.94.d:
स्वर्णनिष्कशतं विप्र ततो दास्ये तथापरम् ।
पूर्णे वर्षे द्विजश्रेष्ठ श्रेयोऽर्थमहमात्मनः ॥ 29
1.94.m: I shall give another hundred gold niṣkas, O brāhmaṇa, / at the completion of the year, best of the twice-born, for my own welfare.'

1.94.s:
evaṃ pravartite tasminpuṇye pustakavācane .
ṣaṇmāsāgatamātre tu kāle suravarottama . .
tathaivāntarataścāyaṃ kāladharmamupeyivān . . 1.94.30
1.94.d:
एवं प्रवर्तिते तस्मिन्पुण्ये पुस्तकवाचने ।
षण्मासागतमात्रे तु काले सुरवरोत्तम ॥
तथैवान्तरतश्चायं कालधर्ममुपेयिवान् ॥ 1.94.30
1.94.m: When that sacred reading of the manuscript had thus begun, / and a time of mere six months had arrived, best among the supreme gods, / he, right in the midst of it, met the law of Time [and died].

1.94.s:
mayā cāsya vimānaṃ tu preṣitaṃ kurvato vratam .
ityeṣā karmaṇastuṣṭiḥ puṇyākhyānakajārcitā . . 31
1.94.d:
मया चास्य विमानं तु प्रेषितं कुर्वतो व्रतम् ।
इत्येषा कर्मणस्तुष्टिः पुण्याख्यानकजार्चिता ॥ 31
1.94.m: And a celestial chariot was sent by me to him who was performing this observance. / Such is the satisfaction born of his deed, revered through the recitation of sacred narratives.

1.94.s:
gandhapuṣpopahāraistu na tathā jāyate mama .
prītirdevavara śreṣṭha purāṇaśravaṇe yathā . . 32
1.94.d:
गन्धपुष्पोपहारैस्तु न तथा जायते मम ।
प्रीतिर्देववर श्रेष्ठ पुराणश्रवणे यथा ॥ 32
1.94.m: My pleasure is not produced by offerings of perfumes and flowers, / O best of eminent gods, as it is in the hearing of a Purāṇa.

1.94.s:
gosuvarṇahiraṇyānāṃ vastrāṇāṃ cāpi kṛtsnaśaḥ .
grāmāṇāṃ nagarāṇāṃ ca dānaṃ prītikaraṃ mama . . 33
1.94.d:
गोसुवर्णहिरण्यानां वस्त्राणां चापि कृत्स्नशः ।
ग्रामाणां नगराणां च दानं प्रीतिकरं मम ॥ 33
1.94.m: The gift of cattle, gold, wealth, and cloths in their entirety, / and of villages and cities, causes me delight;

1.94.s:
na tathā syātsuraśreṣṭha yathā prītikaraṃ guha .
itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ śravaṇaṃ surasainyapa .. 34
1.94.d:
न तथा स्यात्सुरश्रेष्ठ यथा प्रीतिकरं गुह ।
इतिहासपुराणाभ्यां श्रवणं सुरसैन्यप ॥ 34
1.94.m: yet it is not such, best of the gods, as causes delight, O Guha, / as the hearing from the Itihāsas and Purāṇas, O commander of the celestial armies!

1.94.s:
śrāddhaṃ kurvanti ye mahyaṃ bhakṣyabhojyairanekaśaḥ .
na karoti tathā prītiryathā pustakavācanam . . 35
1.94.d:
श्राद्धं कुर्वन्ति ये मह्यं भक्ष्यभोज्यैरनेकशः ।
न करोति तथा प्रीतिर्यथा पुस्तकवाचनम् ॥ 35
1.94.m: Those who perform a śrāddha for me with various foods and refreshments / do not produce such pleasure as the recitation of a manuscript.

1.94.s:
karṇaśrāddhe yathā prītirmama syātsurasattama .
na tathā jāyate prītirbhojyaśrāddhe tathaiva ca . . 36
1.94.d:
कर्णश्राद्धे यथा प्रीतिर्मम स्यात्सुरसत्तम ।
न तथा जायते प्रीतिर्भोज्यश्राद्धे तथैव च ॥ 36
1.94.m: Such pleasure as I have in an offering for the ears, best of the gods, / does not arise likewise in an offering of food.

1.94.s:
atha kiṃ bahunoktena nānyatprītikaraṃ mama .
puṇyākhyānādṛte deva guhyametatprakītitam . . 37
1.94.d:
अथ किं बहुनोक्तेन नान्यत्प्रीतिकरं मम ।
पुण्याख्यानादृते देव गुह्यमेतत्प्रकीतितम् ॥ 37
1.94.m: Now, what is the use of speaking much? Nothing else pleases me / except a sacred narrative, O god. This secret has been declared.

1.94.s:
yaścāyamaparo vipra ihāyato narottamaḥ .
ayamāsīddivajaśreṣṭhastasminneva purottame . . 38
1.94.d:
यश्चायमपरो विप्र इहायतो नरोत्तमः ।
अयमासीद्दिवजश्रेष्ठस्तस्मिन्नेव पुरोत्तमे ॥ 38
1.94.m: And this other brāhmaṇa who came here, best of men, / this best of the twice-born lived in that very same excellent city.

1.94.s:
ekadā tu gataścāyaṃ dharmaśravaṇamuttamam .
śrotuṃ bhaktyā ddvijaśreṣṭha śraddhayā parayā vṛtaḥ . . 39
1.94.d:
एकदा तु गतश्चायं धर्मश्रवणमुत्तमम् ।
श्रोतुं भक्त्या द्द्विजश्रेष्ठ श्रद्धया परया वृतः ॥ 39
1.94.m: Once he went to hear the excellent proclamation of dharma, / filled with supreme faith, to listen with devotion, best of the twice-born.

1.94.s:
śrutvā tatra tato bhaktyā puṇyākhyānamanuttamam .
kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ tasya vācakasya mahātmanaḥ . .
eṣa vipro'maraśreṣṭha dattavānsvarṇamāṣakam . . 1.94.40
1.94.d:
श्रुत्वा तत्र ततो भक्त्या पुण्याख्यानमनुत्तमम् ।
कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं तस्य वाचकस्य महात्मनः ॥
एष विप्रोऽमरश्रेष्ठ दत्तवान्स्वर्णमाषकम् ॥ 1.94.40
1.94.m: Having listened there with devotion to that peerless sacred narrative, / and having circumambulated that noble recitation-reader, / this brāhmaṇa, best of immortals, gave a gold māṣaka.

1.94.s:
dattvā tu dakṣiṇāṃ tasmai vācakāyāmitaujase 1 .
ānandamagamadvipraḥ prāptavānkāñcanaṃ yathā .4 1
etaddhi saphalaṃ cāsya na cānyatkṛtavānayam .
yadanena kṛtā pūjā vācakasya mahātmanaḥ . .
phalaṃ hi karmaṇastasya yanmayā pūjitaḥ svayam . . 42
1.94.d:
दत्त्वा तु दक्षिणां तस्मै वाचकायामितौजसे 1 ।
आनन्दमगमद्विप्रः प्राप्तवान्काञ्चनं यथा .4 1
एतद्धि सफलं चास्य न चान्यत्कृतवानयम् ।
यदनेन कृता पूजा वाचकस्य महात्मनः ॥
फलं हि कर्मणस्तस्य यन्मया पूजितः स्वयम् ॥ 42
1.94.m: And having given the priestly gift to that recitation-reader of boundless splendour, / the brāhmaṇa experienced joy, as if he had obtained gold. / This [reward] indeed bore fruit for him; nor did he do anything else. / Because he performed worship of that noble recitation-reader, / this is indeed the fruit of his deed: that he was personally honoured by me.

1.94.s:
vācakaṃ pūjayedyastu śraddhābhaktisamanvitaḥ .
tenāhaṃ pūjitaḥ syāṃ vai ko viṣṇuḥ śaṅkarastathā . . 43
1.94.d:
वाचकं पूजयेद्यस्तु श्रद्धाभक्तिसमन्वितः ।
तेनाहं पूजितः स्यां वै को विष्णुः शङ्करस्तथा ॥ 43
1.94.m: Whoever worships a recitation-reader endowed with faith and devotion, / by him I am surely worshipped, and Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śaṅkara likewise.

1.94.s:
vācakaṃ bhojayedyastu bhaktyā bhojyeranuttamaiḥ .
tenāhaṃ pūjitaḥ syāṃ vai daśa varṣāṇi pañca ca ..44
1.94.d:
वाचकं भोजयेद्यस्तु भक्त्या भोज्येरनुत्तमैः ।
तेनाहं पूजितः स्यां वै दश वर्षाणि पञ्च च ॥44
1.94.m: Whoever feeds a recitation-reader with devotion, with peerless foods, / by him I am surely worshipped for fifteen years.

1.94.s:
na yamo na yamī cāpi na mando na manustathā .
tapatī na tathānviṣṭā yatheṣṭo vācako mama ..45
1.94.d:
न यमो न यमी चापि न मन्दो न मनुस्तथा ।
तपती न तथान्विष्टा यथेष्टो वाचको मम ॥45
1.94.m: Neither Yama, nor Yamī, nor Saturn, nor Manu, / nor Tapatī is so dear [to me] as my recitation-reader is dear.

1.94.s:
vācake satkṛte deva bhojite surasainyapa .
tṛptirbhavati me deva saṃvatsaraśatadvayam ..46
1.94.d:
वाचके सत्कृते देव भोजिते सुरसैन्यप ।
तृप्तिर्भवति मे देव संवत्सरशतद्वयम् ॥46
1.94.m: When the recitation-reader is honoured and fed, O god, commander of the celestial armies, / my satisfaction lasts for two hundred years, O god.

1.94.s:
na kevalaṃ mama prītirvācake bhojite bhavet .
kṛtsnaśo devatānāṃ ca indrādīnāṃ tathā bhavet ..47
1.94.d:
न केवलं मम प्रीतिर्वाचके भोजिते भवेत् ।
कृत्स्नशो देवतानां च इन्द्रादीनां तथा भवेत् ॥47
1.94.m: Pleasure does not arise for me alone when a recitation-reader is fed; / it arises likewise for all the deities, Indra and the others.

1.94.s:
brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāṃ sa ceṣṭho vācako mama .
prīte tasmindevatāḥ syuḥ sarvāḥ prītā na saṃśayaḥ ..48
1.94.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादीनां स चेष्ठो वाचको मम ।
प्रीते तस्मिन्देवताः स्युः सर्वाः प्रीता न संशयः ॥48
1.94.m: To Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the rest, he is dear, my recitation-reader; / when he is pleased, all the deities are pleased—there is no doubt.

1.94.s: ityetatkathitaṃ sarvamābhyāṃ karma mahābala ..49
1.94.d: इत्येतत्कथितं सर्वमाभ्यां कर्म महाबल ॥49
1.94.m: Thus all the deeds performed by these two has been related, O mighty one.

1.94.s:
na cānyaccakratuḥ karma kimanyacchrotumicchasi .
etaddṛṣṭvāhamāścaryaṃ tavābhyāśamihāgataḥ ..
kimatra tathyaṃ deveśa kathyatāṃ kautukaṃ mama ..1.94.50
1.94.d:
न चान्यच्चक्रतुः कर्म किमन्यच्छ्रोतुमिच्छसि ।
एतद्दृष्ट्वाहमाश्चर्यं तवाभ्याशमिहागतः ॥
किमत्र तथ्यं देवेश कथ्यतां कौतुकं मम ॥1.94.50
1.94.m:
They did no other deed. What else do you wish to hear?'
Having seen this wonder, I have come here to your presence. / What is the truth in this, lord of gods? Let my curiosity be told [and satisfied].'

1.94.s: śrutvā kumāravacanaṃ sarvalokapitāmahaḥ ..51
1.94.d: श्रुत्वा कुमारवचनं सर्वलोकपितामहः ॥51
1.94.m: Having heard the word of Kumāra, the grandfather of all the worlds,

1.94.s:
brahmovāca
hanta bhoḥ sādhu puṇyo'si nāsti tulyastvayāparaḥ .
yaddṛṣṭau bhavatā tau hi supuṇyau puṇyakāriṇau ..52
1.94.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
हन्त भोः साधु पुण्योऽसि नास्ति तुल्यस्त्वयापरः ।
यद्दृष्टौ भवता तौ हि सुपुण्यौ पुण्यकारिणौ ॥52
1.94.m: Brahmā said: / 'Ah, well done! You are meritorious; there is none other equal to you, / since those two highly meritorious performers of good deeds were seen by you.

1.94.s:
yaduktaṃ bhānunā vatsa tattathā nānyathā bhavet .
yadāsīnme mukhaṃ putra prathamaṃ lokapūjitam ..53
1.94.d:
यदुक्तं भानुना वत्स तत्तथा नान्यथा भवेत् ।
यदासीन्मे मुखं पुत्र प्रथमं लोकपूजितम् ॥53
1.94.m: What was spoken by the Sun, my child, that is true, and cannot be otherwise. / That which was my first mouth, my son, revered by the worlds,

1.94.s:
tasmādetāni sarvāṇi nirgatāni samantataḥ .
itihāsapurāṇāni lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā ..54
1.94.d:
तस्मादेतानि सर्वाणि निर्गतानि समन्ततः ।
इतिहासपुराणानि लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥54
1.94.m: from that, all these Itihāsas and Purāṇas / emerged in all directions, out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds.

1.94.s:
yathaitāni mameṣṭāni purāṇāni mahāmate .
na tathā vai caturvedī na cāṅgini mahāmate ..55
1.94.d:
यथैतानि ममेष्टानि पुराणानि महामते ।
न तथा वै चतुर्वेदी न चाङ्गिनि महामते ॥55
1.94.m: Just as these Purāṇas are dear to me, O highly intelligent one, / the four Vedas are not so, nor the Vedāṅgas, O highly intelligent one.

1.94.s:
śṛṇvantyetāni ye bhaktyā nityaṃ śraddhāsamanvitāḥ .
dattvā tu vācake vṛttiṃ te gacchanti paraṃ padam ..56
1.94.d:
शृण्वन्त्येतानि ये भक्त्या नित्यं श्रद्धासमन्विताः ।
दत्त्वा तु वाचके वृत्तिं ते गच्छन्ति परं पदम् ॥56
1.94.m: Those who listen to these daily with devotion, endowed with faith, / and who provide a livelihood for the recitation-reader, go to the supreme state.

1.94.s:
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ spaṣṭīkaraṇamuttamam .
itihāsapurāṇāni mayā sṛṣṭāni suvrata . . 57
1.94.d:
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां स्पष्टीकरणमुत्तमम् ।
इतिहासपुराणानि मया सृष्टानि सुव्रत ॥ 57
1.94.m: The excellent clarification of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, / the Itihāsas and Purāṇas, were created by me, O you of good vows.

1.94.s:
catvāro ya ime vedā gūḍhārthāḥ satataṃ smṛtāḥ .
atastvetāni sṛṣṭāni bodhāyaiṣāṃ mahāmate . . 58
1.94.d:
चत्वारो य इमे वेदा गूढार्थाः सततं स्मृताः ।
अतस्त्वेतानि सृष्टानि बोधायैषां महामते ॥ 58
1.94.m: These four Vedas which are constantly taught are of concealed meaning; / therefore, these were created for their comprehension, O highly intelligent one.

1.94.s:
yastu kārayate nityaṃ dharmaśravaṇamuttamam .
ādityādbhāskaraṃ prāpya yāti tatparamaṃ padam . . 59
1.94.d:
यस्तु कारयते नित्यं धर्मश्रवणमुत्तमम् ।
आदित्याद्भास्करं प्राप्य याति तत्परमं पदम् ॥ 59
1.94.m: Whoever constantly causes the excellent hearing of dharma to be performed, / reaching the Sun from the Āditya, goes to that supreme state.

1.94.s:
dattvā tu dakṣiṇāṃ tatra ādityasya puraṃ vrajet .
kimāścaryaṃ suraśreṣṭha dānapātraṃ hi tatparam . . 1.94.60
1.94.d:
दत्त्वा तु दक्षिणां तत्र आदित्यस्य पुरं व्रजेत् ।
किमाश्चर्यं सुरश्रेष्ठ दानपात्रं हि तत्परम् ॥ 1.94.60
1.94.m: Having given a priestly gift there, he would go to the city of the Sun. / What is the wonder, best of the gods? For that is the supreme recipient of gifts.

1.94.s:
yathā devavaro lekho yathā hetiḥ paraṃ paviḥ .
brāhmaṇānāṃ tathā śreṣṭho vācako nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 61
1.94.d:
यथा देववरो लेखो यथा हेतिः परं पविः ।
ब्राह्मणानां तथा श्रेष्ठो वाचको नात्र संशयः ॥ 61
1.94.m: Just as a god is the best writer, just as the thunderbolt is the supreme weapon, / so is the recitation-reader the best among brāhmaṇas; of this there is no doubt.

1.94.s:
hetiryathā tejasāṃ tu sarasāṃ sāgaro yathā .
tathā sarvadvijebhyastu vācakaḥ pravaraḥ smṛtaḥ . . 62
1.94.d:
हेतिर्यथा तेजसां तु सरसां सागरो यथा ।
तथा सर्वद्विजेभ्यस्तु वाचकः प्रवरः स्मृतः ॥ 62
1.94.m: Just as a missile among fiery splendours, just as the ocean among lakes, / so is the recitation-reader regarded as the foremost among all the twice-born.

1.94.s:
vācakaṃ pūjayedyastu naro bhaktipuraḥ saram .
pūjitaṃ sakalaṃ tena jagatyānnātra saṃśayaḥ . . 63
1.94.d:
वाचकं पूजयेद्यस्तु नरो भक्तिपुरः सरम् ।
पूजितं सकलं तेन जगत्यान्नात्र संशयः ॥ 63
1.94.m: A man who worships a recitation-reader preceded by devotion, / by him the whole world has been worshipped; of this there is no doubt.

1.94.s:
satyamuktaṃ na sandeho bhānunā matkulodvaha .
vācakena samaṃ pātraṃ na jātvanyadbhavetkvacit . . 64
1.94.d:
सत्यमुक्तं न सन्देहो भानुना मत्कुलोद्वह ।
वाचकेन समं पात्रं न जात्वन्यद्भवेत्क्वचित् ॥ 64
1.94.m: The truth was spoken, without doubt, by the Sun, O continuer of my lineage. / There could never at any time be any other recipient equal to a recitation-reader.'

1.94.s: tacchrutvā brahmaṇo vākyaṃ kumāro vākyamabravīt . . 65
1.94.d: तच्छ्रुत्वा ब्रह्मणो वाक्यं कुमारो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 65
1.94.m: Having heard that speech of Brahmā, Kumāra spoke [these] words:

1.94.s:
aho hi dhanyatā tasya puṇyaśravaṇakāriṇaḥ .
dānaṃ ca dadato'tyarthaṃ puṇyatā vācakāya vai . . 66
1.94.d:
अहो हि धन्यता तस्य पुण्यश्रवणकारिणः ।
दानं च ददतोऽत्यर्थं पुण्यता वाचकाय वै ॥ 66
1.94.m: 'Oh, the blessedness of that person who performs the hearing of sacred lore, / and giving generous gifts to the recitation-reader is indeed supreme merit!'

1.94.s:
brahmovāca
itthaṃ diṇḍe sadā yastu devadevasya mandire .
kuryāttu dharmaśravaṇaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim . . 67
1.94.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
इत्थं दिण्डे सदा यस्तु देवदेवस्य मन्दिरे ।
कुर्यात्तु धर्मश्रवणं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ 67
1.94.m: Brahmā said: / 'Thus, whoever constantly performs the hearing of dharma at Diṇḍi in the temple of the god of gods, / goes to the supreme state.'

1.94.s:
iti śrībhaviṣyamahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe puṇyaśravaṇamāhātmya varṇanaṃ
nāma caturnavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 94 .
ādityālayamāhātmyavarṇanam
1.94.d:
इति श्रीभविष्यमहापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे पुण्यश्रवणमाहात्म्य वर्णनं
नाम चतुर्नवतितमोऽध्यायः । 94 ।
आदित्यालयमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्
1.94.m:
Thus ends the ninety-fourth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Greatness of Sacred Hearing", in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣyamahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Greatness of the Temple of the Sun

1.95.s:
brahmovāca
tribhiḥ pradakṣiṇāṃ kṛtvā yo namaskurute ravim .
bhūmau gatena śirasā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim . . 1
1.95.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
त्रिभिः प्रदक्षिणां कृत्वा यो नमस्कुरुते रविम् ।
भूमौ गतेन शिरसा स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ 1
1.95.m:
Brahmā said:
One who bows to the sun after circumambulating thrice,
with their head reaching the ground, goes to the supreme state.

1.95.s:
sopānatko devagṛhamārohedyastu mānavaḥ .
sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ tāmisraṃ nāma nāmataḥ . . 2
1.95.d:
सोपानत्को देवगृहमारोहेद्यस्तु मानवः ।
स याति नरकं घोरं तामिस्रं नाम नामतः ॥ 2
1.95.m:
A person who ascends to the temple of a god wearing sandals
goes to the terrible hell indeed known as Tāmisra.

1.95.s:
śleṣmamūtrapurīṣāṇi samutsṛjati yastu vai .
devasyāyatane bhānoḥ sa gacchennarakaṃ kramāt . . 3
1.95.d:
श्लेष्ममूत्रपुरीषाणि समुत्सृजति यस्तु वै ।
देवस्यायतने भानोः स गच्छेन्नरकं क्रमात् ॥ 3
1.95.m:
One who discharges phlegm, urine, or feces
in the temple of the sun-god will duly go to hell.

1.95.s:
ghṛtaṃ madhu payastoyaṃ tathekṣurasamuttamam .
snapanārthaṃ tu devasya ye dadatīha mānavāḥ . .
sarvakāmānavāpyeha te yānti helimaṇḍalam . . 4
1.95.d:
घृतं मधु पयस्तोयं तथेक्षुरसमुत्तमम् ।
स्नपनार्थं तु देवस्य ये ददतीह मानवाः ॥
सर्वकामानवाप्येह ते यान्ति हेलिमण्डलम् ॥ 4
1.95.m:
Ghee, honey, milk, water, and excellent sugarcane juice—
men here who offer these for the bathing of the god,
having obtained all desires in this world, go to the realm of the sun.

1.95.s:
snāpyamānaṃ raviṃ bhaktyā ye paśyanti vṛṣadhvaja .
te'śvamedhaphalaṃ prāpya layaṃ yānti vṛṣadhvaje . . 5
1.95.d:
स्नाप्यमानं रविं भक्त्या ये पश्यन्ति वृषध्वज ।
तेऽश्वमेधफलं प्राप्य लयं यान्ति वृषध्वजे ॥ 5
1.95.m:
Those who with devotion behold the sun being bathed, O bull-bannered one,
obtain the fruit of an aśvamedha and attain dissolution into the bull-bannered [lord].

1.95.s:
snapanaṃ ye ca kurvaṃti bhānorbhaktisamanvitāḥ .
labhante tatphalaṃ bhīma rājasūyāśvamedhayoḥ . . 6
1.95.d:
स्नपनं ये च कुर्वंति भानोर्भक्तिसमन्विताः ।
लभन्ते तत्फलं भीम राजसूयाश्वमेधयोः ॥ 6
1.95.m:
And those who, filled with devotion, perform the bathing of the sun,
O Bhīma, obtain the fruit of a rājasūya and an aśvamedha.

1.95.s:
yathā na laṅghayetkaścitsnapanaṃ bhāskarasya tu .
tathā kāryaṃ prayatnena laṅghitaṃ hyasukhāvaham . . 7
1.95.d:
यथा न लङ्घयेत्कश्चित्स्नपनं भास्करस्य तु ।
तथा कार्यं प्रयत्नेन लङ्घितं ह्यसुखावहम् ॥ 7
1.95.m:
Effort should be made so that no one crosses over the bathing-water of the sun,
for crossing over it brings misfortune.

1.95.s:
tāmisraṃ narakaṃ yāti laṅghayecca sa rauravān .
tasmātsarvaprayatnena kāryaṃ snapanamāditaḥ . . 8
1.95.d:
तामिस्रं नरकं याति लङ्घयेच्च स रौरवान् ।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन कार्यं स्नपनमादितः ॥ 8
1.95.m:
One goes to the Tāmisra hell, and one who crosses it [goes to] the Raurava hells.
Therefore, with every effort, the bathing must be performed properly.

1.95.s:
ghṛtena snāpayeddevaṃ kañjamāpnoti mānavaḥ .
madhunā priyamāyāti toyenāpi ghṛtaukasam . . 9
1.95.d:
घृतेन स्नापयेद्देवं कञ्जमाप्नोति मानवः ।
मधुना प्रियमायाति तोयेनापि घृतौकसम् ॥ 9
1.95.m:
If a man bathes the god with ghee, he obtains Brahmā;
with honey, he becomes beloved; and with water, [he attains] the abode of ghee [heaven].

1.95.s:
ikṣurasena saṃsnāpya payasā kañjaśadhvajam .
evamebhiḥ snāpayedvai ravimīhitamāpnuyāt . . 1.95.10
1.95.d:
इक्षुरसेन संस्नाप्य पयसा कञ्जशध्वजम् ।
एवमेभिः स्नापयेद्वै रविमीहितमाप्नुयात् ॥ 1.95.10
1.95.m:
Having bathed the sun-god with sugarcane juice and milk,
by thus bathing the sun with these, one attains one's desire.

1.95.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhmeparvaṇi saptamīkalpe ādityālayamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ
nāma pañcanavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ . 95 .
jayānāmasaptamīvarṇanam
1.95.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मेपर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे आदित्यालयमाहात्म्यवर्णनं
नाम पञ्चनवतितमोऽध्यायः । 95 ।
जयानामसप्तमीवर्णनम्
1.95.m:
Thus ends the ninety-fifth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of the Abode of the Sun', in the Saptamīkalpa of the Brāhmaparvan in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Saptamī Named Jayā

1.96.s:
diṇḍiruvāca
yaccaitāḥ sapta saptamyo bhavatā kathitā mama .
tāsāṃ yā prathamā deva kathitā sā savistarā . . 1
1.96.d:
दिण्डिरुवाच
यच्चैताः सप्त सप्तम्यो भवता कथिता मम ।
तासां या प्रथमा देव कथिता सा सविस्तरा ॥ 1
1.96.m:
Diṇḍi said:
Regarding these seven saptamīs that were related by you to me,
of those, O god, the first has been related in detail.

1.96.s:
yāstvanyā devaśārdūla tāḥ sarvāḥ kathayasva me .
yenopoṣya tatastāstu vraje'haṃ helisadma vai . . 6
1.96.d:
यास्त्वन्या देवशार्दूल ताः सर्वाः कथयस्व मे ।
येनोपोष्य ततस्तास्तु व्रजेऽहं हेलिसद्म वै ॥ 6
1.96.m:
Relate to me all the others, O tiger among gods,
so that, having fasted on them, I may go to the abode of the sun.

1.96.s:
brahmovāca
śuklapakṣasya saptamyāṃ nakṣatraṃ pañcatārakam .
yadā syātsā tadā jñeyā jayā nāmeti saptamī . . 3
1.96.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
शुक्लपक्षस्य सप्तम्यां नक्षत्रं पञ्चतारकम् ।
यदा स्यात्सा तदा ज्ञेया जया नामेति सप्तमी ॥ 3
1.96.m:
Brahmā said:
When on the saptamī of the bright fortnight there is a five-starred lunar mansion,
then that is to be known as the saptamī named Jayā.

1.96.s:
tasyāṃ dattāṃ1 hutaṃ jāpastarpaṇaṃ devapūjanam .
sarvaṃ śataguṇaṃ proktaṃ pūjā cāpi divākare . . 4
1.96.d:
तस्यां दत्तां1 हुतं जापस्तर्पणं देवपूजनम् ।
सर्वं शतगुणं प्रोक्तं पूजा चापि दिवाकरे ॥ 4
1.96.m:
What is given, offered in fire, recited as japa, offered as libation, and worshipped on it—
all is declared to be hundredfold, as is worship offered to the sun.

1.96.s:
bhāskarasya priyā hyeṣā saptamī pāpanāśinī .
dhanyā yaśasyā putryā ca kāmadā kañjajāvahā . . 5
1.96.d:
भास्करस्य प्रिया ह्येषा सप्तमी पापनाशिनी ।
धन्या यशस्या पुत्र्या च कामदा कञ्जजावहा ॥ 5
1.96.m:
This saptamī is dear to the sun, destroys sins,
is auspicious, brings renown, grants sons, yields desires, and brings [one to] Brahmā.

1.96.s:
vidhinānena kartavyā tithiryā mama vidyate .
taṃ śṛṇuṣva vidhiṃ matto yena kṛtvārthamaśnumate . 6
1.96.d:
विधिनानेन कर्तव्या तिथिर्या मम विद्यते ।
तं शृणुष्व विधिं मत्तो येन कृत्वार्थमश्नुमते । 6
1.96.m:
This lunar day of mine should be observed according to this rule.
Hear that rule from me, by performing which one achieves one's purpose.

1.96.s:
haṃse haṃsamākye śukleyaṃ saptamī purā .
samupoṣya ca kartavyā vidhinānena śaṅkara . . 7
1.96.d:
हंसे हंसमाक्ये शुक्लेयं सप्तमी पुरा ।
समुपोष्य च कर्तव्या विधिनानेन शङ्कर ॥ 7
1.96.m:
In the past, this bright saptamī when the sun is in Virgo,
O Śaṅkara, is to be performed by fasting according to this rule.

1.96.s:
pāraṇā tṛtīyā'he syātkathitaṃ govṛṣāvaham .
prathamaṃ caturo māsānpāraṇaṃ kathitaṃ budhaiḥ . . 8
1.96.d:
पारणा तृतीयाऽहे स्यात्कथितं गोवृषावहम् ।
प्रथमं चतुरो मासान्पारणं कथितं बुधैः ॥ 8
1.96.m:
The breaking of the fast should be on the third day; it is described as bringing cattle.
The wise have declared the breaking of the fast for the first four months.

1.96.s:
kathitānyatra puṣpāṇi karavīrasya suvrata .
candanaṃ ca tathā raktaṃ dhūpārthaṃ guggulaṃ param . . 9
1.96.d:
कथितान्यत्र पुष्पाणि करवीरस्य सुव्रत ।
चन्दनं च तथा रक्तं धूपार्थं गुग्गुलं परम् ॥ 9
1.96.m:
Karavīra flowers are prescribed here, O one of good vows,
as well as red sandalwood, and supreme guggulu for incense.

1.96.s:
kāsāraṃ tu supakvaṃ ca naivedyaṃ bhāskarāya vai .
anena vidhinā pūjya mārtaṇḍaṃ vibudhādhipam . . 1.96.10
1.96.d:
कासारं तु सुपक्वं च नैवेद्यं भास्कराय वै ।
अनेन विधिना पूज्य मार्तण्डं विबुधाधिपम् ॥ 1.96.10
1.96.m:
And well-cooked kāsāra as a food offering for the sun;
having worshipped Mārtaṇḍa, the lord of gods, according to this rule,

1.96.s:
pūjayedbrāhmaṇānbhīma bhakṣyabhojyairyathāvidhi .
kāsāraṃ bhojayedviprānpāraṇe'sminvicakṣaṇaḥ . .
svayameva tathāśnīyātprayato maunamāśritaḥ . . 11
1.96.d:
पूजयेद्ब्राह्मणान्भीम भक्ष्यभोज्यैर्यथाविधि ।
कासारं भोजयेद्विप्रान्पारणेऽस्मिन्विचक्षणः ॥
स्वयमेव तथाश्नीयात्प्रयतो मौनमाश्रितः ॥ 11
1.96.m:
O Bhīma, one should properly honour brāhmaṇas with foods and refreshments.
A wise person should feed the vipras with kāsāra at this breaking of the fast,
and should himself eat in the same way, restrained and observing silence.

1.96.s:
pañcamyāmekabhaktaṃ tu ṣaṣṭhyāṃ naktaṃ pravartate .
kṛtvopavāsaṃ saptamyāmaṣṭamyāṃ pāraṇaṃ bhavet . . 12
1.96.d:
पञ्चम्यामेकभक्तं तु षष्ठ्यां नक्तं प्रवर्तते ।
कृत्वोपवासं सप्तम्यामष्टम्यां पारणं भवेत् ॥ 12
1.96.m:
On the pañcamī there is a single meal, on the ṣaṣṭhī a nocturnal meal is undertaken;
having fasted on the saptamī, the breaking of the fast should be on the aṣṭamī.

1.96.s:
ṣaṣṭhyā sametā kartavyā nāṣṭamyeyaṃ kadācana .
yasyopavāsanāyaiva ṣaṣṭhyāmāhurupoṣitam . . 13
1.96.d:
षष्ठ्या समेता कर्तव्या नाष्टम्येयं कदाचन ।
यस्योपवासनायैव षष्ठ्यामाहुरुपोषितम् ॥ 13
1.96.m:
This should be performed conjoined with the ṣaṣṭhī, never with the aṣṭamī;
for the fasting-day itself, they declare the fast is kept on the ṣaṣṭhī.

1.96.s:
yathaikādaśyāṃ kurvanti upavāsaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ .
upavāsanāya dvādaśyāṃ tatheyaṃ parikīrtitā . . 14
1.96.d:
यथैकादश्यां कुर्वन्ति उपवासं मनीषिणः ।
उपवासनाय द्वादश्यां तथेयं परिकीर्तिता ॥ 14
1.96.m:
Just as the wise fast on the ekādaśī
for the sake of fasting on the dvādaśī, so this is proclaimed.

1.96.s:
siddhārthakaiḥ snānamantraḥ prāśanaṃ gomayasya tu .
bhānurme prīyatāmatra dantakāṣṭhaṃ tathārkajam . . 15
1.96.d:
सिद्धार्थकैः स्नानमन्त्रः प्राशनं गोमयस्य तु ।
भानुर्मे प्रीयतामत्र दन्तकाष्ठं तथार्कजम् ॥ 15
1.96.m:
The bath-mantra is with white mustard seeds, and the sipping is of cow dung;
one should use a tooth-stick made of arka wood, [praying:] 'May the sun be pleased with me here.'

1.96.s:
ityeṣa kathitastāta prathame pāraṇe vidhiḥ .
dvitīyaṃ śrūyatāṃ bhīma pāraṇaṃ gadato mama . . 16
1.96.d:
इत्येष कथितस्तात प्रथमे पारणे विधिः ।
द्वितीयं श्रूयतां भीम पारणं गदतो मम ॥ 16
1.96.m:
Thus this rule has been related, dear one, for the first breaking of the fast.
Listen, O Bhīma, as I speak of the second breaking of the fast.

1.96.s:
mālatīkusumānīha śrīkhaṇḍaṃ candanaṃ tathā .
naivedyaṃ pāyasaṃ bhānordhūpaṃ vijayamādiśet . . 17
1.96.d:
मालतीकुसुमानीह श्रीखण्डं चन्दनं तथा ।
नैवेद्यं पायसं भानोर्धूपं विजयमादिशेत् ॥ 17
1.96.m:
Here, mālatī blossoms, śrīkhaṇḍa and sandalwood,
pāyasa as the food offering to the sun, and vijaya incense should be prescribed.

1.96.s:
brāhmaṇānbhojayedvāpi tathāśnīyātsvayaṃ vibho .
ravirme prīyatāmatra nāma devasya kīrtayet . . 18
1.96.d:
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेद्वापि तथाश्नीयात्स्वयं विभो ।
रविर्मे प्रीयतामत्र नाम देवस्य कीर्तयेत् ॥ 18
1.96.m:
One should feed brāhmaṇas and eat oneself, O mighty one,
and utter the name of the god: 'May the sun be pleased with me here.'

1.96.s:
prāśayetpañcagavyaṃ tu khadiraṃ dantadhāvane .
dvitīye pāraṇe vīra vidhirukto mayādhunā . . 19
1.96.d:
प्राशयेत्पञ्चगव्यं तु खदिरं दन्तधावने ।
द्वितीये पारणे वीर विधिरुक्तो मयाधुना ॥ 19
1.96.m:
One should partake of pañcagavya and use khadira for tooth-cleaning;
now the rule for the second breaking of the fast has been spoken by me, O hero.

1.96.s:
tṛtīyaṃ pāraṇaṃ cāpi kathyamānaṃ nibodha me .
agastikusumairatra bhāskaraṃ pūjayedbudhaḥ . . 1.96.20
1.96.d:
तृतीयं पारणं चापि कथ्यमानं निबोध मे ।
अगस्तिकुसुमैरत्र भास्करं पूजयेद्बुधः ॥ 1.96.20
1.96.m:
Understand from me also the third breaking of the fast as it is spoken.
Here, a wise person should worship the sun with agasti flowers.

1.96.s:
samālambhanamatroktaṃ śrīkhaṇḍaṃ kusumaṃ tathā .
sihlako dhūpa uddiṣṭo bhānoḥ prītikaraḥ paraḥ . . 21
1.96.d:
समालम्भनमत्रोक्तं श्रीखण्डं कुसुमं तथा ।
सिह्लको धूप उद्दिष्टो भानोः प्रीतिकरः परः ॥ 21
1.96.m:
Śrīkhaṇḍa and blossoms are declared here for anointing;
sihlaka is prescribed as incense, causing supreme delight to the sun.

1.96.s:
śālyodanaṃ tu naivedyaṃ rasāloparisaṃyutam .
brāhmaṇānāṃ tu dātavyaṃ bhakṣayeta tathātmanā . . 22
1.96.d:
शाल्योदनं तु नैवेद्यं रसालोपरिसंयुतम् ।
ब्राह्मणानां तु दातव्यं भक्षयेत तथात्मना ॥ 22
1.96.m:
Boiled rice of winter crop topped with rasālā is the food offering;
it should be given to brāhmaṇas, and one should eat it oneself in like manner.

1.96.s:
kuśodakaprāśanaṃ tu badaryā dantadhāvanam .
vikartanaḥ prīyatāṃ me nāma devasya kīrtayet . . 23
1.96.d:
कुशोदकप्राशनं तु बदर्या दन्तधावनम् ।
विकर्तनः प्रीयतां मे नाम देवस्य कीर्तयेत् ॥ 23
1.96.m:
Sipping kuśa-grass water and cleaning teeth with badarī,
one should utter the name of the god: 'May Vikartana be pleased with me.'

1.96.s:
varṣāsu devadevasya pūjā kāryā vidhānataḥ .
gandhapuṣpopahāraistu nānāprekṣaṇakaistathā . . 24
1.96.d:
वर्षासु देवदेवस्य पूजा कार्या विधानतः ।
गन्धपुष्पोपहारैस्तु नानाप्रेक्षणकैस्तथा ॥ 24
1.96.m:
In the rainy season, worship of the god of gods should be performed according to rule,
with offerings of fragrant scents, flowers, and various dramatic shows,

1.96.s:
godānairbhūmidānairvā brāhmaṇānāṃ ca tarpaṇaiḥ .
itthaṃ sampūjya deveśaṃ devasya purataḥ sthitaḥ . . 25
1.96.d:
गोदानैर्भूमिदानैर्वा ब्राह्मणानां च तर्पणैः ।
इत्थं सम्पूज्य देवेशं देवस्य पुरतः स्थितः ॥ 25
1.96.m:
or with gifts of cattle, gifts of land, and propitiations of brāhmaṇas.
Having thus worshipped the lord of gods, standing before the god,

1.96.s:
kārayetparamaṃ puṇyaṃ dhanyaṃ pustakavācanam .
vastrairgandhaistathā dhūpairvācakaṃ pūjayettataḥ . . 26
1.96.d:
कारयेत्परमं पुण्यं धन्यं पुस्तकवाचनम् ।
वस्त्रैर्गन्धैस्तथा धूपैर्वाचकं पूजयेत्ततः ॥ 26
1.96.m:
one should have a sacred, auspicious recitation of the scripture performed.
Then one should worship the reciter with garments, scents, and incenses.

1.96.s:
devasya purataḥ sthitvā tato mantramudīrayet .
devadeva jagannātha sarvarogārtināśana . .
graheśa lokanayana vikartana tamo'paha . . 27
1.96.d:
देवस्य पुरतः स्थित्वा ततो मन्त्रमुदीरयेत् ।
देवदेव जगन्नाथ सर्वरोगार्तिनाशन ॥
ग्रहेश लोकनयन विकर्तन तमोऽपह ॥ 27
1.96.m:
Standing before the god, one should then utter the mantra:
'O god of gods, lord of the world, destroyer of all distress and diseases,
O lord of planets, eye of the world, Vikartana, dispeller of darkness!

1.96.s:
kṛteyaṃ devadeveśa jayā nāmeti saptamī .
mayā tava prasādena dhanyā pāpaharā śivā . . 28
1.96.d:
कृतेयं देवदेवेश जया नामेति सप्तमी ।
मया तव प्रसादेन धन्या पापहरा शिवा ॥ 28
